docs.title: MT5Account — Low-Level API (Layer 1 of 3)
docs.text:
metarpc::MT5Account is the thin, 1:1-with-the-wire layer. Every method maps to a single gRPC RPC: you pass a protobuf *Request and get back the protobuf *Data payload of the reply. It owns the gRPC channel, the service stubs, the connection/identity state and the transport machinery — transient-failure retry with exponential back-off and an automatic ConnectEx re-attach on TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND.

#include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>   // pulls in the generated protobuf headers

When to use this layer

Use MT5Account when you need a field the friendly layers do not expose, or full control over the exact request. For everyday work prefer MT5Service (friendly structs) or MT5Sugar (one-liners), which hide protobuf and compile fast.

docs.title: How a call works
docs.text:
• Protobuf in, protobuf out. accountSummary() returns a pb::AccountSummaryData; you read fields with the generated accessors (.account_balance(), .account_login(), …).
  • No UTC conversion. Times are raw broker server time. MT5Service is the layer that converts to/from UTC.
  • Errors are exceptions (never error codes):
    • metarpc::ApiError — the gateway/terminal answered with an error payload (bad login, unknown symbol, trade rejected, …). Carries code, message, and the MQL5 codes.
    • metarpc::TransportError — a gRPC transport failure that outlived the retry budget.
  • Retry & reconnect are automatic (see ClientOptions). You do not retry yourself.
using namespace metarpc;
namespace pb = mt5_term_api;

MT5Account acc("mt5.mrpc.pro", 443, /*apiKey*/ "");
acc.connect(5057947437, "password", "MetaQuotes-Demo");

try {
    pb::AccountSummaryData s = acc.accountSummary();
    std::cout << s.account_login() << "  " << s.account_balance() << " " << s.account_currency() << "\n";
} catch (const ApiError& e) {
    std::cerr << e.code << ": " << e.message << "\n";
}

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
Every onX() opens a server stream and delivers raw protobuf payloads to your callback on a background thread. The returned AccountStream owns the subscription — keep it alive to keep receiving, destroy it (or call stop()) to cancel.

Method Callback payload onSymbolTick(req, cb) pb::OnSymbolTickData onTrade(req, cb) pb::OnTradeData onTradeTransaction(req, cb) pb::OnTradeTransactionData onPositionProfit(req, cb) pb::OnPositionProfitData onPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets(req, cb) pb::OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsData

AccountStream exposes stop(), running(), count(), lastError().

pb::OnSymbolTickRequest req;
req.add_symbol_names("EURUSD");
auto stream = acc.onSymbolTick(req, [](const pb::OnSymbolTickData& d) {
    if (d.has_symbol_tick())
        std::cout << d.symbol_tick().symbol() << " " << d.symbol_tick().bid() << "\n";
});
std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(5));
stream->stop();   // (also happens automatically when `stream` is destroyed)

docs.title: Example — a single symbol property, the raw way
docs.text:
using namespace metarpc;
namespace pb = mt5_term_api;

// SymbolInfoIntegerProperty: 17 = SYMBOL_DIGITS
pb::SymbolInfoIntegerRequest req;
req.set_symbol("EURUSD");
req.set_type((pb::SymbolInfoIntegerProperty)17);
int64_t digits = acc.symbolInfoInteger(req).value();

docs.title: MT5Service — Facade API (Layer 2 of 3)
docs.text:
metarpc::MT5Service owns an MT5Account and gives you a comfortable, protobuf-free API: friendly C++ structs instead of protobuf messages, plain arguments instead of hand-built *Request objects, and automatic UTC ↔ broker-server time conversion. This is the layer most application code should use directly.

#include <metarpc/mt5_service.hpp>   // protobuf-free — compiles fast

Why it compiles fast

This header does not include the generated protobuf headers (it forward-declares MT5Account). Reach the low-level layer with account() when you need a raw RPC — that translation unit then pays the protobuf include cost, nothing else does.

docs.title: Construction
docs.text:
MT5Service(const std::string& host = "mt5.mrpc.pro", int port = 443,
           const std::string& apiKey = "", const std::string& name = "",
           bool utcTimes = true);
  • utcTimes (default true): every time the facade returns is UTC and every time you pass in is treated as UTC. Set false to work in raw broker-server time.
  • account() → the underlying MT5Account for raw RPCs.
using namespace metarpc;
MT5Service svc("mt5.mrpc.pro", 443);
svc.connect(5057947437, "password", "MetaQuotes-Demo");

AccountInfo a = svc.accountSummary();
std::cout << a.login << "  " << a.balance << " " << a.currency << "  1:" << a.leverage << "\n";

docs.text:

Enums: TradeMode, Timeframe, TradeAction.

Errors are the same exceptions as the low level: ApiError / TransportError.

docs.title: Streaming (friendly)
docs.text:
Each subscribe*/stream* converts the raw payload to friendly structs (times in UTC) and delivers them to callback on a background thread. The returned ServiceStream has stop()/running()/ count()/lastError(). Keep it alive to keep receiving.

Method Callback payload subscribeTicks(symbols, cb) Tick streamTradeUpdates(cb) TradeEvent streamTransactions(cb) TransactionEvent streamPositionProfits(cb) PositionProfitEvent streamOpenedTickets(cb) TicketsSnapshot

    std::cout << t.symbol << "  bid=" << t.bid << " ask=" << t.ask << "  t=" << t.time << " (UTC)\n";
});
std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(5));

docs.title: MT5Sugar — High-Level API (Layer 3 of 3)
docs.text:
metarpc::MT5Sugar owns an MT5Service and offers the shortest possible one-liners for everyday tasks: "what's my balance?", "what's the bid?", "buy 0.1 lots", "close everything". No context, no request objects, no protobuf — prototyping code reads like plain English.

#include <metarpc/mt5_sugar.hpp>   // protobuf-free

When you outgrow it, drop down to service() (friendly facade) or account() (raw RPCs).

docs.title: Construction & connection
docs.text:
using namespace metarpc;
MT5Sugar sugar("mt5.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(5057947437, "password", "MetaQuotes-Demo");
// or, from MT5_LOGIN / MT5_PASSWORD / MT5_SERVER env vars:
// sugar.quickConnect();

std::cout << "balance " << sugar.getBalance() << ",  EURUSD bid " << sugar.getBid("EURUSD") << "\n";

docs.title: Enums Reference
docs.text:
A complete catalog of the enums used across CppMT5 — the friendly C++ enums you use at the Service/Sugar level, and the protobuf enums you meet at the raw MT5Account level. They split naturally into input enums (you pass them, e.g. "which property?", "which order type?") and output enums (you read them back, e.g. a position's type, a deal's entry, an order's state).

🧱 C++ rule — values are namespace-scope. The generated protobuf enums are not enum class, so every value lives directly in the mt5_term_api namespace: write pb::ACCOUNT_BALANCE, pb::TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY, pb::BMT5_POSITION_TYPE_SELL (where namespace pb = mt5_term_api;). The prefixed pb::SomeEnumType_VALUE form is a Go/C# convention and does not exist in C++.

docs.title: 1. Friendly C++ enums (metarpc::…)
docs.text: Defined in mt5_service.hpp, usable without protobuf. The friendly layers accept/return these; they mirror the raw wire values 1:1.

docs.text:
enum class TradeAction { Buy=0, Sell=1, BuyLimit=2, SellLimit=3,
                         BuyStop=4, SellStop=5, BuyStopLimit=6, SellStopLimit=7 };

OrderRequest q; q.symbol = "EURUSD"; q.action = TradeAction::BuyLimit; q.price = 1.0800;

docs.title: 4. Usage at each layer
docs.text:
namespace pb = mt5_term_api;

// Low level — the real protobuf enum, namespace-scope value:
pb::AccountInfoDoubleRequest r;
r.set_property_id(pb::ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE);              // input enum
double fm = acc.accountInfoDouble(r).requested_value();  // account → requested_value(); symbol → value()

// Reading an output enum:
pb::AccountSummaryData s = acc.accountSummary();
if (s.account_trade_mode() == pb::MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL) { /* be careful */ }

// Mid level — pass the id as a plain int (the enum value converts implicitly):
double freeMargin = svc.accountInfoDouble(pb::ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE);
int64_t digits    = svc.symbolInfoInteger("EURUSD", pb::SYMBOL_DIGITS);

Tip

You rarely need the raw property ids — MT5Service::symbolParams() returns a SymbolInfo with every field already named (digits, point, volumeMin, spread, …), and accountSummary() returns a named AccountInfo. Reach for property ids only when you want a single value the structs don't carry.

docs.title: 5. Discovering enum values
docs.text:
Don't guess the constants — list them from the real descriptors with the Protobuf Inspector:

> enum TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE
  TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY        = 0
  TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_SELL       = 1
  ...
> enum BMT5_ENUM_DEAL_TYPE
> field property_id           # which messages take a property enum

It runs offline (./build/protobuf_inspector) and prints the exact names and values compiled into the SDK.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: CppMT5 is a C++17 client for the MetaRPC MT5 gRPC gateway. It ships as a small static library with a three-layer API — MT5Account (low-level protobuf), MT5Service (friendly facade) and MT5Sugar (one-liners).

docs.title: 1. Requirements
docs.text:
• A C++17 compiler
  • CMake ≥ 3.15 and a generator (Ninja recommended)
  • protobuf and grpc++ development packages, discovered via pkg-config
  • the protoc compiler and the grpc_cpp_plugin — the build generates the gRPC stubs from the shipped contract at configure time (the install commands below include them)

Install the dependencies:

=== "Debian / Ubuntu" 

sudo apt install build-essential cmake ninja-build pkg-config \
     libprotobuf-dev protobuf-compiler libgrpc++-dev protobuf-compiler-grpc

=== "MSYS2 (Windows, UCRT64)" 

pacman -S mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-{gcc,cmake,ninja,pkgconf,protobuf,grpc}

=== "macOS (Homebrew)" 

brew install cmake ninja pkg-config protobuf grpc

Generated protobuf code

The repository ships the gRPC contract as a single version-independent proto/mt5_term_api.desc (a protobuf FileDescriptorSet). At build time CMake runs your protoc on it, so the generated C++/gRPC stubs always match the protobuf/grpc installed above — no version pinning, nothing to regenerate by hand. If you only want the raw contract (to build your own client in any language), download that one file and feed it to protoc --descriptor_set_in=….

docs.title: 2. Build
docs.text:
cmake -G Ninja -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build

What the first configure does

git clone + these two commands is all you need — no manual protoc step. The first cmake configure runs protoc on proto/mt5_term_api.desc to generate the C++/gRPC stubs into build/generated/ (a few seconds), then compiles them into the library. That's why protoc and grpc_cpp_plugin must be installed (they're in the dependencies above). Later builds reuse the generated code; it regenerates only if the contract changes.

This produces the metarpc_cppmt5 static library and the demos launcher (14 runnable examples). Turn the demos off with -DBUILD_DEMOS=OFF.

docs.title: 3. Get an API key
docs.text:
Connecting to MetaRPC production (mt5.mrpc.pro:443) needs an API key:

  1. Sign up — free at https://mrpc.pro/signup.
  2. Generate a key — in the portal at https://mrpc.pro/my, under API Keys.
  3. Provide it — the SDK reads MRPC_API_KEY from the environment (falling back to "TRIAL"), and sends it as the apikey metadata header on every call. You can also pass it to the layer constructor or set api_key in config.json.

You also need an MT5 demo account (login, password, server name) — see MT5 for Beginners.

The terminal session id is automatic

Two things authenticate each call: your apikey and a terminal session id. You don't fetch the id yourself — connect() obtains it from the gateway (ConnectEx → terminalInstanceGuid), the SDK stores it and attaches it to every later unary call and stream. Read it any time with terminalGuid().

docs.title: 4. Configure credentials
docs.text:
The demos read examples/demos/config/config.json (or environment variables). Create it from your MetaRPC account:

{
  "user": 5057947437,
  "password": "YourPassword",
  "grpc_server": "mt5.mrpc.pro:443",
  "mt_cluster": "MetaQuotes-Demo",
  "api_key": "",
  "test_symbol": "EURUSD",
  "test_volume": 0.01
}

Environment variables override the file: MT5_LOGIN, MT5_PASSWORD, MT5_SERVER, MT5_GRPC, MT5_API_KEY. The api_key is "" for trial access or your gateway key for production.

docs.title: 5. Run a demo
docs.text:
./build/demos        # interactive menu
./build/demos 6      # run demo [6] (Sugar basics) directly

docs.title: 6. Your first program
docs.text:
#include <iostream>
#include <metarpc/mt5_sugar.hpp>

int main() {
    using namespace metarpc;
    MT5Sugar sugar("mt5.mrpc.pro", 443 /*, apiKey */);

    try {
        sugar.connect(5057947437, "YourPassword", "MetaQuotes-Demo");

        std::cout << "balance : " << sugar.getBalance() << "\n";
        std::cout << "EURUSD  : bid " << sugar.getBid("EURUSD")
                  << "  ask " << sugar.getAsk("EURUSD") << "\n";
    } catch (const ApiError& e) {
        std::cerr << "API error: " << e.code << ": " << e.message << "\n";
        return 1;
    } catch (const TransportError& e) {
        std::cerr << "transport error: " << e.what() << "\n";
        return 1;
    }
    return 0;
}

Link it against the library:

add_executable(my_app main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE metarpc_cppmt5)

docs.title: Which layer should I use?
docs.text:
You want… Use The quickest possible code, smart defaults MT5Sugar Friendly C++ structs, full method set, UTC times MT5Service A field the facades don't expose, raw protobuf control MT5Account

All three live in one object: a connected MT5Sugar exposes service() and account(), so you can mix levels freely.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Your First Project — a guided build.
  • The examples/demos/ folder — 14 runnable examples across all three layers, plus orchestrators and a preset.

docs.title: 📖 CppMT5 Glossary
docs.text: The terms and concepts used across the CppMT5 SDK and MetaTrader 5 trading — the three layers in depth, then the C++, protocol, and trading vocabulary.

docs.title: MT5Account
docs.text:
🔹 Layer 1 — Low-level API

The base layer: direct access to the MT5 terminal over gRPC.

Key characteristics

  • Builds each protobuf …Request and attaches apikey + session id metadata.
  • Unwraps every reply's oneof { data, error } into the typed …Data payload, or throws ApiError.
  • Returns the protobuf …Data payloads — full control, maximum detail.
  • Owns the channel, stubs, retry/reconnect, and streaming (onSymbolTick, onTrade, …).
  • 39 methods across 7 groups, plus connection/identity helpers.

When to use: you need a field or variant the higher layers don't surface, or raw protobuf control.

Location: include/metarpc/mt5_account.hpp + src/mt5_account.cpp

Docs: MT5Account Master Overview

docs.title: MT5Service
docs.text:
🔸 Layer 2 — Friendly facade

The middle layer: friendly C++ structs and plain arguments, times in UTC — no protobuf.

Key characteristics

  • Takes plain args (&str symbols, int property ids, typed enums); builds the requests for you.
  • Unwraps …Data into clean values and named structs (AccountInfo, Tick, SymbolInfo, OrderResult, …).
  • Converts broker-server time ↔ UTC automatically (utcTimes = true by default).
  • The header is protobuf-free (forward-declares MT5Account) → fast compiles.
  • ~58 methods across 6 groups; reach the layer below with account().

When to use: most application code — ergonomic, typed calls without protobuf ceremony.

Location: include/metarpc/mt5_service.hpp + src/mt5_service.cpp

Docs: MT5Service Overview

docs.title: MT5Sugar
docs.text:
🔺 Layer 3 — Convenience API

The high-level layer: business logic and one-liners.

Key characteristics

  • Order construction from side/volume; pip-based SL/TP; risk-based position sizing.
  • Compact result structs (PriceInfo, DailyStats) on top of the Service structs.
  • Order methods return the resulting ticket (0 on rejection); management methods return bool / counts.
  • Also protobuf-free; reach down with service() and account().
  • ~58 methods across 11 groups — the best starting point for most apps.

Key examples

  • buyMarket(symbol, volume) — open a position in one line.
  • buyMarketWithPips(symbol, volume, slPips, tpPips) — open with a pip bracket.
  • calculatePositionSize(symbol, riskPercent, slPips) — size by risk.
  • getBalance() / getEquity() · closeAllPositions() — quick reads and an emergency exit.

When to use: rapid development, prototyping, simple strategies.

Location: include/metarpc/mt5_sugar.hpp + src/mt5_sugar.cpp

Docs: MT5Sugar API Overview

docs.title: No async/await — blocking calls + threads
docs.text: Every unary method is an ordinary blocking function that returns a value or throws. There is no async runtime. Run work concurrently with std::thread / std::async. See Concurrency Model.

docs.title: Errors are exceptions
docs.text: Calls don't return error codes — they throw. ApiError = the gateway/terminal rejected the request (bad login, invalid stops, trade rejected…). TransportError = the gRPC transport failed past the retry budget. Catch them at a sensible boundary.

docs.title: Streams
docs.text: Subscriptions return a std::unique_ptr<AccountStream> (low level) or ServiceStream (friendly). The SDK reads the server stream on a background thread and invokes your callback per payload. Keep the handle alive; stop() ends it. Handle API: stop() / running() / count() / lastError(). See gRPC Streaming.

docs.title: Friendly structs
docs.text: MT5Service / MT5Sugar return plain structs instead of protobuf: AccountInfo (login, balance, equity, leverage, currency, times…), Tick (symbol, bid, ask, volume, UTC time), SymbolInfo (digits, point, volume min/step/max, tick value…), OrderResult / OrderCheckResult, Position / PendingOrder, Bar, DailyStats.

docs.title: Enums
docs.text: Protobuf enums are int under the hood. In C++ the generated values live at namespace scope — write pb::ACCOUNT_BALANCE, pb::TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY (not a prefixed form). The friendly layers add typed C++ enums (TradeAction, Timeframe, TradeMode). See Enums Reference.

docs.title: ClientOptions
docs.text: Per-client transport knobs: unaryTimeoutMs, connectTimeoutMs, tradeTimeoutMs, maxRetries, maxBackoffMs, maxReceiveMessageBytes, rootCertsPath, verbose. Reach them via options().

docs.title: 🔌 gRPC & protocol
docs.text:
• gRPC — the RPC protocol the SDK uses to reach the MetaRPC gateway (HTTP/2 + TLS).
  • grpc++ / protobuf — the C++ libraries the SDK links against (from your toolchain, via pkg-config).
  • proto/mt5_term_api.desc (mt5_term_api) — the gRPC contract as a version-independent FileDescriptorSet. CMake runs protoc on it at build time to generate the C++ + gRPC stubs (namespace mt5_term_api, aliased pb inside the SDK) into build/generated/, matching your installed protobuf.
  • …Request / …Data / …Reply — a call sends a …Request; the server answers a …Reply carrying a …Data payload or an Error.
  • oneof { data, error } — how most replies wrap the result; MT5Account unwraps it to …Data or throws ApiError.
  • apikey — your MetaRPC token ("" → MRPC_API_KEY env, else "TRIAL"), sent as metadata on every call.
  • session id / Terminal GUID (terminalInstanceGuid) — the terminal session the gateway assigns on connect() (ConnectEx), auto-attached to later calls; read via terminalGuid().
  • ConnectEx — the RPC that starts/attaches an MT5 terminal for your account; connect() calls it.
  • RetCode (returned_code) — the trade-server result after a trading call; 10009 = DONE (success). See Return Codes.

docs.title: 💹 Market & prices
docs.text: Term Meaning Symbol A tradable instrument (EURUSD); names are broker-specific (suffixes like .m). Bid / Ask Best sell / best buy price. Spread = ask − bid. Point Smallest price step (SYMBOL_POINT), e.g. 0.00001 for 5-digit EURUSD. Pip 10 × point on 3/5-digit symbols (EURUSD 1 pip = 0.0001). Digits Decimal places in the price (SYMBOL_DIGITS). Tick One price update; tick value = money per tick per lot. Contract size Units per lot (e.g. 100,000 for FX). Volume / lot Trade size; bounded by volumeMin / volumeStep / volumeMax. Bar One OHLC candle for a Timeframe (M1…MN1). Market Watch The terminal's selected-symbols list; some calls need a symbol selected (symbolSelect). DOM (Depth of Market) Level-II order book; subscribe/read/release (marketBookAdd/Get/Release).

docs.title: 📈 Orders, positions & deals
docs.text:
In MT5, orders, positions and deals are distinct:

  • Order — an instruction to trade (market or pending).
  • Position — the open exposure from a filled order.
  • Deal — an executed transaction in history; realized P/L lives on deals.
  • Pending order — rests until a price triggers it: Limit (better price) / Stop (breakout) / Stop-Limit.
  • SL / TP — protective Stop-Loss / Take-Profit exit prices.
  • Stops level (SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL) — minimum distance SL/TP may sit from the market, in points.
  • Freeze level — distance within which modify/close is blocked.
  • Slippage / deviation — allowed price movement between request and fill, in points.
  • Magic number — a client id tagging orders from one strategy (sent as expert_id).
  • Ticket — the numeric id of an order / position / deal.

docs.title: 💰 Account & money
docs.text: Term Meaning Balance Realized funds, excluding floating P/L. Equity Balance + floating P/L (live account value). Margin Funds reserved to hold open positions. Free margin equity − margin; available for new positions. Margin level equity / margin × 100, in percent (margin-call / stop-out below thresholds; 0 when flat). Leverage Borrowing ratio (e.g. 1:100). Floating / unrealized P/L Profit of still-open positions (equity − balance). Realized P/L Profit of closed positions (from history).

docs.title: 🕐 Time
docs.text:
• Broker server time — the raw time on the wire; MT5Account returns it unchanged.
  • UTC conversion — MT5Service / MT5Sugar convert to/from UTC using the broker offset (serverOffsetSeconds). With utcTimes = true (the default) every time you see and pass is UTC.

docs.title: 🛡️ Strategy mechanics
docs.text:
• Breakeven — moving SL to (around) the entry once in profit, to remove risk.
  • Trailing stop — an SL that follows price in the favorable direction, ratcheting and never loosening.
  • Risk sizing — choosing lot size so a stop-out risks a fixed % of balance (calculatePositionSize).
  • Orchestrator — a small strategy manager (loop: read → act → repeat) built on MT5Sugar: Trailing Stop, Grid Trader, Risk Manager.
  • Preset — a coordinator that classifies the market and dispatches to an orchestrator: Adaptive Market Mode. See Strategies.

docs.title: 📚 See also
docs.text:
• Getting Started · Project Map · MT5 for Beginners
  • Return Codes · Enums Reference · gRPC Streaming · Protobuf Inspector

docs.title: gRPC Streaming
docs.text: Besides request/response calls, the gateway offers server streams — long-lived subscriptions that push data (ticks, trade events, position profit, …). In CppMT5 a subscription runs on its own background thread and delivers payloads to a callback.

docs.title: The model
docs.text:
sugar.service().subscribeTicks({...}, cb)  ──▶  ServiceStream handle   (you hold this)
                                                      │
                                                      ▼  background reader thread
                                                   cb(Tick)   cb(Tick)   cb(Tick) …
  • Opening a stream returns a handle (AccountStream at the low level, ServiceStream at the friendly level). Keep the handle alive for as long as you want data.
  • The callback runs on a dedicated reader thread. Destroying the handle — or calling stop() — cancels the stream and joins that thread.
  • Streams do not go through the retry/reconnect machinery (there is nothing to retry on a long-lived stream); an error ends the stream and is reported via lastError().
Handle method stop() cancel and join the reader thread (idempotent; also run by the destructor) running() false once the stream ended or was cancelled count() payloads delivered so far lastError() the error that ended it, or "" if clean

docs.title: Friendly streams (MT5Service)
docs.text:
Converted structs, times in UTC:

Method Payload subscribeTicks(symbols, cb) Tick streamTradeUpdates(cb) TradeEvent streamTransactions(cb) TransactionEvent streamPositionProfits(cb) PositionProfitEvent streamOpenedTickets(cb) TicketsSnapshot 
using namespace metarpc;
MT5Service& svc = sugar.service();
svc.symbolSelect("EURUSD", true);   // a symbol must be selected to stream

auto stream = svc.subscribeTicks({"EURUSD"}, [](const Tick& t) {
    std::cout << t.symbol << "  bid=" << t.bid << " ask=" << t.ask << "  t=" << t.time << "\n";
});

// ... let it run; the handle keeps the subscription alive ...
std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(10));
stream->stop();
if (!stream->lastError().empty()) std::cerr << "ended: " << stream->lastError() << "\n";

docs.title: Low-level streams (MT5Account)
docs.text:
Raw protobuf payloads, raw server time:

namespace pb = mt5_term_api;
pb::OnSymbolTickRequest req; req.add_symbol_names("EURUSD");
auto s = sugar.account().onSymbolTick(req, [](const pb::OnSymbolTickData& d) {
    if (d.has_symbol_tick()) std::cout << d.symbol_tick().bid() << "\n";
});

Also available: onTrade, onTradeTransaction, onPositionProfit, onPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets.

docs.title: Guidelines
docs.text:
• Don't block the callback. It runs on the reader thread and holds up the next payload — do slow work on another thread or push into a queue.
  • Exceptions thrown by your callback are swallowed (they will not crash the reader thread), so handle errors inside it if you care about them.
  • One handle per subscription. Store it; a dropped handle immediately cancels the stream.
  • Thread-safety: the handle's accessors are safe from any thread; your own shared state is not — guard it (e.g. with an atomic or a mutex), as the demos do with std::atomic<int>.

docs.title: Re-subscribing after an error
docs.text:
Streams are not auto-reconnected (unlike unary calls). When a stream ends on an error, running() turns false and lastError() holds the reason — it's up to you to open a new one:

std::unique_ptr<ServiceStream> stream = svc.subscribeTicks({"EURUSD"}, onTick);

// a supervisor loop that re-subscribes if the stream drops
while (keepRunning) {
    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(1));
    if (!stream->running()) {
        std::cerr << "stream ended: " << stream->lastError() << " — resubscribing\n";
        stream = svc.subscribeTicks({"EURUSD"}, onTick);   // old handle is replaced (and stopped)
    }
}

Because a dropped stream often follows a terminal hiccup, the next unary call will transparently re-attach the terminal (ConnectEx), so a fresh subscription usually succeeds immediately.

docs.title: 📚 See also
docs.text:
• Low-level: MT5Account · Streaming Methods (per-method pages)
  • Friendly: MT5Service · Streaming Methods
  • Concurrency Model — threads, deadlines, running work in parallel

docs.title: MT5 for Beginners: Your First Steps in Trading
docs.text: Welcome! This guide is for complete beginners who have never worked with MetaTrader 5 or trading. We'll get you from zero to a working demo account you can automate with CppMT5.

docs.title: What is MetaTrader 5 (MT5)?
docs.text:
MetaTrader 5 is a trading platform used by millions of traders worldwide. It lets you:

  • Trade forex, stocks, commodities, and cryptocurrencies
  • Analyze markets with charts and indicators
  • Execute automated trading strategies
  • Monitor your positions in real-time

Think of MT5 as the "cockpit" for the markets. MetaRPC runs real MT5 terminals in the cloud and CppMT5 lets your C++ program drive one over gRPC. So the chain is:

your C++ program  ──▶  CppMT5  ──gRPC──▶  MetaRPC gateway  ──▶  an MT5 terminal  ──▶  your broker

docs.title: Demo vs Live account: start safely
docs.text:
A demo account is a risk-free practice account with virtual money — start here:

  • ✅ Zero risk — virtual funds (typically $10,000 – $100,000)
  • ✅ Real market conditions — live prices and behavior
  • ✅ Learn the platform — before risking real money
  • ✅ Test your code — perfect for developing CppMT5 apps

A live account uses real money. Only go live once you understand MT5, have tested thoroughly on demo, and understand the risks.

docs.title: The vocabulary you need
docs.text:
• Symbol — a tradable instrument, e.g. EURUSD, XAUUSD.
  • Bid / Ask — the price to sell at / buy at. Their gap is the spread.
  • Lot / volume — trade size. 0.01 lots is the usual minimum ("a micro lot").
  • Position — an open trade. It has a direction (BUY/SELL), a volume, and a floating profit.
  • Pending order — an order waiting at a price to become a position (limit/stop).
  • SL / TP — stop loss and take profit: prices at which the position auto-closes to cap a loss or lock a gain.
  • Balance vs Equity — balance is settled money; equity is balance plus the profit/loss of what is currently open.
  • Margin / free margin — money the broker reserves to hold your positions, and what's left to open more.

See the full Glossary.

docs.title: Order vs position vs deal
docs.text:
MT5 keeps these three separate — it trips up almost everyone at first:

  • An order is the instruction ("buy 0.1 lots of EURUSD").
  • Once it fills, you hold a position — the live exposure that shows a floating profit.
  • Every execution is recorded in history as a deal — that's where realized profit lives.

A single market buy creates an order → a position → a deal. A pending order sits as just an order until its price is reached.

docs.title: Quick start: creating a demo account
docs.text: The fastest way is to create a demo account directly in the MT5 terminal.

docs.title: Step 1️⃣ — Download and install the MT5 terminal
docs.text:
1. Visit https://www.metatrader5.com/en/download
  2. Download the version for your OS (Windows / macOS / Linux)
  3. Install the application

docs.title: Step 2️⃣ — Launch MT5 and find the Navigator panel
docs.text:
On first launch a popup usually offers to open a new account. If not, find the Navigator panel (left side, below Market Watch).

Inside Navigator you'll see Accounts, Indicators, Expert Advisors, and more.

docs.title: Step 3️⃣ — Open a new demo account
docs.text:
1. In Navigator, find Accounts
  2. Right-click "Accounts"
  3. Select "Open an account"

docs.title: Step 4️⃣ — Select the MetaQuotes demo server
docs.text: In the broker search window, look for "MetaQuotes-Demo" (the standard demo server). Use the search field if needed, select it, and click Next.

docs.title: Step 5️⃣ — Account type
docs.text: Choose "Open a new demo account" and click Next.

docs.title: Step 6️⃣ — Fill in your details
docs.text: Name, email, account type, virtual deposit (e.g. $10,000), leverage (1:100 is fine to start), currency. Agree to the terms and click Next.

docs.title: Step 7️⃣ — Save your credentials
docs.text:
MT5 creates the account and shows:

  • Login — your account number (e.g. 5057947437)
  • Password — your master (trading) password
  • Investor Password — read-only password
  • Server — e.g. "MetaQuotes-Demo"

⚠️ Save these now — you need Login, Password, and Server to connect from CppMT5. Click Finish.

docs.title: Step 8️⃣ — Connect from CppMT5
docs.text:
You also need a MetaRPC API key (free) — sign up at https://mrpc.pro/signup and generate one at https://mrpc.pro/my. Provide it via the MRPC_API_KEY environment variable (or the constructor / config.json):

export MRPC_API_KEY=your_mrpc_token    # from https://mrpc.pro/my

Then pass your MT5 credentials straight to the SDK:

#include <iostream>
#include <metarpc/mt5_sugar.hpp>
using namespace metarpc;

int main() {
    MT5Sugar sugar("mt5.mrpc.pro", 443);                 // default endpoint
    sugar.connect(5057947437, "YourPasswordHere", "MetaQuotes-Demo");   // exact server name

    std::cout << "balance " << sugar.getBalance() << "\n";
    std::cout << "EURUSD  " << sugar.getBid("EURUSD") << " / " << sugar.getAsk("EURUSD") << "\n";

    sugar.disconnect();
}
  • Login / password — exactly what MT5 showed you.
  • Server name — the exact string (e.g. "MetaQuotes-Demo").
  • endpoint / API key — "mt5.mrpc.pro", 443 is the default; the key comes from MRPC_API_KEY.

docs.title: Step 9️⃣ — Verify the MT5 connection
docs.text: In the MT5 terminal, the bottom-right corner should show a green connection indicator and your balance (e.g. $10,000).

docs.title: Step 🔟 — Build and run
docs.text:
cmake -G Ninja -B build && cmake --build build
./build/my_bot

Trades your program makes appear in the MT5 terminal in real time. It's virtual money — experiment freely. See Your First Project for a fuller walkthrough.

docs.title: Your first five calls
docs.text:
Everything below uses MT5Sugar, the friendliest layer:

MT5Sugar sugar("mt5.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(5057947437, "YourPassword", "MetaQuotes-Demo");   // 1. connect

double bal = sugar.getBalance();              // 2. how much money?
double bid = sugar.getBid("EURUSD");          // 3. what's the price?
uint64_t t = sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.01); // 4. buy a micro lot
sugar.closePosition((int64_t)t);              // 5. close it

Did the order actually fill?

A call returning without an error is not the same as a filled trade. buyMarket returns the new ticket, or 0 if the broker rejected it — always check it. The friendly orderSend returns an OrderResult whose retcode == 10009 means done. See Return Codes.

docs.title: 🧩 MT5 password types
docs.text:
Master password — full access (open/close trades, change settings). This is the one CppMT5 uses to trade.

Investor password — view-only: see trades/balance/history but cannot trade. Good for sharing performance or monitoring. Set it via Tools → Options → Server → Change (Investor Password).

docs.title: Choosing a broker (optional)
docs.text:
The MetaQuotes demo server is fine for practice. For live trading later you may pick a specific broker for better conditions or regional support.

Not financial advice — do your own research. Popular MT5 brokers include IC Markets, Pepperstone, OANDA, XM, RoboForex, FxPro.

What to look for: regulation (FCA/ASIC/CySEC/…), genuine MT5 support (not just MT4), a free demo, tight spreads, responsive support.

docs.title: Important reminders
docs.text:
• 🛡️ Security — never share your master password; use the investor password for monitoring tools. Keep credentials out of your repo (don't commit config.json with real values).
  • 📊 Risk management — even on demo, build good habits: always use a stop-loss, risk ≤ 1–2% per trade, size with MT5Sugar::calculatePositionSize.
  • 🧪 Testing — test on demo first; verify strategies over weeks/months, not days. Demo results don't guarantee live results.
  • 📚 Education — trading has a steep learning curve; focus on learning, not earning.

docs.title: What's next?
docs.text:
1. Getting Started — install, build, get an API key, run a demo.
  2. Your First Project — a complete little program.
  3. Understand the layers: MT5Account (low-level) · MT5Service (friendly) · MT5Sugar (one-liners, most beginner-friendly).
  4. Strategies — ready orchestrators and a preset.
  5. Glossary · Project Map — the vocabulary and the lay of the land.

Good luck on your trading journey! 🚀

docs.title: 🗺️ CppMT5 Project Map
docs.text: The whole project as one annotated tree, with links. Links point to section overviews, never to individual method pages — open an overview to drill down into its methods.

docs.title: 🧱 The three layers
docs.text:
CppMT5 is built in three decoupled layers (composition, not inheritance). Each layer owns the one below it, so a connected MT5Sugar gives you all three. Your code can enter at any level.

Layer Source What it does Overview 3 · MT5Sugar include/metarpc/mt5_sugar.hpp · src/mt5_sugar.cpp Convenience on top of Service: one-liners, pip-based SL/TP, risk-based sizing, batch close, quick reads. MT5Sugar overview 2 · MT5Service include/metarpc/mt5_service.hpp · src/mt5_service.cpp Friendly facade: plain args and named C++ structs, UTC times, protobuf-free header. What most code uses. MT5Service overview 1 · MT5Account include/metarpc/mt5_account.hpp · src/mt5_account.cpp Low-level gRPC: builds each proto …Request, attaches auth metadata, unwraps replies to …Data (or throws); connection & streaming. Everything builds on it. MT5Account overview 
Your code → MT5Sugar → MT5Service → MT5Account → gRPC → MetaRPC gateway → MT5 terminal

Mix freely: sugar.service() borrows the Service, service.account() (or sugar.account()) borrows the Account.

Compile-time note: mt5_service.hpp and mt5_sugar.hpp are protobuf-free (they forward-declare MT5Account), so including them does not pull in the ~11 MB of generated headers. Only translation units that reach mt5_account.hpp — directly or via account() — pay that cost.

docs.title: 🎯 Which layer should you use?
docs.text:
• Most trading apps → MT5Sugar. Risk sizing, pip math and bulk ops out of the box.
  • Custom execution → MT5Service. Friendly typed calls when you manage your own order shapes.
  • Protocol-level control → MT5Account. Raw proto structures and streams.

docs.title: 🔧 Transport behaviour (shared by every call)
docs.text:
• Retry — transient gRPC failures (UNAVAILABLE, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) are retried with exponential back-off, up to ClientOptions::maxRetries.
  • Reconnect — a TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND transparently re-issues ConnectEx and retries, so a terminal restart is invisible to your code.
  • Errors — anything else becomes an ApiError (server said no) or TransportError (transport gave up). See Return Codes.

docs.title: Protobuf Inspector — Interactive Type Explorer
docs.text:
An offline developer tool that explores the MT5 gRPC protobuf messages, fields and enums — browse, search, find which message declares a field, and list enum values, all without connecting to MT5.

Source: examples/tools/protobuf_inspector.cpp · Run: ./build/protobuf_inspector

docs.title: How C++ does this
docs.text:
The C# / Go / Java inspectors use runtime reflection over the protobuf descriptors their libraries keep in memory — and so does this one. Unlike Rust's prost (which keeps no runtime descriptors), the C++ protobuf runtime registers a full descriptor for every generated message and enum at static-init time.

So this tool simply reads the global generated descriptor pool:

const auto* pool = google::protobuf::DescriptorPool::generated_pool();

and walks the mt5_term_api proto files compiled into the library. Because it reads the very descriptors the SDK uses on the wire, it can never drift from your types — the field names, tags, proto types and repeated / map / oneof shapes it prints are exactly what the generated C++ structs expose.

Why --whole-archive

The generated .pb.cc live in the static library metarpc_cppmt5. A static library only pulls in a translation unit that something references — so descriptors for messages your main() never names would be dropped, and the inspector would see an incomplete pool. The CMake target links the library with -Wl,--whole-archive (MSVC: /WHOLEARCHIVE) so every generated file registers itself. That's the whole trick.

docs.title: 🏁 Running it
docs.text:
It's a standalone target and needs no credentials or connection:

cmake --build build --target protobuf_inspector
./build/protobuf_inspector

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║   🔍 PROTOBUF INSPECTOR — mt5_term_api               ║
║  Explore MT5 gRPC messages & enums offline           ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
Indexed 359 messages, 70 enums from the generated code.
Type 'help' for commands.

>

docs.title: 🧰 Commands
docs.text:
Command Description Example list / ls List all message types list enums List all enum types enums <TypeName> Inspect a message — its fields and types AccountSummaryData search <text> / find <text> Search types by name search Position field <name> Find messages that declare a field field ticket enum <name> Show an enum's values enum TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE help / ? Help help exit / quit / q Exit exit

Type names and field names are case-insensitive. A bare token is resolved as a message first, then an enum.

docs.title: 1) Inspect a message's fields
docs.text:
> AccountSummaryData

╔═══════════════════════ MESSAGE: AccountSummaryData ═══════════════════════╗

📋 Fields (21):

  • #1   account_login                             : int64
  • #2   account_balance                           : double
  • #3   account_equity                            : double
  • #5   account_leverage                          : int64
  • #6   account_trade_mode                        : MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode
  • #9   server_time                               : Timestamp
  • #14  server_time_utc                           : Timestamp
  • #17  account_margin_mode                       : MrpcEnumAccountMarginMode
  ...

#n is the protobuf field tag; the type is the proto type. repeated … and map<…> are shown where relevant, and message / enum fields show the referenced type name. These are the real accessors on the generated class — summary.account_balance(), summary.account_trade_mode(), etc. (snake_case getters in C++).

docs.title: 2) A oneof reply
docs.text:
> AccountSummaryReply

╔═════════════ MESSAGE: AccountSummaryReply ═════════════╗

📋 Fields (2):

  • #1   data    : AccountSummaryData   (oneof response)
  • #2   error   : Error                (oneof response)

The *Reply messages wrap their payload in a response oneof of Data | Error — exactly what MT5Account unwraps (returning the Data, or throwing ApiError for the Error).

docs.title: 3) Which messages carry a ticket field?
docs.text:
> field ticket

  📦 DealHistoryData
       └─ ticket : uint64
  📦 OpenedOrderInfo
       └─ ticket : uint64
  📦 OrderCloseRequest
       └─ ticket : uint64
  📦 OrderModifyRequest
       └─ ticket : uint64
  📦 PositionInfo
       └─ ticket : uint64
  📦 OnPositionProfitPositionInfo
       └─ ticket : int64
  ...

docs.title: 4) See an enum's values
docs.text:
> enum TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE

╔═════════════ ENUM: TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE ═════════════╗

  TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY                            = 0
  TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_SELL                           = 1
  TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY_LIMIT                      = 2
  TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_SELL_LIMIT                     = 3
  TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY_STOP                       = 4
  TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_SELL_STOP                      = 5
  TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY_STOP_LIMIT                 = 6
  TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_SELL_STOP_LIMIT                = 7
  TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_CLOSE_BY                       = 8

In C++ these enum values live at namespace scope — you write pb::TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY (where namespace pb = mt5_term_api;), not a prefixed form. See Enums Reference.

docs.title: 🧩 How it works
docs.text:
• DescriptorPool::generated_pool() returns the global pool the protobuf runtime fills at static-init.
  • The tool calls FindFileByName(...) for each of the 19 mt5-term-api-*.proto files, then walks file->message_type(i) / file->enum_type(i), recursing into nested types — building the complete 359 messages / 70 enums index.
  • For each message it reads Descriptor::field(i): the tag (field->number()), name (field->name()), proto type (field->type_name(), or the referenced message_type() / enum_type() name), and shape (is_repeated(), is_map(), real_containing_oneof()).
  • Everything is static — no terminal connection, no network, no extra dependencies beyond the protobuf runtime the SDK already links.

Source: examples/tools/protobuf_inspector.cpp.

Want just the contract? The whole gRPC contract everything is built on ships as one version-independent file, proto/mt5_term_api.desc (a protobuf FileDescriptorSet). Download that single file and generate stubs for any language: protoc --descriptor_set_in=mt5_term_api.desc --python_out=. <file>.proto. CMake does exactly this (for C++) at build time, so the SDK never ships version-locked generated code.

See also: Enums Reference · Project Map · Glossary · Return Codes

docs.title: Return Codes & Error Handling
docs.text: CppMT5 reports failures two ways: exceptions for failed RPCs, and a numeric trade retcode inside a successful trade reply. Understand both.

docs.title: Exceptions (RPC-level)
docs.text:
Every method throws on failure — there are no error-code return values.

try {
    sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.1);
} catch (const metarpc::ApiError& e) {
    // the gateway/terminal said no
    std::cerr << e.code << ": " << e.message
              << "  (mql " << e.mqlErrorCode << ", trade " << e.mqlTradeCode << ")\n";
    if (e.isInvalidLogin()) { /* bad credentials — do not retry */ }
} catch (const metarpc::TransportError& e) {
    // transport failed past the retry budget
    std::cerr << "transport " << e.grpcCode << ": " << e.what() << "\n";
}
Exception When Key fields ApiError the server understood the request and returned an error payload (bad login, unknown symbol, trade rejected, terminal not found) code, message, mqlErrorCode, mqlTradeCode, where; helpers isInvalidLogin(), isTerminalNotFound() TransportError a gRPC transport failure survived all retries grpcCode (14 = UNAVAILABLE, 4 = DEADLINE_EXCEEDED)

What is not an exception, because the SDK handles it for you:

  • Transient transport failures → retried with exponential back-off (ClientOptions::maxRetries).
  • TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND → automatic ConnectEx re-attach, then retry.

docs.title: Trade retcodes (order-level)
docs.text:
A trade RPC can succeed as an RPC and still reject the trade. Always inspect the retcode:

OrderResult r = sugar.service().orderSend(req);
if (r.ok()) std::cout << "done, deal #" << r.deal << "\n";       // ok() = 10009 / 10008 / 10010
else        std::cout << "rejected " << r.retcode << ": " << r.retcodeDescription << "\n";

OrderResult::ok() is true for the accepted codes (done / placed / done-partial). The ones you will meet most:

Code Name Meaning 10009 TRADE_RETCODE_DONE Request completed — success 10008 TRADE_RETCODE_PLACED Pending order placed 10010 TRADE_RETCODE_DONE_PARTIAL Only part of the volume filled 10004 TRADE_RETCODE_REQUOTE Price changed — retry with a fresh price 10006 TRADE_RETCODE_REJECT Request rejected 10013 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID Invalid request 10014 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_VOLUME Volume below min / above max / off step 10015 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_PRICE Invalid price 10016 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_STOPS SL/TP too close (below the symbol's stops level) 10018 TRADE_RETCODE_MARKET_CLOSED Market is closed 10019 TRADE_RETCODE_NO_MONEY Not enough free margin 10027 TRADE_RETCODE_CLIENT_DISABLES_AT Autotrading disabled on the client

orderCheck() returns the same kind of retcode without sending anything — use it to pre-flight a trade (0 means it would pass).

docs.title: A robust trade pattern
docs.text:
try {
    OrderRequest q; q.symbol = "EURUSD"; q.action = TradeAction::Buy; q.volume = 0.1;

    auto check = sugar.service().orderCheck(q);
    if (!check.ok()) { std::cerr << "pre-check failed: " << check.comment << "\n"; return; }

    auto r = sugar.service().orderSend(q);
    if (!r.ok()) std::cerr << "send rejected: " << r.retcode << " " << r.retcodeDescription << "\n";
}
catch (const metarpc::ApiError& e)       { std::cerr << "API: " << e.what() << "\n"; }
catch (const metarpc::TransportError& e) { std::cerr << "transport: " << e.what() << "\n"; }

docs.title: Where the two meet
docs.text:
Some trade failures surface as an ApiError rather than a retcode on a returned OrderResult (for example when the terminal rejects the request outright). In that case the MQL trade code is on the exception as mqlTradeCode, and the symbolic code is in code:

try {
    sugar.service().orderSend(q);
} catch (const metarpc::ApiError& e) {
    if (e.mqlTradeCode == 10019) std::cerr << "not enough money\n";   // same 10019 as the table
    else std::cerr << e.code << ": " << e.message << "\n";
}

So: inspect OrderResult::retcode when a call returns, and ApiError::mqlTradeCode when it throws — they speak the same numbering.

docs.title: Concurrency Model
docs.text: CppMT5 has no async/await. There are exactly two shapes of call, and plain C++ threads are all you need to run things concurrently.

docs.title: Two shapes of call
docs.text: Shape What it is How you consume it Unary (request/response) getBalance(), symbolInfoTick(), orderSend() … an ordinary blocking function; it returns (value) or throws Server stream subscribeTicks(), streamTradeUpdates() … returns a handle; the SDK reads the stream on a background thread and calls your callback

docs.title: Unary — synchronous
docs.text:
double bal = sugar.getBalance();        // blocks until the reply (or the deadline), then returns
auto    t  = sugar.getPriceInfo("EURUSD");

There is nothing to await; the gRPC round-trip happens inside the function, with the deadline from ClientOptions. Failures are exceptions (ApiError / TransportError).

docs.title: Streaming — one background thread per subscription
docs.text: See gRPC Streaming. The callback runs on the stream's reader thread; keep the handle alive, call stop() to end it.

docs.title: Running work concurrently
docs.text:
Use std::thread / std::async yourself — fan out independent calls:

#include <future>

auto bid = std::async(std::launch::async, [&]{ return sugar.getBid("EURUSD"); });
auto ask = std::async(std::launch::async, [&]{ return sugar.getAsk("GBPUSD"); });
std::cout << bid.get() << " " << ask.get() << "\n";

Or run a management loop in the background while the main flow continues:

std::atomic<bool> stop{false};
std::thread monitor([&]{
    while (!stop) {
        if (sugar.getMarginLevel() < 150 && sugar.countOpenPositions() > 0)
            sugar.closeAllPositions();
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(2));
    }
});
// ... later ...
stop = true; monitor.join();

docs.title: Thread-safety rules
docs.text:
• One MT5Account/MT5Service/MT5Sugar owns one gRPC channel. Unary calls may be issued from multiple threads, but connect() / reconnect() / close() mutate the channel and must not race with in-flight calls — do them from one thread, before fanning out.
  • Stream callbacks run on their own threads. Guard any state you share with the main thread (the demos use std::atomic), and don't block the callback — push slow work elsewhere.
  • Prefer one stream with many symbols over many single-symbol streams where the API allows it (subscribeTicks({"EURUSD","GBPUSD"}, cb)).

docs.title: Deadlines & timeouts
docs.text:
There is no per-call ctx/cancellation token. Each unary call runs against a per-attempt deadline from ClientOptions; set it once on the client before you fan out:

sugar.service().options().unaryTimeoutMs = 5000;    // ordinary reads (default 30000)
sugar.service().options().tradeTimeoutMs = 60000;   // OrderSend/Modify/Close
sugar.service().options().connectTimeoutMs = 200000;// ConnectEx (a cold terminal start is slow)
sugar.service().options().maxRetries = 5;           // transient-failure / reconnect budget

A call that exceeds its deadline is retried up to maxRetries, then throws TransportError (grpcCode == 4, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED). Timeouts are per attempt, not a total budget — size them for one round-trip, not the whole retry sequence.

docs.title: Your First Project
docs.text: A standalone C++ program that connects, reads the account, quotes a symbol, and places one tiny order — then closes it. ~10 minutes.

docs.title: 0. Get an API key
docs.text:
To reach MetaRPC (mt5.mrpc.pro:443):

  1. Register free at https://mrpc.pro/signup.
  2. Generate a token in the portal at https://mrpc.pro/my, under API Keys.
  3. Expose it to your program: export MRPC_API_KEY=your_token (the SDK reads MRPC_API_KEY, falling back to "TRIAL"), or pass it to the MT5Sugar constructor.

You also need an MT5 demo account (login, password, server name) — see MT5 for Beginners. Keep the trade block below on a demo account you're happy to trade.

docs.title: 1. Project files
docs.text:
my_bot/
├── CMakeLists.txt
└── main.cpp

CMakeLists.txt — link against the CppMT5 library (built per Getting Started, installed or added via add_subdirectory):

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.15)
project(my_bot CXX)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)

add_subdirectory(path/to/CppMT5 cppmt5)   # or find_package if installed
add_executable(my_bot main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(my_bot PRIVATE metarpc_cppmt5)

docs.title: 2. Connect and read
docs.text:
#include <iostream>
#include <metarpc/mt5_sugar.hpp>
using namespace metarpc;

int main() {
    MT5Sugar sugar("mt5.mrpc.pro", 443 /*, "YOUR_API_KEY" */);
    try {
        sugar.connect(5057947437, "YourPassword", "MetaQuotes-Demo");

        std::cout << "connected: " << sugar.isConnected()
                  << "  balance: " << sugar.getBalance() << "\n";

        auto px = sugar.getPriceInfo("EURUSD");
        std::cout << "EURUSD  bid " << px.bid << "  ask " << px.ask
                  << "  spread " << px.spread << "\n";

docs.title: 3. Size the trade and pre-check
docs.text:
double lots = sugar.calculatePositionSize("EURUSD", /*risk%*/ 1.0, /*stopPips*/ 50);
        std::string why;
        if (!sugar.canOpenPosition("EURUSD", lots, why)) {
            std::cout << "cannot open: " << why << "\n";
            return 0;
        }

docs.title: 4. Open, manage, close
docs.text:
uint64_t ticket = sugar.buyMarketWithPips("EURUSD", lots, /*sl*/ 50, /*tp*/ 100);
        if (!ticket) { std::cout << "order rejected\n"; return 0; }
        std::cout << "opened #" << ticket << " (" << lots << " lots)\n";

        // ... your logic would monitor it here ...

        std::cout << "close -> " << (sugar.closePosition((int64_t)ticket) ? "ok" : "failed") << "\n";

    } catch (const ApiError& e) {
        std::cerr << "API error: " << e.code << ": " << e.message << "\n";
        return 1;
    } catch (const TransportError& e) {
        std::cerr << "transport error: " << e.what() << "\n";
        return 1;
    }
    return 0;
}

docs.title: 5. Build and run
docs.text:
cmake -G Ninja -B build && cmake --build build
./build/my_bot

docs.title: 🔌 Usage pattern (raw gRPC)
docs.text:
Every method is called on an MT5Account (#include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc). It owns the gRPC channel, sends the terminal id and API key as metadata, retries transient failures, re-attaches a dropped terminal session, and unwraps the reply — returning the protobuf *Data payload or throwing.

#include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>
using namespace metarpc;
namespace pb = mt5_term_api;              // the generated protobuf namespace

// Create the account (prepares the gRPC channel)
MT5Account account("mt5.mrpc.pro", 443);

// Connect the terminal (login, password, broker server)
account.connect(5057947437, "password", "MetaQuotes-Demo");
// The gateway returns a terminal session GUID; later calls reuse it automatically.

// Call a method: returns the Data payload, or throws ApiError / TransportError
pb::AccountSummaryData s = account.accountSummary();
std::printf("Balance: $%.2f\n", s.account_balance());

Every method follows the same shape:

  • Proto Service/Method: Service.Method(Request) → Reply
  • C++ call: account.method(const pb::Request&) returns pb::MethodData (by value)
  • Reply structure: the gRPC reply carries either a Data payload or an Error; MT5Account returns the Data and turns Error into a thrown ApiError (server-side error) — transport failures past the retry budget throw TransportError
  • Return codes: trading operations return status codes (10009 = success / DONE)

Timestamps: proto uses google.protobuf.Timestamp. The raw layer gives you broker/server time; the friendly MT5Service layer converts to UTC for you.

Streaming methods: return a std::unique_ptr<AccountStream>. The SDK reads the stream on a background thread and invokes your callback for each message; keep the handle alive and call stop() to end it.

docs.title: Layer 1: MT5Account (Low-Level) — You are here!
docs.text:
What: direct proto/gRPC communication with the MT5 terminal.

When to use: - You need full control over the protocol - You are building custom wrappers - Proto-level integration is required

Characteristics: - Works with proto *Request / *Data objects - Raw gRPC method calls - Complete access to all MT5 functions - Highest complexity

Location: include/metarpc/mt5_account.hpp + src/mt5_account.cpp (on top of the gRPC stubs generated at build time from proto/mt5_term_api.desc into build/generated/)

Documentation: this folder (you are here!)

docs.title: Layer 2: MT5Service
docs.text:
What: a friendly facade over MT5Account — clean arguments, friendly C++ structs, times in UTC. Its header is protobuf-free, so strategy code compiles fast.

When to use: - You want a clean API without touching protobuf - You want named struct fields instead of proto getters - You want times already converted to UTC

Location: include/metarpc/mt5_service.hpp + src/mt5_service.cpp

Documentation: MT5Service.Overview.md

docs.title: Layer 3: MT5Sugar
docs.text:
What: high-level convenience API with ~60 one-liner methods.

When to use: - Most trading scenarios (95% of cases) - You want risk-based position sizing and smart defaults - You are building strategies quickly

Location: include/metarpc/mt5_sugar.hpp + src/mt5_sugar.cpp

Documentation: MT5Sugar.API_Overview.md

docs.title: 🎓 Learning Path
docs.text:
Recommended sequence: start from the foundation (MT5Account) → build up to the convenience layers (MT5Service → MT5Sugar).

Each layer owns the one below it: MT5Sugar owns an MT5Service, which owns an MT5Account. From Sugar you can always reach down with sugar.service() and sugar.account().

Summary: MT5Account (foundation) → MT5Service (friendly facade) → MT5Sugar (one-liners).

docs.title: Proto Return Codes
docs.text:
• 10009 = Success / DONE
  • 10004 = Requote
  • 10006 = Request rejected
  • 10013 = Invalid request
  • 10014 = Invalid volume
  • 10015 = Invalid price
  • 10016 = Invalid stops
  • 10018 = Market closed
  • 10019 = Not enough money
  • 10031 = No connection with trade server

Always check the returned_code field of a trading reply. See the full Return Codes Reference.

docs.title: ⚠️ Important Notes
docs.text:
• Demo account first: always test on demo before live trading.
  • Check return codes: every trading operation returns a status code (10009 = success).
  • Validate parameters: use orderCheck() before orderSend().
  • Handle errors: catch ApiError (server rejected the request) and TransportError (network/transport failed past retries).
  • Stream cleanup: call stop() on the stream handle, and keep the handle alive while you need events.
  • Time zones: raw-layer time fields are in the broker server's time zone; the MT5Service layer converts them to UTC.
  • Broker limitations: not all brokers support all features (DOM, hedging, etc.).

"Trade safe, code clean, and may your gRPC streams always flow smoothly."

docs.title: ✅ Getting a Single Double Account Property
docs.text:
Request: one floating-point account value (AccountInfoDoubleData) from MT5 — balance, equity, margin, profit, etc. — selected by a property enum.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::accountInfoDouble(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: AccountInfoDouble (defined in mt5-term-api-account-information.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: AccountInfoDouble(AccountInfoDoubleRequest) → AccountInfoDoubleReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC that returns a single double chosen by an AccountInfoDoublePropertyType enum.
  • Why you need it. Lighter than accountSummary() when you only need one number (e.g. just the free margin before sizing a trade).
  • Sanity check. ACCOUNT_BALANCE should match the balance from accountSummary().

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Read one monetary metric without pulling the whole summary.
  • Poll a single value cheaply (e.g. ACCOUNT_EQUITY on a timer).
  • Feed risk math: ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE, ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL, ACCOUNT_PROFIT.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns the single double value selected by req.property_id().
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::AccountInfoDoubleData accountInfoDouble(const pb::AccountInfoDoubleRequest& req);

Request message:

AccountInfoDoubleRequest {
  AccountInfoDoublePropertyType property_id = 1;
}

Reply message:

AccountInfoDoubleReply {
  oneof response {
    AccountInfoDoubleData data  = 1;   // { double requested_value = 1; }
    Error                 error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
⬆️ Output — AccountInfoDoubleData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description RequestedValue requested_value() double The value of the chosen property.

docs.title: 🧱 Property enum — AccountInfoDoublePropertyType
docs.text:
Values live at namespace scope: write pb::ACCOUNT_BALANCE.

Constant Value Meaning ACCOUNT_BALANCE 0 Account balance (excludes floating P/L). ACCOUNT_CREDIT 1 Credit amount. ACCOUNT_PROFIT 2 Current floating profit/loss of open positions. ACCOUNT_EQUITY 3 Equity = balance + floating P/L. ACCOUNT_MARGIN 4 Margin currently used. ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE 5 Free margin available for new positions. ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL 6 Margin level in percent (equity / margin × 100). ACCOUNT_MARGIN_SO_CALL 7 Margin Call level. ACCOUNT_MARGIN_SO_SO 8 Stop Out level. ACCOUNT_MARGIN_INITIAL 9 Reserved initial margin. ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MAINTENANCE 10 Reserved maintenance margin. ACCOUNT_ASSETS 11 Current assets. ACCOUNT_LIABILITIES 12 Current liabilities. ACCOUNT_COMMISSION_BLOCKED 13 Blocked commission.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Automatic reconnection: transient gRPC errors are retried and a dropped terminal session is re-attached inside MT5Account.
  • Default timeout: ClientOptions::unaryTimeoutMs (default 30000 ms).
  • Errors are exceptions: ApiError (server rejected) / TransportError (transport failed past retries).
  • One value only. If you need several numbers at once, accountSummary() is cheaper than many accountInfoDouble() calls.

docs.title: 1) Read the balance
docs.text:
pb::AccountInfoDoubleRequest r;
r.set_property_id(pb::ACCOUNT_BALANCE);
double balance = account.accountInfoDouble(r).requested_value();
std::printf("Balance: %.2f\n", balance);

docs.title: 2) A tiny helper that wraps the enum
docs.text:
double accDouble(MT5Account& a, pb::AccountInfoDoublePropertyType id) {
    pb::AccountInfoDoubleRequest r;
    r.set_property_id(id);
    return a.accountInfoDouble(r).requested_value();
}

double equity    = accDouble(account, pb::ACCOUNT_EQUITY);
double freeMargin = accDouble(account, pb::ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE);
double profit    = accDouble(account, pb::ACCOUNT_PROFIT);
std::printf("Eq %.2f | Free %.2f | P/L %.2f\n", equity, freeMargin, profit);

docs.title: 3) Margin-level guard before sizing a trade
docs.text:
double accDouble(MT5Account& a, pb::AccountInfoDoublePropertyType id);  // as above

bool safeToTrade(MT5Account& account) {
    double level = accDouble(account, pb::ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL);
    if (level == 0) return true;                 // no open margin yet
    if (level < 150) { std::puts("⚠️ margin level too low"); return false; }
    return true;
}

docs.title: 4) Error handling
docs.text:
try {
    double p = accDouble(account, pb::ACCOUNT_PROFIT);
    std::printf("Floating P/L: %.2f\n", p);
} catch (const ApiError& e) {
    std::printf("Server error: %s\n", e.what());
} catch (const TransportError& e) {
    std::printf("Transport error: %s\n", e.what());
}

docs.text:
• AccountSummary — all account values in one call (incl. the margin fields)
  • AccountInfoInteger — single integer property (login, leverage, …)
  • AccountInfoString — single string property (name, currency, …)
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::accountInfoDouble(int propertyId) takes the id as a plain int.

docs.title: ✅ Getting a Single Integer Account Property
docs.text:
Request: one integer account value (AccountInfoIntegerData) from MT5 — login, leverage, limit orders, trade flags — selected by a property enum.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::accountInfoInteger(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: AccountInfoInteger (defined in mt5-term-api-account-information.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: AccountInfoInteger(AccountInfoIntegerRequest) → AccountInfoIntegerReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC that returns a single int64 chosen by an AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType enum.
  • Why you need it. Read the login number, leverage, or a boolean-style flag (ACCOUNT_TRADE_ALLOWED) without the full summary.
  • Sanity check. ACCOUNT_LOGIN should equal the login you connected with.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Read leverage before computing required margin.
  • Check whether trading / Expert Advisors are allowed.
  • Detect the account trade mode (ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE: 0 = DEMO, 1 = CONTEST, 2 = REAL).

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns the single int64 value selected by req.property_id().
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::AccountInfoIntegerData accountInfoInteger(const pb::AccountInfoIntegerRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

AccountInfoIntegerRequest { AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType property_id = 1; }

AccountInfoIntegerReply {
  oneof response {
    AccountInfoIntegerData data  = 1;   // { int64 requested_value = 1; }
    Error                  error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description property_id set_property_id(pb::ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE) — AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType Which integer property to read.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — AccountInfoIntegerData
docs.text:
Field C++ accessor C++ type Description RequestedValue requested_value() int64_t The value of the chosen property.

Flag-style properties (ACCOUNT_TRADE_ALLOWED, ACCOUNT_TRADE_EXPERT, ACCOUNT_FIFO_CLOSE, ACCOUNT_HEDGE_ALLOWED) return 0 / 1. Enum-style properties (ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE, ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE) return the enum's integer value.

docs.title: 🧱 Property enum — AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType
docs.text: Constant Value Meaning ACCOUNT_LOGIN 0 Account login (ID). ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE 1 Account type: 0 = DEMO, 1 = CONTEST, 2 = REAL. ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE 2 Leverage (e.g. 100 = 1:100). ACCOUNT_LIMIT_ORDERS 3 Max number of pending orders allowed. ACCOUNT_MARGIN_SO_MODE 4 Mode for Stop Out level (percent vs money). ACCOUNT_TRADE_ALLOWED 5 Trading allowed for this account (0/1). ACCOUNT_TRADE_EXPERT 6 Automated (EA) trading allowed (0/1). ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE 7 Margin mode: 0 = NETTING, 1 = EXCHANGE, 2 = RETAIL_HEDGING. ACCOUNT_CURRENCY_DIGITS 8 Number of decimal digits for the account currency. ACCOUNT_FIFO_CLOSE 9 Positions must be closed FIFO (0/1). ACCOUNT_HEDGE_ALLOWED 10 Hedging (opposite positions on one symbol) allowed (0/1).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Automatic reconnection: handled inside MT5Account.
  • Default timeout: ClientOptions::unaryTimeoutMs (default 30000 ms).
  • Errors are exceptions: ApiError / TransportError.
  • Enums as int: when you query ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE the value is returned as int64 (0/1/2), not a typed enum — compare against the numeric values.

docs.title: 1) Read leverage
docs.text:
pb::AccountInfoIntegerRequest r;
r.set_property_id(pb::ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE);
int64_t leverage = account.accountInfoInteger(r).requested_value();
std::printf("Leverage: 1:%lld\n", (long long)leverage);

docs.title: 2) A helper + the trade-mode check
docs.text:
int64_t accInt(MT5Account& a, pb::AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType id) {
    pb::AccountInfoIntegerRequest r;
    r.set_property_id(id);
    return a.accountInfoInteger(r).requested_value();
}

int64_t mode = accInt(account, pb::ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE);
std::printf("Account is %s\n", mode == 0 ? "DEMO" : mode == 2 ? "REAL" : "CONTEST");

docs.title: 3) Guard: refuse to trade on a real account
docs.text:
int64_t accInt(MT5Account& a, pb::AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType id);  // as above

if (accInt(account, pb::ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE) == 2 /* REAL */) {
    throw std::runtime_error("Refusing to run a test strategy on a REAL account");
}
if (!accInt(account, pb::ACCOUNT_TRADE_ALLOWED)) {
    std::puts("Trading is disabled for this account");
}

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• AccountSummary — login, leverage, trade mode and more in one call
  • AccountInfoDouble — single double property (balance, margin, …)
  • AccountInfoString — single string property (name, currency, …)
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::accountInfoInteger(int propertyId) takes the id as a plain int.

docs.title: ✅ Getting a Single String Account Property
docs.text:
Request: one text account value (AccountInfoStringData) from MT5 — name, server, currency, company — selected by a property enum.

API Information:

docs.text:

docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC that returns a single string chosen by an AccountInfoStringPropertyType enum.
  • Why you need it. Read the account currency, broker name, or server string without the full summary.
  • Sanity check. ACCOUNT_CURRENCY should be a 3-letter code like "USD".

docs.text:
• Display the account's deposit currency (needed to format money and compute P/L).
  • Show the broker/company and server in a status line.
  • Label logs with the account name.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns the single string value selected by req.property_id().
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::AccountInfoStringData accountInfoString(const pb::AccountInfoStringRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

AccountInfoStringRequest { AccountInfoStringPropertyType property_id = 1; }

AccountInfoStringReply {
  oneof response {
    AccountInfoStringData data  = 1;   // { string requested_value = 1; }
    Error                 error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description property_id set_property_id(pb::ACCOUNT_CURRENCY) — AccountInfoStringPropertyType Which string property to read.

docs.title: 🧱 Property enum — AccountInfoStringPropertyType
docs.text: Constant Value Meaning ACCOUNT_NAME 0 Account holder name. ACCOUNT_SERVER 1 Trade server name (e.g. MetaQuotes-Demo). ACCOUNT_CURRENCY 2 Deposit currency (e.g. USD). ACCOUNT_COMPANY 3 Broker/company display name.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Automatic reconnection: handled inside MT5Account.
  • Default timeout: ClientOptions::unaryTimeoutMs (default 30000 ms).
  • Errors are exceptions: ApiError / TransportError.
  • Currency matters: always read ACCOUNT_CURRENCY before formatting money or computing tick value — profits are expressed in it.

docs.title: 1) Read the currency
docs.text:
pb::AccountInfoStringRequest r;
r.set_property_id(pb::ACCOUNT_CURRENCY);
std::string ccy = account.accountInfoString(r).requested_value();
std::printf("Currency: %s\n", ccy.c_str());

docs.title: 2) A helper + a full identity line
docs.text:
std::string accStr(MT5Account& a, pb::AccountInfoStringPropertyType id) {
    pb::AccountInfoStringRequest r;
    r.set_property_id(id);
    return a.accountInfoString(r).requested_value();
}

std::printf("%s @ %s (%s), currency %s\n",
            accStr(account, pb::ACCOUNT_NAME).c_str(),
            accStr(account, pb::ACCOUNT_SERVER).c_str(),
            accStr(account, pb::ACCOUNT_COMPANY).c_str(),
            accStr(account, pb::ACCOUNT_CURRENCY).c_str());

try {
    std::string server = accStr(account, pb::ACCOUNT_SERVER);
    std::printf("Server: %s\n", server.c_str());
} catch (const ApiError& e) {
    std::printf("Server error: %s\n", e.what());
} catch (const TransportError& e) {
    std::printf("Transport error: %s\n", e.what());
}
