docs.title: ✅ Getting an Account Summary
docs.text:
Request: full account summary (AccountSummaryData) from MT5. Fetch all core account metrics in a single call.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::accountSummary(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: AccountSummary (defined in mt5-term-api-account-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: AccountSummary(AccountSummaryRequest) → AccountSummaryReply
  • Low-level client (generated): AccountHelper::Stub::AccountSummary(context, request, response)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A single RPC returning full account state: balance, equity, credit, currency, leverage, trade mode, margin / free margin / margin level / margin mode, and server time.
  • Why you need it. Fast dashboard/CLI status; double-check login/currency/leverage; heartbeat via server_time().
  • Sanity check. If you see account_login(), account_currency(), account_leverage(), account_equity() → the connection is alive.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use it to display real-time account state and sanity-check connectivity:

  • Dashboard/CLI status in one call.
  • Verify balance & equity before trading.
  • Terminal heartbeat via server_time() / server_time_utc() and server_utc_offset_seconds().

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
namespace metarpc {

class MT5Account {
    // ...
public:
    // Retrieves full account information in a single call.
    // Returns AccountSummaryData with balance, equity, leverage, currency and
    // other account properties. Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
    pb::AccountSummaryData accountSummary(const pb::AccountSummaryRequest& req = {});
};

} // namespace metarpc

namespace pb = mt5_term_api; — the generated protobuf namespace.

Request message:

AccountSummaryRequest {} (empty message — just pass the default)

Reply message:

AccountSummaryReply {
  oneof response {
    AccountSummaryData data  = 1;
    Error              error = 2;
  }
}

MT5Account unwraps the oneof: it returns data on success and throws ApiError (carrying the server-side Error) otherwise.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
Parameter Type Description req const pb::AccountSummaryRequest& Empty request message. Optional — defaults to {}.

There is no ctx parameter. The per-call deadline comes from ClientOptions. Tune it on the account:

account.options().unaryTimeoutMs = 5000;   // deadline for ordinary read RPCs (default 30000)
account.options().maxRetries     = 5;       // transient-failure / reconnect retry budget

Each call runs on a background deadline; on UNAVAILABLE / DEADLINE_EXCEEDED it is retried with exponential back-off, and a dropped terminal session is re-attached automatically before the retry.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — AccountSummaryData
docs.text:
Field (proto) C++ accessor C++ type Description AccountLogin account_login() int64_t Trading account login (ID). AccountBalance account_balance() double Balance excluding floating P/L. AccountEquity account_equity() double Equity = balance + floating P/L. AccountUserName account_user_name() const std::string& Account holder name. AccountLeverage account_leverage() int64_t Leverage (e.g., 100 for 1:100). AccountTradeMode account_trade_mode() MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode See enum below. AccountCompanyName account_company_name() const std::string& Broker/company display name. AccountCurrency account_currency() const std::string& Deposit currency (e.g., "USD"). ServerTime server_time() google::protobuf::Timestamp Server time at response, in the broker's time zone. ServerTimeUtc server_time_utc() google::protobuf::Timestamp The same moment as server_time(), in UTC. UtcTimezoneServerTimeShiftMinutes utc_timezone_server_time_shift_minutes() int64_t Server offset relative to UTC (minutes). AccountCredit account_credit() double Credit amount. ServerUtcOffsetSeconds server_utc_offset_seconds() int32_t Broker server's offset from UTC in seconds (positive = ahead of UTC); 0 while not connected yet. AccountMargin account_margin() double Margin currently used by open positions. AccountMarginFree account_margin_free() double Free margin available for new positions. AccountMarginLevel account_margin_level() double Margin level in percent (equity / margin × 100); 0 when no margin is used. AccountMarginMode account_margin_mode() MrpcEnumAccountMarginMode Margin mode (MT5 demo = RETAIL_HEDGING). AccountTradeAllowed account_trade_allowed() bool Trading allowed for this account. AccountTradeExpert account_trade_expert() bool Automated (Expert Advisor) trading allowed. TerminalConnected terminal_connected() bool Terminal is connected to the broker. TerminalTradeAllowed terminal_trade_allowed() bool Trading is allowed in the terminal.

C++ protobuf accessors are snake_case and return the value by reference for strings/messages, by value for scalars.

docs.title: 🧱 Related enums (from proto)
docs.text: 💡 Enum Usage Note: in C++ the generated enum values live at namespace scope (they are not enum class), so you write pb::MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO, not a prefixed form.

docs.title: MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode
docs.text:
Defined in mt5-term-api-account-helper.proto:

enum MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode {
  MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO    = 0;  // demo/practice
  MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_CONTEST = 1;  // contest
  MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL    = 2;  // real trading
}

Helper to convert the enum to a string:

const char* tradeModeToString(pb::MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode m) {
    switch (m) {
        case pb::MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO:    return "DEMO";
        case pb::MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_CONTEST: return "CONTEST";
        case pb::MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL:    return "REAL";
        default:                                  return "UNKNOWN";
    }
}

docs.title: MrpcEnumAccountMarginMode
docs.text:
enum MrpcEnumAccountMarginMode {
  MRPC_ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_NETTING = 0;  // netting (one position per symbol)
  MRPC_ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_EXCHANGE       = 1;  // exchange margin
  MRPC_ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_HEDGING = 2;  // hedging (multiple positions per symbol) — typical MT5
}

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Automatic reconnection: every MT5Account method runs through an internal call<> wrapper that retries transient gRPC errors and re-attaches a dropped terminal session (TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND) before retrying.
  • Default timeout: read RPCs use ClientOptions::unaryTimeoutMs (default 30000 ms).
  • Errors are exceptions: a server-side rejection throws metarpc::ApiError; a transport failure past the retry budget throws metarpc::TransportError. There are no error return values.
  • Timestamps: server_time() / server_time_utc() are google.protobuf.Timestamp; read .seconds() for epoch seconds, or use the friendly MT5Service::accountSummary() which returns UTC fields already converted.

docs.title: 1) Basic usage
docs.text:
#include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>
#include <cstdio>
using namespace metarpc;
namespace pb = mt5_term_api;

int main() {
    MT5Account account("mt5.mrpc.pro", 443);
    account.connect(5057947437, "password", "MetaQuotes-Demo");

    pb::AccountSummaryData s = account.accountSummary();

    std::printf("Account Login: %lld\n", (long long)s.account_login());
    std::printf("Balance: %.2f %s\n", s.account_balance(), s.account_currency().c_str());
    std::printf("Equity: %.2f\n", s.account_equity());
    std::printf("Leverage: 1:%lld\n", (long long)s.account_leverage());
    return 0;
}

docs.title: 2) Compact status line for a CLI
docs.text:
void printAccountStatus(MT5Account& account) {
    try {
        pb::AccountSummaryData s = account.accountSummary();
        std::printf("Acc %lld | %s | Bal %.2f | Eq %.2f | Lev 1:%lld | Mode %s\n",
                    (long long)s.account_login(),
                    s.account_currency().c_str(),
                    s.account_balance(),
                    s.account_equity(),
                    (long long)s.account_leverage(),
                    tradeModeToString(s.account_trade_mode()));
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        std::printf("❌ Error: %s\n", e.what());
    }
}
// Output: Acc 5057947437 | USD | Bal 99806.00 | Eq 99850.25 | Lev 1:100 | Mode DEMO

docs.title: 3) Server time with timezone shift
docs.text:
#include <ctime>

void printServerTime(MT5Account& account) {
    pb::AccountSummaryData s = account.accountSummary();

    std::time_t utc    = (std::time_t)s.server_time_utc().seconds();
    std::time_t broker = (std::time_t)s.server_time().seconds();

    char buf[32];
    std::strftime(buf, sizeof buf, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", std::gmtime(&utc));
    std::printf("Server time (UTC): %s\n", buf);
    std::strftime(buf, sizeof buf, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", std::gmtime(&broker));
    std::printf("Server time (broker): %s\n", buf);
    std::printf("Broker offset from UTC: %+d seconds\n", s.server_utc_offset_seconds());
}

docs.title: 4) Tightening the deadline for one account
docs.text:
MT5Account account("mt5.mrpc.pro", 443);
account.options().unaryTimeoutMs = 2000;   // fail fast after 2 s
account.connect(5057947437, "password", "MetaQuotes-Demo");

try {
    pb::AccountSummaryData s = account.accountSummary();
    std::printf("Balance: %.2f\n", s.account_balance());
} catch (const TransportError& e) {
    std::printf("Timed out / transport error: %s\n", e.what());
}

docs.title: 5) Structured data model
docs.text:
// A clean plain struct for UI / business logic
struct AccountSummaryView {
    int64_t      login;
    std::string  currency;
    double       balance;
    double       equity;
    int64_t      leverage;
    std::string  tradeMode;
    std::string  company;
};

AccountSummaryView fromProto(const pb::AccountSummaryData& d) {
    return AccountSummaryView{
        d.account_login(),
        d.account_currency(),
        d.account_balance(),
        d.account_equity(),
        d.account_leverage(),
        tradeModeToString(d.account_trade_mode()),
        d.account_company_name(),
    };
}

// Usage:
AccountSummaryView v = fromProto(account.accountSummary());
std::printf("%lld %s %.2f\n", (long long)v.login, v.currency.c_str(), v.balance);

docs.title: 6) Error handling (reconnect is automatic)
docs.text:
bool tryGetSummary(MT5Account& account, pb::AccountSummaryData& out) {
    try {
        out = account.accountSummary();   // transient errors already retried inside
        return true;
    } catch (const ApiError& e) {
        std::printf("Server rejected the request: %s\n", e.what());
    } catch (const TransportError& e) {
        std::printf("Transport failed after retries: %s\n", e.what());
    }
    return false;
}

docs.title: Health check
docs.text:
bool isAccountHealthy(MT5Account& account) {
    try {
        pb::AccountSummaryData s = account.accountSummary();
        return s.account_login() > 0 &&
               !s.account_currency().empty() &&
               s.account_leverage() > 0;
    } catch (...) {
        return false;
    }
}

docs.title: Monitor account changes
docs.text:
#include <thread>
#include <chrono>

void monitorAccount(MT5Account& account, std::chrono::seconds interval) {
    for (;;) {
        try {
            pb::AccountSummaryData s = account.accountSummary();
            std::printf("Balance: %.2f | Equity: %.2f\n",
                        s.account_balance(), s.account_equity());
        } catch (const std::exception& e) {
            std::printf("❌ Error: %s\n", e.what());
        }
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(interval);
    }
}
// Usage: monitorAccount(account, std::chrono::seconds(5));

docs.title: MT5Account · Account Information — Overview
docs.text: Account balance, equity, margin, leverage, currency, and other account properties. Use this page to choose the right API for accessing account state.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• AccountSummary — all account info at once (login, balance, equity, credit, leverage, currency, margin / free margin / margin level, server time, etc.; no floating profit). Returns MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode and MrpcEnumAccountMarginMode enums.
  • AccountInfoDouble — single double value from the account (balance, equity, margin, profit, credit, etc.). Uses the AccountInfoDoublePropertyType enum as input.
  • AccountInfoInteger — single integer value (login, leverage, limit orders, trade flags, etc.). Uses the AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType enum as input.
  • AccountInfoString — single string value (name, server, currency, company). Uses the AccountInfoStringPropertyType enum as input.

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English
docs.text:
• AccountSummary → the one-stop shop for a complete account snapshot (balance, equity, leverage, currency, etc.). Returns trade mode as an enum.
  • AccountInfoDouble → grab one numeric property when you need just balance or margin. Requires a property enum as input.
  • AccountInfoInteger → grab one integer property like login number or leverage. Requires a property enum as input.
  • AccountInfoString → grab one text property like account name or currency. Requires a property enum as input.

Rule of thumb: need the full snapshot → accountSummary(); need one specific value → accountInfo* (Double/Integer/String).

🧱 Enum note: all 4 methods use enums. accountInfo* require a property enum as input to select which value to read; accountSummary() returns the account trade mode (DEMO/CONTEST/REAL) and margin mode as output enums.

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Returns Enums used Complete account snapshot (all values) accountSummary AccountSummaryData Output: MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode, MrpcEnumAccountMarginMode One numeric value (balance, equity, margin, etc.) accountInfoDouble single double Input: AccountInfoDoublePropertyType One integer value (login, leverage, etc.) accountInfoInteger single int64_t Input: AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType One text value (name, currency, server, etc.) accountInfoString single std::string Input: AccountInfoStringPropertyType

docs.title: ❌ Cross-refs & gotchas
docs.text:
• Margin — accountSummary() already returns account_margin(), account_margin_free() and account_margin_level() (and account_margin_mode()); accountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL / ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE) is just the single-value alternative.
  • Floating profit — accountSummary() carries balance, equity, leverage and the margin fields; the one thing it does not carry is floating profit — use accountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_PROFIT) for that.
  • accountInfo* methods are lighter if you only need one property.
  • Currency affects how profits are calculated — always check ACCOUNT_CURRENCY.
  • Leverage determines margin requirements — higher leverage = less margin needed.
  • Timeout — read RPCs use ClientOptions::unaryTimeoutMs (default 30000 ms); tune with account.options().

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippets
docs.text:
// Complete account snapshot
pb::AccountSummaryData s = account.accountSummary();
std::printf("Balance: %.2f, Equity: %.2f, Leverage: 1:%lld\n",
            s.account_balance(), s.account_equity(), (long long)s.account_leverage());

// Single property — account balance
pb::AccountInfoDoubleRequest rd;
rd.set_property_id(pb::ACCOUNT_BALANCE);
std::printf("Balance: %.2f\n", account.accountInfoDouble(rd).requested_value());

// Account leverage
pb::AccountInfoIntegerRequest ri;
ri.set_property_id(pb::ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE);
std::printf("Leverage: 1:%lld\n", (long long)account.accountInfoInteger(ri).requested_value());

// Account currency
pb::AccountInfoStringRequest rs;
rs.set_property_id(pb::ACCOUNT_CURRENCY);
std::printf("Currency: %s\n", account.accountInfoString(rs).requested_value().c_str());

// Account health — accountSummary already carries the margin level
pb::AccountSummaryData h = account.accountSummary();
double level = h.account_margin_level();          // also: account_margin(), account_margin_free()
if (level != 0 && level < 100)      std::puts("⚠️ Margin level critical!");
else if (level != 0 && level < 200) std::puts("⚠️ Low margin level");
else                                std::puts("✅ Healthy margin level");

docs.title: Input enums (property selectors)
Output enums (return values)
📝 Important notes about enums
docs.text:
• Input enums are required — you must specify which property to read.
  • Namespace-scope values — in C++ the generated values are not enum class; write pb::ACCOUNT_BALANCE, pb::MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO.
  • Output enums — accountSummary() returns account_trade_mode() / account_margin_mode() as typed enum fields.
  • accountInfoInteger special case — some integer properties represent enums (e.g. ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE) but are returned as plain int64 (0/1/2).

docs.title: ✅ Checking Whether a Symbol Exists
docs.text:
Request: does a symbol exist on the server (SymbolExistData), and is it custom?

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbolExist(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolExist (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolExist(SymbolExistRequest) → SymbolExistReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Tells you whether a symbol name is valid on the server, and whether it is a custom (synthetic) symbol.
  • Why you need it. Validate user input before selecting/quoting/trading a symbol.
  • Sanity check. symbolExist("EURUSD").exists() is true.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns existence/custom flags for req.name(). Throws ApiError / TransportError.
pb::SymbolExistData symbolExist(const pb::SymbolExistRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

SymbolExistRequest { string name = 1; }

SymbolExistReply {
  oneof response {
    SymbolExistData data  = 1;   // { bool exists = 1; bool is_custom = 2; }
    Error           error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
Field C++ setter / type Description name set_name("EURUSD") — string The symbol name to check.

Note: this request uses name, not symbol.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolExistData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description Exists exists() bool true if the symbol exists on the server. IsCustom is_custom() bool true if it is a custom/synthetic symbol.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Existence ≠ selected. A symbol can exist on the server but not be in Market Watch — use SymbolSelect to quote it.
  • Cheap guard. Call this before building a request with user-supplied symbols to turn a server error into a clean boolean.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 1) Validate before trading
docs.text:
pb::SymbolExistRequest r; r.set_name("EURUSD");
pb::SymbolExistData d = account.symbolExist(r);
if (!d.exists()) { std::puts("Unknown symbol"); return; }
std::printf("EURUSD exists (custom: %s)\n", d.is_custom() ? "yes" : "no");

docs.title: 2) A boolean helper
docs.text:
bool symbolExists(MT5Account& a, const std::string& name) {
    pb::SymbolExistRequest r; r.set_name(name);
    return a.symbolExist(r).exists();
}

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• SymbolSelect — add an existing symbol to Market Watch
  • SymbolList — list all valid names
  • SymbolIsSynchronized — check the symbol's data is ready

docs.title: ✅ Getting a Single Double Symbol Property
docs.text:
Request: one floating-point symbol property (SymbolInfoDoubleData) from MT5 — bid, ask, point, tick value, volume limits, swaps, etc. — selected by a property enum.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbolInfoDouble(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolInfoDouble (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolInfoDouble(SymbolInfoDoubleRequest) → SymbolInfoDoubleReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC that returns a single double property of a symbol, chosen by a SymbolInfoDoubleProperty enum.
  • Why you need it. The constants that turn a raw price into money: SYMBOL_POINT, SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_VALUE, SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE, SYMBOL_VOLUME_MIN/MAX/STEP.
  • Sanity check. SYMBOL_BID should match symbolInfoTick().bid().

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Read SYMBOL_POINT and SYMBOL_DIGITS to format/round prices correctly.
  • Read SYMBOL_VOLUME_MIN / MAX / STEP to validate and normalize lot sizes.
  • Read SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_VALUE + SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE for P/L and risk math.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns the single double property selected by req.type() for req.symbol().
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::SymbolInfoDoubleData symbolInfoDouble(const pb::SymbolInfoDoubleRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

SymbolInfoDoubleRequest {
  string                   symbol = 1;
  SymbolInfoDoubleProperty type   = 2;
}

SymbolInfoDoubleReply {
  oneof response {
    SymbolInfoDoubleData data  = 1;   // { double value = 1; }
    Error                error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
⬆️ Output — SymbolInfoDoubleData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description Value value() double The value of the chosen property.

docs.title: 🧱 Property enum — SymbolInfoDoubleProperty (common values)
docs.text:
60 values total (SYMBOL_BID … SYMBOL_COUNT); the most used:

Constant Value Meaning SYMBOL_BID 0 Current best bid. SYMBOL_ASK 3 Current best ask. SYMBOL_LAST 6 Last deal price. SYMBOL_POINT 13 Point size (smallest price step). SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_VALUE 14 Value of one tick in the account currency. SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE 17 Minimal price change (tick size). SYMBOL_TRADE_CONTRACT_SIZE 18 Contract size (units per lot). SYMBOL_VOLUME_MIN 22 Minimum volume (lots). SYMBOL_VOLUME_MAX 23 Maximum volume (lots). SYMBOL_VOLUME_STEP 24 Volume step (lot increment). SYMBOL_VOLUME_LIMIT 25 Max total volume per symbol. SYMBOL_SWAP_LONG 26 Swap charged on long positions. SYMBOL_SWAP_SHORT 27 Swap charged on short positions. SYMBOL_MARGIN_INITIAL 35 Initial margin per lot.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Point vs tick size. For most FX symbols SYMBOL_POINT equals SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE, but not always — use the right one for your math.
  • Money per point ≈ SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_VALUE × (SYMBOL_POINT / SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE).
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.
  • Batch alternative. Need many fields for many symbols at once? Use SymbolParamsMany.

docs.title: 1) Point and digits-driven formatting
docs.text:
double sd(MT5Account& a, const std::string& s, pb::SymbolInfoDoubleProperty p) {
    pb::SymbolInfoDoubleRequest r; r.set_symbol(s); r.set_type(p);
    return a.symbolInfoDouble(r).value();
}

double point = sd(account, "EURUSD", pb::SYMBOL_POINT);
std::printf("Point size: %.5f\n", point);

docs.title: 2) Validate a lot size against min/max/step
docs.text:
double vmin = sd(account, "EURUSD", pb::SYMBOL_VOLUME_MIN);
double vmax = sd(account, "EURUSD", pb::SYMBOL_VOLUME_MAX);
double step = sd(account, "EURUSD", pb::SYMBOL_VOLUME_STEP);

double wanted = 0.037;
double norm = std::round(wanted / step) * step;          // snap to step
norm = std::max(vmin, std::min(vmax, norm));             // clamp
std::printf("Normalized volume: %.2f (min %.2f / step %.2f)\n", norm, vmin, step);

docs.title: 3) Spread in points
docs.text:
double bid = sd(account, "EURUSD", pb::SYMBOL_BID);
double ask = sd(account, "EURUSD", pb::SYMBOL_ASK);
double point = sd(account, "EURUSD", pb::SYMBOL_POINT);
std::printf("Spread: %.1f points\n", (ask - bid) / point);

docs.title: ✅ Getting a Single Integer Symbol Property
docs.text:
Request: one integer symbol property (SymbolInfoIntegerData) from MT5 — digits, spread, trade mode, session times, flags — selected by a property enum.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbolInfoInteger(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolInfoInteger (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolInfoInteger(SymbolInfoIntegerRequest) → SymbolInfoIntegerReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC that returns a single int64 property of a symbol, chosen by a SymbolInfoIntegerProperty enum.
  • Why you need it. SYMBOL_DIGITS and SYMBOL_SPREAD for formatting; SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE to know whether trading is allowed; time fields for sessions.
  • Sanity check. SYMBOL_DIGITS for EURUSD is usually 5.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Read SYMBOL_DIGITS to round prices and SYMBOL_SPREAD (in points).
  • Check SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE before trying to trade a symbol.
  • Read SYMBOL_TIME (last quote time) for staleness checks.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:

// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::SymbolInfoIntegerData symbolInfoInteger(const pb::SymbolInfoIntegerRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

SymbolInfoIntegerRequest {
  string                    symbol = 1;
  SymbolInfoIntegerProperty type   = 2;
}

SymbolInfoIntegerReply {
  oneof response {
    SymbolInfoIntegerData data  = 1;   // { int64 value = 1; int64 value_utc = 2; }
    Error                 error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description symbol set_symbol("EURUSD") — string The symbol. type set_type(pb::SYMBOL_DIGITS) — SymbolInfoIntegerProperty Which integer property to read.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolInfoIntegerData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description Value value() int64_t The value of the chosen property (broker time zone for time-based ones). ValueUtc value_utc() int64_t For time-based properties (SYMBOL_TIME, SYMBOL_START_TIME, …), the same moment in UTC. 0 for non-time properties.

docs.title: 🧱 Property enum — SymbolInfoIntegerProperty (common values)
docs.text: Constant Value Meaning SYMBOL_EXIST 6 Symbol exists (0/1). SYMBOL_SELECT 7 Symbol is selected in Market Watch (0/1). SYMBOL_VISIBLE 8 Symbol is visible in Market Watch (0/1). SYMBOL_TIME 15 Time of the last quote (epoch seconds). SYMBOL_DIGITS 17 Decimal digits in the price. SYMBOL_SPREAD_FLOAT 18 Spread is floating (0/1). SYMBOL_SPREAD 19 Current spread in points. SYMBOL_TRADE_CALC_MODE 21 Contract price calculation mode. SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE 22 Order execution permissions for the symbol. SYMBOL_START_TIME 23 Trading start date (epoch seconds; 0 if none). SYMBOL_EXPIRATION_TIME 24 Trading end date (epoch seconds; 0 if none). SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL 25 Min distance (points) for SL/TP from price. SYMBOL_TRADE_FREEZE_LEVEL 26 Freeze distance (points) for orders. SYMBOL_FILLING_MODE 32 Allowed order filling modes (bit flags).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Time fields: for SYMBOL_TIME / SYMBOL_START_TIME / SYMBOL_EXPIRATION_TIME use value_utc() to avoid broker-timezone confusion.
  • Flags are int. Properties like SYMBOL_SELECT / SYMBOL_VISIBLE return 0/1.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 1) Digits & spread
docs.text:
int64_t si(MT5Account& a, const std::string& s, pb::SymbolInfoIntegerProperty p) {
    pb::SymbolInfoIntegerRequest r; r.set_symbol(s); r.set_type(p);
    return a.symbolInfoInteger(r).value();
}

std::printf("EURUSD digits=%lld spread=%lld points\n",
            (long long)si(account, "EURUSD", pb::SYMBOL_DIGITS),

docs.title: 2) Is the symbol tradable right now?

// 0 = disabled; non-zero = some form of trading allowed (long/short/close-only…)

docs.title: 3) Last quote time (UTC) for a staleness check

#include <ctime>
pb::SymbolInfoIntegerRequest r; r.set_symbol("EURUSD"); r.set_type(pb::SYMBOL_TIME);
pb::SymbolInfoIntegerData d = account.symbolInfoInteger(r);
std::time_t utc = (std::time_t)d.value_utc();
char buf[32]; std::strftime(buf, sizeof buf, "%F %T", std::gmtime(&utc));
std::printf("Last quote (UTC): %s\n", buf);

docs.text:

// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.

Request / Reply:

SymbolInfoStringRequest {

}

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolInfoStringData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description Value value() const std::string& The value of the chosen property.

docs.title: 🧱 Property enum — SymbolInfoStringProperty
docs.text: Constant Value Meaning SYMBOL_BASIS 0 Underlying asset of a derivative. SYMBOL_CATEGORY 1 Symbol category. SYMBOL_COUNTRY 2 Country of the issuer. SYMBOL_SECTOR_NAME 3 Economic sector name. SYMBOL_INDUSTRY_NAME 4 Industry/branch name. SYMBOL_CURRENCY_BASE 5 Base currency. SYMBOL_CURRENCY_PROFIT 6 Profit currency (P/L is denominated in it). SYMBOL_CURRENCY_MARGIN 7 Margin currency. SYMBOL_BANK 8 Quote source / bank. SYMBOL_DESCRIPTION 9 Human-readable description. SYMBOL_EXCHANGE 10 Exchange the symbol is traded on. SYMBOL_FORMULA 11 Formula for a custom/synthetic symbol. SYMBOL_ISIN 12 ISIN code. SYMBOL_PAGE 13 Web page with symbol info. SYMBOL_PATH 14 Path in the Market Watch tree.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Currencies matter. SYMBOL_CURRENCY_PROFIT tells you the currency of your floating P/L; if it differs from the account currency, a conversion is applied by the server.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 1) Description + currencies
docs.text:
std::string ss(MT5Account& a, const std::string& s, pb::SymbolInfoStringProperty p) {
    pb::SymbolInfoStringRequest r; r.set_symbol(s); r.set_type(p);
    return a.symbolInfoString(r).value();
}

std::printf("%s — base %s / profit %s / margin %s\n",
            ss(account, "EURUSD", pb::SYMBOL_DESCRIPTION).c_str(),
            ss(account, "EURUSD", pb::SYMBOL_CURRENCY_BASE).c_str(),
            ss(account, "EURUSD", pb::SYMBOL_CURRENCY_PROFIT).c_str(),
            ss(account, "EURUSD", pb::SYMBOL_CURRENCY_MARGIN).c_str());

docs.title: 2) Group symbols by path
docs.text:
std::string path = ss(account, "EURUSD", pb::SYMBOL_PATH);   // e.g. "Forex\\Majors\\EURUSD"
std::printf("Market Watch path: %s\n", path.c_str());

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• SymbolInfoDouble — point, tick value, volume limits
  • SymbolInfoInteger — digits, spread, trade mode
  • SymbolInfoTick — the full current tick in one call
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::symbolParams("EURUSD") returns description, currencyBase, currencyProfit, … already named.

docs.title: ✅ Getting the Current Tick (Quote)
docs.text:
Request: the latest quote for a symbol (MrpcMqlTick) from MT5 — bid, ask, last, volume and timestamps in one call.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbolInfoTick(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolInfoTick (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolInfoTick(SymbolInfoTickRequest) → SymbolInfoTickRequestReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A single RPC returning the most recent tick for one symbol.
  • Why you need it. Current price before placing a trade; spread; a lightweight price feed via polling.
  • Sanity check. bid() and ask() are > 0 and ask() >= bid().

Note. symbolInfoTick() returns the tick payload directly (pb::MrpcMqlTick), not a *Data wrapper.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Read the live bid/ask to decide entry price and compute spread (ask - bid).
  • Timestamp a quote (time() broker tz, time_utc() UTC; time_msc* in milliseconds).
  • Build a simple price poller (for push updates use OnSymbolTick instead).

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns the latest tick for req.symbol(). Throws ApiError / TransportError.
pb::MrpcMqlTick symbolInfoTick(const pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

SymbolInfoTickRequest { string symbol = 1; }

SymbolInfoTickRequestReply {
  oneof response {
    MrpcMqlTick data  = 1;
    Error       error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
⬆️ Output — MrpcMqlTick
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description Bid bid() double Best bid (price to sell at). Ask ask() double Best ask (price to buy at). Last last() double Last deal price (for exchange instruments). Volume volume() uint64_t Volume for the last deal (integer). VolumeReal volume_real() double Volume with greater precision. Time time() int64_t Tick time (epoch seconds), broker server time zone. TimeUtc time_utc() int64_t Tick time (epoch seconds), UTC. TimeMsc time_msc() int64_t Tick time in milliseconds, broker time zone. TimeMscUtc time_msc_utc() int64_t Tick time in milliseconds, UTC. Flags flags() uint32_t Tick change flags (bid/ask/last/volume changed, etc.).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Symbol must be selected. If a symbol is not in Market Watch, call SymbolSelect first (or the quote may be stale/empty).
  • Spread = ask() - bid(); in points, divide by the symbol's SYMBOL_POINT (SymbolInfoDouble).
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method (ApiError / TransportError, ClientOptions::unaryTimeoutMs).
  • Streaming alternative. For continuous updates don't poll in a tight loop — subscribe with OnSymbolTick.

docs.title: 1) Bid / ask / spread
docs.text:
pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest r;
r.set_symbol("EURUSD");
pb::MrpcMqlTick t = account.symbolInfoTick(r);

std::printf("Bid %.5f  Ask %.5f  Spread %.5f\n",
            t.bid(), t.ask(), t.ask() - t.bid());

docs.title: 2) A helper that returns just the mid price
docs.text:
double midPrice(MT5Account& a, const std::string& symbol) {
    pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest r;
    r.set_symbol(symbol);
    pb::MrpcMqlTick t = a.symbolInfoTick(r);
    return (t.bid() + t.ask()) / 2.0;
}

docs.title: 3) Timestamped quote (UTC)
docs.text:
#include <ctime>

pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest r; r.set_symbol("XAUUSD");
pb::MrpcMqlTick t = account.symbolInfoTick(r);

std::time_t utc = (std::time_t)t.time_utc();
char buf[32]; std::strftime(buf, sizeof buf, "%F %T", std::gmtime(&utc));
std::printf("[%s UTC] XAUUSD bid=%.2f ask=%.2f\n", buf, t.bid(), t.ask());

docs.title: 4) Error handling
docs.text:
try {
    pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest r; r.set_symbol("EURUSD");
    pb::MrpcMqlTick t = account.symbolInfoTick(r);
    std::printf("EURUSD %.5f / %.5f\n", t.bid(), t.ask());
} catch (const ApiError& e) {
    std::printf("Server error (symbol unknown?): %s\n", e.what());
} catch (const TransportError& e) {
    std::printf("Transport error: %s\n", e.what());
}

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• SymbolInfoDouble — point size, tick value, volume limits (needed to interpret the price)
  • SymbolSelect — make sure the symbol is in Market Watch first
  • OnSymbolTick — push-based live tick stream
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::tick("EURUSD") returns a named Tick struct with UTC time.

docs.title: ✅ Checking Symbol Data Synchronization
docs.text:
Request: is a symbol's data synchronized with the server (SymbolIsSynchronizedData)?

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbolIsSynchronized(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolIsSynchronized (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolIsSynchronized(SymbolIsSynchronizedRequest) → SymbolIsSynchronizedReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Tells you whether the terminal has finished synchronizing a symbol's specification and quotes with the server.
  • Why you need it. Right after selecting a fresh symbol, its parameters/quotes may not be ready yet — this confirms they are.
  • Sanity check. After SymbolSelect + a short wait, synchronized() becomes true.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns whether req.symbol()'s data is synchronized. Throws ApiError / TransportError.
pb::SymbolIsSynchronizedData symbolIsSynchronized(const pb::SymbolIsSynchronizedRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

SymbolIsSynchronizedRequest { string symbol = 1; }

SymbolIsSynchronizedReply {
  oneof response {
    SymbolIsSynchronizedData data  = 1;   // { bool synchronized = 1; }
    Error                    error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description symbol set_symbol("EURUSD") — string The symbol to check.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolIsSynchronizedData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description Synchronized synchronized() bool true if the symbol's data is ready.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Use after selecting a new symbol. Freshly selected symbols may need a moment to synchronize before their SymbolInfoDouble parameters are valid.
  • Poll gently. If false, wait a short interval and check again rather than spinning.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 1) Wait until a symbol is ready
docs.text:
#include <thread>
#include <chrono>

bool waitSynced(MT5Account& a, const std::string& symbol, int tries = 10) {
    for (int i = 0; i < tries; ++i) {
        pb::SymbolIsSynchronizedRequest r; r.set_symbol(symbol);
        if (a.symbolIsSynchronized(r).synchronized()) return true;
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(200));
    }
    return false;
}

// Usage: select, then wait before reading parameters
pb::SymbolSelectRequest sel; sel.set_symbol("USDMXN"); sel.set_select(true);
account.symbolSelect(sel);
if (waitSynced(account, "USDMXN"))
    std::puts("USDMXN ready");

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• SymbolSelect — select the symbol first
  • SymbolInfoDouble — read parameters once synchronized
  • SymbolExist — confirm the symbol exists at all

docs.title: ✅ Listing All Symbol Names
docs.text:
Request: every symbol name in one call (SymbolListData) — no index loop needed.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbolList(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolList (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolList(SymbolListRequest) → SymbolListReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Returns a repeated list of symbol names in a single response.
  • Why you need it. The convenient alternative to SymbolsTotal + SymbolName in a loop.
  • Sanity check. symbols_size() > 0.

This is a CppMT5 convenience RPC — it rolls the count-then-index pattern into one call.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns the list of symbol names. Request defaults to {}.
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::SymbolListData symbolList(const pb::SymbolListRequest& req = {});

Request / Reply:

SymbolListRequest {}   // (empty)

SymbolListReply {
  oneof response {
    SymbolListData data  = 1;   // { repeated string symbols = 1; }
    Error          error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description req const pb::SymbolListRequest& Empty request. Optional — defaults to {}.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolListData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description Symbols symbols() / symbols(i) / symbols_size() repeated string All symbol names.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Iterate with a range-for: for (const auto& s : data.symbols()) { ... }.
  • Cheaper than the loop: one round-trip instead of 1 + total calls.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 1) Print all symbols
docs.text:
pb::SymbolListData d = account.symbolList();
std::printf("%d symbols:\n", d.symbols_size());
for (const auto& name : d.symbols())
    std::printf("  %s\n", name.c_str());

docs.title: 2) Filter to a prefix
docs.text:
pb::SymbolListData d = account.symbolList();
for (const auto& name : d.symbols())
    if (name.rfind("EUR", 0) == 0)      // starts with "EUR"
        std::printf("%s\n", name.c_str());

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• SymbolsTotal / SymbolName — the index-based alternative
  • SymbolSelect — add/remove a symbol from Market Watch
  • SymbolExist — check one symbol without listing everything

docs.title: ✅ Getting a Symbol Name by Index
docs.text:
Request: the name of the symbol at a given index (SymbolNameData), from the full list or the Market Watch list.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbolName(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolName (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolName(SymbolNameRequest) → SymbolNameReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Resolves an index to a symbol name.
  • Why you need it. To enumerate symbols together with SymbolsTotal.
  • Sanity check. index = 0 returns a valid, non-empty name.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns the symbol name at req.index(). Throws ApiError / TransportError.
pb::SymbolNameData symbolName(const pb::SymbolNameRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

SymbolNameRequest {
  int32 index    = 1;
  bool  selected = 2;   // true = index into Market Watch; false = index into the full list
}

SymbolNameReply {
  oneof response {
    SymbolNameData data  = 1;   // { string name = 1; }
    Error          error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
Field C++ setter / type Description index set_index(int32) — int32 Zero-based index into the chosen list. selected set_selected(bool) — bool true → index into the Market Watch (selected) list; false → index into the full server list.

Keep selected consistent with the mode you passed to SymbolsTotal, or your index bounds won't match.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolNameData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description Name name() const std::string& Symbol name at the index.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Bounds: valid indices are 0 … total-1 for the matching list; out-of-range indices throw ApiError.
  • Prefer SymbolList when you want every name — it avoids a call per index.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 1) First symbol
docs.text:
pb::SymbolNameRequest r; r.set_index(0); r.set_selected(true);
std::printf("First MW symbol: %s\n", account.symbolName(r).name().c_str());

docs.title: 2) Enumerate the Market Watch list
docs.text:
pb::SymbolsTotalRequest tr; tr.set_mode(true);
int32_t n = account.symbolsTotal(tr).total();
for (int32_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    pb::SymbolNameRequest nr; nr.set_index(i); nr.set_selected(true);
    std::printf("%2d: %s\n", i, account.symbolName(nr).name().c_str());
}

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• SymbolsTotal — how many symbols there are to index
  • SymbolList — all names at once
  • SymbolSelect — add a symbol to Market Watch so it appears in the selected list

docs.title: ✅ Selecting a Symbol in Market Watch
docs.text:
Request: add a symbol to, or remove it from, Market Watch (SymbolSelectData).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbolSelect(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolSelect (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolSelect(SymbolSelectRequest) → SymbolSelectReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Enables (or disables) a symbol in Market Watch.
  • Why you need it. Quotes, ticks and DOM only flow for selected symbols — select before you quote or trade an unusual symbol.
  • Sanity check. success() is true.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Make a symbol quotable before SymbolInfoTick / OnSymbolTick.
  • Clean up Market Watch by removing symbols you no longer track.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Adds (select=true) or removes (select=false) req.symbol() from Market Watch.
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::SymbolSelectData symbolSelect(const pb::SymbolSelectRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

SymbolSelectRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
  bool   select = 2;   // true = add to Market Watch; false = remove
}

SymbolSelectReply {
  oneof response {
    SymbolSelectData data  = 1;   // { bool success = 1; }
    Error            error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description symbol set_symbol("GBPJPY") — string The symbol to add/remove. select set_select(bool) — bool true = add to Market Watch; false = remove.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolSelectData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description Success success() bool true if the operation succeeded.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• A symbol in use cannot be removed. Removing a symbol that has open positions or orders will fail.
  • Select is idempotent. Selecting an already-selected symbol just returns success.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 1) Ensure a symbol is quotable
docs.text:
pb::SymbolSelectRequest r; r.set_symbol("GBPJPY"); r.set_select(true);
if (account.symbolSelect(r).success()) {
    pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest tr; tr.set_symbol("GBPJPY");
    pb::MrpcMqlTick t = account.symbolInfoTick(tr);
    std::printf("GBPJPY %.3f / %.3f\n", t.bid(), t.ask());
}

docs.title: 2) Remove a symbol from Market Watch
docs.text:
pb::SymbolSelectRequest r; r.set_symbol("GBPJPY"); r.set_select(false);
std::printf("Removed: %s\n", account.symbolSelect(r).success() ? "yes" : "no");

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• SymbolExist — check a symbol exists before selecting it
  • SymbolInfoTick — quote a selected symbol
  • SymbolIsSynchronized — confirm data is ready after selecting

docs.title: MT5Account · Symbol Information — Overview
docs.text: Quotes, symbol properties, trading rules, and Market Watch management. Use this page to choose the right API for everything symbol-related.

docs.title: Current quotes
docs.text: • SymbolInfoTick — the current tick (bid, ask, last, volume, timestamps) in one call. Returns MrpcMqlTick directly.

docs.title: Symbol inventory & management
docs.text:
• SymbolsTotal — count of symbols (all, or only Market Watch).
  • SymbolName — resolve an index → symbol name.
  • SymbolList — all symbol names in one call (CppMT5 convenience).
  • SymbolSelect — add/remove a symbol in Market Watch.
  • SymbolExist — does a symbol exist (and is it custom)?
  • SymbolIsSynchronized — is the symbol's data ready?

docs.title: Symbol properties (enum-selected)
docs.text:
• SymbolInfoDouble — one double property (point, tick value, volume limits, swaps…). Uses SymbolInfoDoubleProperty.
  • SymbolInfoInteger — one int64 property (digits, spread, trade mode, session times…). Uses SymbolInfoIntegerProperty.
  • SymbolInfoString — one string property (description, currencies, path…). Uses SymbolInfoStringProperty.

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English
docs.text:
• Need the price now → symbolInfoTick().
  • Need one spec value (point, digits, volume min…) → symbolInfo* with the right property enum.
  • Need to walk the catalog → symbolsTotal() + symbolName(), or just symbolList().
  • A symbol isn't quoting → symbolSelect() it into Market Watch, then symbolIsSynchronized().

🧱 Enum note: the three symbolInfo* methods take a property enum as input (set_type(...)) and return a single value in value().

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Returns Enum used Current bid/ask/last symbolInfoTick MrpcMqlTick — One numeric spec (point, tick value, vol min) symbolInfoDouble double (value()) Input: SymbolInfoDoubleProperty One integer spec (digits, spread, trade mode) symbolInfoInteger int64 (value()/value_utc()) Input: SymbolInfoIntegerProperty One text spec (description, currencies) symbolInfoString string (value()) Input: SymbolInfoStringProperty Count symbols symbolsTotal int32 (total()) — Name by index symbolName string (name()) — All names at once symbolList repeated string — Add/remove in Market Watch symbolSelect bool (success()) — Exists? custom? symbolExist bool (exists(), is_custom()) — Data ready? symbolIsSynchronized bool (synchronized()) —

docs.title: ❌ Cross-refs & gotchas
docs.text:
• Select before you quote. Quotes/ticks/DOM flow only for selected symbols — call symbolSelect(true) first for unusual symbols, then symbolIsSynchronized().
  • value() not requested_value(). Unlike the Account group, symbolInfo* data uses value() (and value_utc() for time-based integer properties).
  • name vs symbol. symbolExist uses the name field; everything else uses symbol.
  • Point vs tick size. Use SYMBOL_POINT for price formatting and SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE / SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_VALUE for money math — they can differ.
  • Batch alternative. For many fields across many symbols, SymbolParamsMany is far cheaper than many single calls.

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippets
docs.text:
// Current price
pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest tr; tr.set_symbol("EURUSD");
pb::MrpcMqlTick t = account.symbolInfoTick(tr);
std::printf("Bid %.5f Ask %.5f\n", t.bid(), t.ask());

// One double property — point size
pb::SymbolInfoDoubleRequest dr; dr.set_symbol("EURUSD"); dr.set_type(pb::SYMBOL_POINT);
std::printf("Point: %.5f\n", account.symbolInfoDouble(dr).value());

// One integer property — digits
pb::SymbolInfoIntegerRequest ir; ir.set_symbol("EURUSD"); ir.set_type(pb::SYMBOL_DIGITS);
std::printf("Digits: %lld\n", (long long)account.symbolInfoInteger(ir).value());

// List every symbol
pb::SymbolListData list = account.symbolList();
std::printf("%d symbols\n", list.symbols_size());

docs.title: 🧱 Enums used in Symbol Information
docs.text:
Method Input enum Example values symbolInfoDouble SymbolInfoDoubleProperty SYMBOL_BID(0), SYMBOL_ASK(3), SYMBOL_POINT(13), SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_VALUE(14), SYMBOL_VOLUME_MIN(22) … (60 total) symbolInfoInteger SymbolInfoIntegerProperty SYMBOL_DIGITS(17), SYMBOL_SPREAD(19), SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE(22), SYMBOL_TIME(15) … symbolInfoString SymbolInfoStringProperty SYMBOL_DESCRIPTION(9), SYMBOL_CURRENCY_BASE(5), SYMBOL_CURRENCY_PROFIT(6), SYMBOL_PATH(14) …

Values are namespace-scope (pb::SYMBOL_POINT), not enum class.

  • Additional: SymbolParamsMany — many symbols, many fields, one call

  • Trading: OrderSend — place an order on a selected symbol

docs.title: ✅ Counting Available Symbols
docs.text:
Request: the number of symbols (SymbolsTotalData) available on the server, optionally only those in Market Watch.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbolsTotal(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolsTotal (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolsTotal(SymbolsTotalRequest) → SymbolsTotalReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Returns a single count of symbols.
  • Why you need it. To iterate symbols by index with SymbolName, or to size a UI list.
  • Sanity check. The count is > 0 on any live server.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns the symbol count. Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::SymbolsTotalData symbolsTotal(const pb::SymbolsTotalRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

SymbolsTotalRequest { bool mode = 1; }   // true = only Market Watch selected; false = all

SymbolsTotalReply {
  oneof response {
    SymbolsTotalData data  = 1;   // { int32 total = 1; }
    Error            error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description mode set_mode(bool) — bool true → count only symbols selected in Market Watch; false → count all symbols on the server.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolsTotalData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description Total total() int32_t Number of symbols counted.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Pair with SymbolName: iterate index = 0 … total-1 to enumerate symbols.
  • mode matters: the "all" count can be thousands; the Market Watch count is usually a short, curated list.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 1) Count all vs selected
docs.text:
auto count = [&](bool onlyMW) {
    pb::SymbolsTotalRequest r; r.set_mode(onlyMW);
    return account.symbolsTotal(r).total();
};
std::printf("All: %d | Market Watch: %d\n", count(false), count(true));

docs.title: 2) Enumerate every selected symbol
docs.text:
pb::SymbolsTotalRequest tr; tr.set_mode(true);
int32_t n = account.symbolsTotal(tr).total();

for (int32_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    pb::SymbolNameRequest nr; nr.set_index(i); nr.set_selected(true);
    std::printf("%2d: %s\n", i, account.symbolName(nr).name().c_str());
}

  • SymbolList — get all names in one call (no index loop)
  • SymbolSelect — add/remove a symbol from Market Watch

docs.title: ✅ Getting Open Positions and Pending Orders
docs.text:
Request: full details of every open position and pending order (OpenedOrdersData) in one call.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::openedOrders(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: OpenedOrders (defined in mt5-term-api-account-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: OpenedOrders(OpenedOrdersRequest) → OpenedOrdersReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Returns two lists: open positions (position_infos) and pending orders (opened_orders).
  • Why you need it. The core "what do I have live right now?" call — P/L, SL/TP, volumes, tickets.
  • Sanity check. position_infos_size() matches PositionsTotal.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Dashboard of all live exposure (positions) and resting orders.
  • Compute total floating P/L, net volume, SL/TP coverage.
  • Find a ticket to pass to OrderModify / OrderClose.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns all open positions and pending orders. Throws ApiError / TransportError.
pb::OpenedOrdersData openedOrders(const pb::OpenedOrdersRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

OpenedOrdersRequest {
  BMT5_ENUM_OPENED_ORDER_SORT_TYPE inputSortMode = 1;   // sort order
}

OpenedOrdersReply {
  oneof response {
    OpenedOrdersData data  = 1;
    Error            error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
⬆️ Output — OpenedOrdersData
docs.text:
Field C++ accessor Element type Description PositionInfos position_infos() PositionInfo Open positions (live exposure). OpenedOrders opened_orders() OpenedOrderInfo Pending orders (not yet filled).

Use position_infos_size() / opened_orders_size(), position_infos(i) / opened_orders(i), or range-for.

docs.title: PositionInfo — key fields
docs.text: Accessor Type Description ticket() int64 Position ticket. symbol() string Symbol. type() enum TMT5_ENUM_POSITION_TYPE — 0 = BUY, 1 = SELL. volume() double Position volume (lots). price_open() double Open price. price_current() double Current price. stop_loss() double SL price (0 = none). take_profit() double TP price (0 = none). profit() double Floating profit in account currency. swap() double Accrued swap. position_commission() double Commission. magic_number() int64 Magic (EA identifier). comment() string Order comment. open_time() Timestamp Open time (.seconds() for epoch). identifier() int64 Position identifier (stable across modifications). reason() enum Reason the position was opened.

docs.title: OpenedOrderInfo — key fields (pending orders)
docs.text: Accessor Type Description ticket() int64 Order ticket. symbol() string Symbol. type() enum Order type (BUY_LIMIT, SELL_STOP, …). state() enum Order state. volume_initial() double Requested volume. volume_current() double Remaining volume. price_open() double Trigger price. price_current() double Current market price. stop_loss() double SL price. take_profit() double TP price. stop_limit() double Stop-limit price (for *_STOP_LIMIT orders). magic_number() int64 Magic. comment() string Comment. time_setup() Timestamp When the order was placed. time_expiration() Timestamp Expiry (0 = GTC). position_id() int64 Linked position id.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Two separate lists. position_infos are live positions; opened_orders are pending orders. Don't mix them.
  • Position type is an enum. type() is 0 (BUY) or 1 (SELL) — not the order-type enum used when placing orders.
  • Guard with PositionsTotal if you only need a count.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 1) List positions with P/L
docs.text:
pb::OpenedOrdersRequest r; r.set_inputsortmode(0);
pb::OpenedOrdersData d = account.openedOrders(r);

double total = 0;
for (const auto& p : d.position_infos()) {
    std::printf("#%lld %s %s %.2f @ %.5f  P/L %.2f\n",
                (long long)p.ticket(), p.symbol().c_str(),
                p.type() == 0 ? "BUY" : "SELL",
                p.volume(), p.price_open(), p.profit());
    total += p.profit();
}
std::printf("Total floating P/L: %.2f\n", total);

docs.title: 2) List pending orders
docs.text:
pb::OpenedOrdersRequest r;
pb::OpenedOrdersData d = account.openedOrders(r);
for (const auto& o : d.opened_orders())
    std::printf("Pending #%lld %s vol %.2f @ %.5f\n",
                (long long)o.ticket(), o.symbol().c_str(),
                o.volume_current(), o.price_open());

docs.title: 3) Find a ticket for a symbol, then close it
docs.text:
pb::OpenedOrdersRequest r;
for (const auto& p : account.openedOrders(r).position_infos()) {
    if (p.symbol() == "EURUSD") {
        pb::OrderCloseRequest cr; cr.set_ticket(p.ticket());
        account.orderClose(cr);
        break;
    }
}

Full catalog: Enums Reference.

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Returns two lists of int64 tickets: open position tickets and pending order tickets.
  • Why you need it. A cheap way to detect which tickets exist (e.g. diffing against a previous snapshot) without the full OpenedOrders payload.
  • Sanity check. opened_position_tickets_size() matches PositionsTotal.

docs.text:
// Returns ticket numbers of open positions and pending orders.
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.

Request / Reply:

OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest {}   // (empty)

OpenedOrdersTicketsReply {

  }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description req const pb::OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest& Empty request message.

docs.text:
Field C++ accessor Element type Description OpenedPositionTickets opened_position_tickets() int64 Tickets of open positions. OpenedOrdersTickets opened_orders_tickets() int64 Tickets of pending orders.

Use *_size(), (i) indexing, or range-for.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Two lists. Positions and pending orders are returned separately.
  • Great for change detection. Compare consecutive snapshots to see what opened/closed without pulling full details.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 1) Print all tickets
docs.text:
pb::OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest r;
pb::OpenedOrdersTicketsData d = account.openedOrdersTickets(r);

std::printf("Positions: ");
for (int64_t t : d.opened_position_tickets()) std::printf("%lld ", (long long)t);
std::printf("\nPending: ");
for (int64_t t : d.opened_orders_tickets())   std::printf("%lld ", (long long)t);
std::printf("\n");

docs.title: 2) Detect newly opened positions
docs.text:
#include <set>
std::set<int64_t> snapshot(MT5Account& a) {
    std::set<int64_t> s;
    pb::OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest r;
    for (int64_t t : a.openedOrdersTickets(r).opened_position_tickets()) s.insert(t);
    return s;
}

std::set<int64_t> before = snapshot(account);
// ... later ...
for (int64_t t : snapshot(account))
    if (!before.count(t)) std::printf("New position: #%lld\n", (long long)t);

docs.title: ✅ Getting Historical Orders & Deals
docs.text:
Request: historical orders/deals within a time range (OrdersHistoryData), with sorting and pagination.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::orderHistory(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: OrderHistory (defined in mt5-term-api-account-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: OrderHistory(OrderHistoryRequest) → OrderHistoryReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Returns the order/deal history in a time window, sorted and paginated.
  • Why you need it. Trade journals, P/L reports, reconciling what actually executed.
  • Sanity check. arraytotal() is the total count across all pages.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Build a trade log for a date range.
  • Paginate through large histories with pagenumber / itemsperpage (or next_page_token).
  • Each HistoryData item carries both an order view (history_order) and a deal view (history_deal).

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns historical orders/deals for the requested window.
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::OrdersHistoryData orderHistory(const pb::OrderHistoryRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

OrderHistoryRequest {
  google.protobuf.Timestamp         inputFrom      = 1;   // broker tz
  google.protobuf.Timestamp         inputTo        = 2;
  BMT5_ENUM_ORDER_HISTORY_SORT_TYPE inputSortMode  = 3;
  int32                             pageNumber     = 4;
  int32                             itemsPerPage   = 5;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp         inputFromUtc   = 6;   // UTC equivalents
  google.protobuf.Timestamp         inputToUtc     = 7;
  string                            page_token     = 8;
}

OrderHistoryReply {
  oneof response {
    OrdersHistoryData data  = 1;
    Error             error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
Field C++ setter / type Description inputFromUtc mutable_inputfromutc()->set_seconds(epoch) Window start (UTC). Prefer the *Utc fields. inputToUtc mutable_inputtoutc()->set_seconds(epoch) Window end (UTC). inputSortMode set_inputsortmode(pb::BMT5_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_DESC) Sort order (see enum below). pageNumber set_pagenumber(0) — int32 Zero-based page index. itemsPerPage set_itemsperpage(100) — int32 Page size. page_token set_page_token(token) — string Alternative cursor-based pagination.

inputFrom / inputTo are in the broker time zone; inputFromUtc / inputToUtc are UTC. Use the UTC pair to avoid timezone surprises.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrdersHistoryData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor Type Description HistoryData history_data() repeated HistoryData The history items on this page. ArrayTotal arraytotal() int32 Total items across all pages. PageNumber pagenumber() int32 Current page index. ItemsPerPage itemsperpage() int32 Page size echoed back. NextPageToken next_page_token() string Cursor for the next page (if any).

docs.title: HistoryData — structure
docs.text: Accessor Type Description index() uint32 Item index. history_order() OrderHistoryData The order as it appears in history. history_deal() DealHistoryData The corresponding executed deal.

docs.title: 🧱 Sort enum — BMT5_ENUM_ORDER_HISTORY_SORT_TYPE
docs.text: Constant Value Meaning BMT5_SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC 0 By open time, ascending. BMT5_SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_DESC 1 By open time, descending. BMT5_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_ASC 2 By close time, ascending. BMT5_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_DESC 3 By close time, descending. BMT5_SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_ASC 4 By ticket id, ascending. BMT5_SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_DESC 5 By ticket id, descending.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Set the Timestamps via mutable_*(). Protobuf message fields aren't set with a set_ scalar — use r.mutable_inputfromutc()->set_seconds(epoch).
  • Big histories need a larger inbound limit. ClientOptions::maxReceiveMessageBytes defaults to 64 MB, which already covers large pages.
  • Prefer paging. Pull in pages (itemsperpage ~100–500) rather than an unbounded window.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 1) Last 7 days, newest first, first page
docs.text:
#include <ctime>
std::time_t now = std::time(nullptr);

pb::OrderHistoryRequest r;
r.mutable_inputfromutc()->set_seconds(now - 7 * 24 * 3600);
r.mutable_inputtoutc()->set_seconds(now);
r.set_inputsortmode(pb::BMT5_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_DESC);
r.set_pagenumber(0);
r.set_itemsperpage(100);

pb::OrdersHistoryData d = account.orderHistory(r);
std::printf("Total history items: %d (showing %d)\n", d.arraytotal(), d.history_data_size());
for (const auto& h : d.history_data())
    std::printf("  #%u order+deal pair\n", h.index());

docs.title: 2) Walk all pages
docs.text:
int page = 0;
for (;;) {
    pb::OrderHistoryRequest r;
    r.mutable_inputfromutc()->set_seconds(now - 30 * 24 * 3600);
    r.mutable_inputtoutc()->set_seconds(now);
    r.set_inputsortmode(pb::BMT5_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_ASC);
    r.set_pagenumber(page);
    r.set_itemsperpage(200);

    pb::OrdersHistoryData d = account.orderHistory(r);
    if (d.history_data_size() == 0) break;
    // ... process page ...
    if ((page + 1) * d.itemsperpage() >= d.arraytotal()) break;
    ++page;
}

  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::orderHistory(...) returns named HistoryItem / HistoryOrder / Deal structs with UTC times.

docs.title: PositionHistoryInfo — key fields
docs.text: Accessor Type Description ticket() int64 Position ticket. symbol() string Symbol. type() enum Position type (0 = BUY, 1 = SELL). reason() enum Why the position closed. volume() double Volume (lots). price_open() double Open price. price_current() double Close price. sl() double Stop loss. tp() double Take profit. profit() double Realized profit. swap() double Swap. magic() int64 Magic (EA id). from_pending_order() bool Whether it originated from a pending order. comment() string Comment.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Position-centric. One row per closed position — simpler than the order/deal pairs in OrderHistory.
  • Timestamps via mutable_*(). Use the *_utc fields for unambiguous windows.
  • sl() / tp(). Note this struct uses the short sl()/tp() accessors (not stop_loss()/take_profit()).
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 1) Last 30 days of closed positions, newest first
docs.text:
#include <ctime>
std::time_t now = std::time(nullptr);

pb::PositionsHistoryRequest r;
r.mutable_position_open_time_from_utc()->set_seconds(now - 30 * 24 * 3600);
r.mutable_position_open_time_to_utc()->set_seconds(now);
r.set_sort_type(pb::AH_POSITION_OPEN_TIME_DESC);
r.set_page_number(0);
r.set_items_per_page(100);

pb::PositionsHistoryData d = account.positionsHistory(r);
std::printf("Closed positions: %d\n", d.total_count());
for (const auto& p : d.history_positions())
    std::printf("#%lld %s %.2f lots  P/L %.2f\n",
                (long long)p.ticket(), p.symbol().c_str(), p.volume(), p.profit());

docs.title: 2) Aggregate realized P/L and win rate
docs.text:
double gross = 0; int wins = 0, n = 0;
for (const auto& p : account.positionsHistory(r).history_positions()) {
    gross += p.profit(); ++n;
    if (p.profit() > 0) ++wins;
}
std::printf("Net %.2f over %d trades, win rate %.0f%%\n",
            gross, n, n ? 100.0 * wins / n : 0.0);

docs.title: MT5Account · Positions & Orders — Overview
docs.text: Open positions, pending orders, ticket lists, and historical trades. Use this page to choose the right read API for account state over time.

docs.title: Current state
docs.text:
• PositionsTotal — count of open positions (no args). Service TradeFunctions.
  • OpenedOrders — full details of all open positions (position_infos) and pending orders (opened_orders).
  • OpenedOrdersTickets — ticket numbers only (lightweight), positions and pending orders.

docs.title: Historical data
docs.text:
• OrderHistory — order/deal history in a time range (sorted, paginated). Each item pairs an order view and a deal view.
  • PositionsHistory — closed positions in a time range (one row per position; sorted, paginated).

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English
docs.text:
• "Do I have anything open?" → positionsTotal().
  • "Show me everything live" → openedOrders() (positions + pending orders).
  • "Just the tickets" (cheap, for diffing) → openedOrdersTickets().
  • "What happened last week?" → orderHistory() (orders/deals) or positionsHistory() (closed positions).

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Returns Notes Count of open positions positionsTotal int32 (total_positions()) No arguments. All open positions + pending orders openedOrders PositionInfo[] + OpenedOrderInfo[] Sort via inputSortMode. Just ticket numbers openedOrdersTickets int64[] positions + int64[] orders Lightweight; great for change detection. Order/deal history orderHistory HistoryData[] + pagination Each item = order view + deal view. Closed positions positionsHistory PositionHistoryInfo[] + pagination One row per closed position.

docs.title: ❌ Cross-refs & gotchas
docs.text:
• Positions vs pending orders. openedOrders() returns them as two separate lists — don't conflate position_infos with opened_orders.
  • Two histories, two shapes. orderHistory is order/deal-centric (each HistoryData has history_order + history_deal); positionsHistory is position-centric (one PositionHistoryInfo per closed position).
  • Timestamps via mutable_*(). History requests use google.protobuf.Timestamp fields — set them with mutable_...()->set_seconds(epoch), and prefer the *Utc variants.
  • Accessor naming differs. Live PositionInfo uses stop_loss()/take_profit(); closed PositionHistoryInfo uses sl()/tp().
  • Pagination. History methods support page number + size and a next_page_token cursor — don't request unbounded windows.

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippets
docs.text:
// Count
std::printf("Open: %d\n", account.positionsTotal().total_positions());

// Live positions
pb::OpenedOrdersRequest r;
for (const auto& p : account.openedOrders(r).position_infos())
    std::printf("#%lld %s P/L %.2f\n", (long long)p.ticket(), p.symbol().c_str(), p.profit());

// Tickets only
pb::OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest tr;
pb::OpenedOrdersTicketsData td = account.openedOrdersTickets(tr);
std::printf("%d open position tickets\n", td.opened_position_tickets_size());

// Closed positions, last 7 days
#include <ctime>
std::time_t now = std::time(nullptr);
pb::PositionsHistoryRequest hr;
hr.mutable_position_open_time_from_utc()->set_seconds(now - 7*24*3600);
hr.mutable_position_open_time_to_utc()->set_seconds(now);
hr.set_sort_type(pb::AH_POSITION_OPEN_TIME_DESC);
std::printf("Closed: %d\n", account.positionsHistory(hr).total_count());

• Service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • Method: OrderCalcMargin(OrderCalcMarginRequest) → OrderCalcMarginReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Computes the margin needed to open a given volume of a symbol at a price.
  • Why you need it. Pre-trade risk checks and position sizing — "can I afford this?".
  • Sanity check. Larger volume → larger margin.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns the margin required for the described trade. Throws ApiError / TransportError.
pb::OrderCalcMarginData orderCalcMargin(const pb::OrderCalcMarginRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

OrderCalcMarginRequest {
  ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TF order_type = 1;   // BUY/SELL/...
  string             symbol     = 2;
  double             volume     = 3;   // lots
  double             open_price = 4;
}

OrderCalcMarginReply { oneof response { OrderCalcMarginData data = 1; Error error = 2; } }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
Field C++ setter / type Description order_type set_order_type(pb::ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY) Direction (see ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TF). symbol set_symbol("EURUSD") Instrument. volume set_volume(1.0) Lots. open_price set_open_price(1.0850) Hypothetical entry price.

ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TF mirrors TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE: ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY(0), ..._SELL(1), ..._BUY_LIMIT(2), … ..._CLOSE_BY(8).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderCalcMarginData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description Margin margin() double Required margin in the account currency.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Compare with free margin from AccountSummary (account_margin_free()): trade is affordable if margin() ≤ free margin (with a buffer).
  • Great for sizing. Back out the max volume for a given margin budget by scaling linearly.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 1) Margin for 1 lot EURUSD
docs.text:
pb::OrderCalcMarginRequest r;
r.set_order_type(pb::ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY);
r.set_symbol("EURUSD");
r.set_volume(1.0);
r.set_open_price(1.0850);
std::printf("Margin for 1.0 lot: %.2f\n", account.orderCalcMargin(r).margin());

docs.title: 2) Affordability check
docs.text:
double freeMargin = account.accountSummary().account_margin_free();
pb::OrderCalcMarginRequest r;
r.set_order_type(pb::ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY); r.set_symbol("EURUSD");
r.set_volume(0.5); r.set_open_price(1.0850);

double need = account.orderCalcMargin(r).margin();
std::printf("%s (need %.2f / free %.2f)\n",
            need <= freeMargin ? "OK" : "NOT ENOUGH MARGIN", need, freeMargin);

  • OrderCheck — full pre-trade validation (margin + free margin + retcode)
  • OrderSend — place the trade
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::orderCalcMargin(...) / MT5Sugar risk-sizing helpers.

docs.title: ✅ Calculating Potential Profit
docs.text:
Request: the profit a trade would yield for a given price move (OrderCalcProfitData).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::orderCalcProfit(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • Proto definition: OrderCalcProfit (defined in mt5-term-api-trade-functions.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • Method: OrderCalcProfit(OrderCalcProfitRequest) → OrderCalcProfitReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Computes the profit (account currency) of moving volume of a symbol from open_price to close_price.
  • Why you need it. Project TP/SL money value, compare setups, size by reward.
  • Sanity check. For a BUY, close_price > open_price → positive profit.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns the profit for the described move. Throws ApiError / TransportError.
pb::OrderCalcProfitData orderCalcProfit(const pb::OrderCalcProfitRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

OrderCalcProfitRequest {
  ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TF order_type  = 1;   // BUY/SELL
  string             symbol      = 2;
  double             volume      = 3;
  double             open_price  = 4;
  double             close_price = 5;
}

OrderCalcProfitReply { oneof response { OrderCalcProfitData data = 1; Error error = 2; } }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description order_type set_order_type(pb::ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY) Direction. symbol set_symbol("EURUSD") Instrument. volume set_volume(1.0) Lots. open_price set_open_price(1.0850) Entry price. close_price set_close_price(1.0900) Exit price.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderCalcProfitData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description Profit profit() double Profit in the account currency (can be negative).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Direction matters. Use ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY vs ORDER_TYPE_TF_SELL — a SELL profits when price falls.
  • Money value of a TP/SL. Pass your target/stop as close_price to see the $ outcome before trading.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 1) Profit of a 50-pip TP on 1 lot
docs.text:
pb::OrderCalcProfitRequest r;
r.set_order_type(pb::ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY);
r.set_symbol("EURUSD");
r.set_volume(1.0);
r.set_open_price(1.0850);
r.set_close_price(1.0900);
std::printf("Profit at TP: %.2f\n", account.orderCalcProfit(r).profit());

docs.title: 2) Risk/reward of a setup
docs.text:
auto calc = [&](double open, double close) {
    pb::OrderCalcProfitRequest r;
    r.set_order_type(pb::ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY); r.set_symbol("EURUSD");
    r.set_volume(0.10); r.set_open_price(open); r.set_close_price(close);
    return account.orderCalcProfit(r).profit();
};
double reward = calc(1.0850, 1.0900);   // +50 pips
double risk   = calc(1.0850, 1.0820);   // -30 pips
std::printf("R:R = %.2f : %.2f\n", reward, -risk);
