  • OrderSend — place the trade
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::orderCalcProfit(...).

docs.title: ✅ Validating a Trade Before Sending
docs.text:
Request: dry-run a trade request and get the resulting margin/equity and a retcode (OrderCheckData) — without executing.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::orderCheck(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • Proto definition: OrderCheck (defined in mt5-term-api-trade-functions.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • Method: OrderCheck(OrderCheckRequest) → OrderCheckReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Validates a full trade request and reports whether it would succeed, plus the margin/free-margin/equity after the hypothetical deal.
  • Why you need it. The safest pre-flight: catches "not enough money", "invalid stops", "invalid volume" before you send.
  • Success = result's returned_code() == 0 (check passed). (This is the check retcode, not the trade 10009.)

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Validates req.mql_trade_request(). Returns the check result.
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::OrderCheckData orderCheck(const pb::OrderCheckRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

OrderCheckRequest { MrpcMqlTradeRequest mql_trade_request = 1; }

OrderCheckReply {
  oneof response {
    OrderCheckData data  = 1;   // { MrpcMqlTradeCheckResult mql_trade_check_result = 1; }
    Error          error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input — MrpcMqlTradeRequest (key fields)
docs.text:
Build the embedded request via req.mutable_mql_trade_request():

Field C++ setter / type Description action set_action(...) — MRPC_ENUM_TRADE_REQUEST_ACTIONS DEAL (market) / PENDING / SLTP / MODIFY / REMOVE / CLOSE_BY. symbol set_symbol("EURUSD") Instrument. order_type set_order_type(pb::ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY) — ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TF Direction/type. volume set_volume(0.10) Lots. price set_price(1.0850) Entry price. stop_loss / take_profit set_stop_loss(...) / set_take_profit(...) SL/TP. stop_limit set_stop_limit(...) For *_STOP_LIMIT. deviation set_deviation(10) Max slippage (points). expert_advisor_magic_number set_expert_advisor_magic_number(777) Magic number. type_filling / type_time set_type_filling(...) / set_type_time(...) Filling & time policy. position / position_by set_position(...) / set_position_by(...) For modify/close-by. comment set_comment("...") Comment.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderCheckData → mql_trade_check_result() (MrpcMqlTradeCheckResult)
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description ReturnedCode returned_code() uint32_t Check retcode (0 = request is valid). Comment comment() string Explanation (e.g. reason it would fail). Balance balance_after_deal() double Balance after the hypothetical deal. Equity equity_after_deal() double Equity after the hypothetical deal. Profit profit() double Projected profit of the deal. Margin margin() double Margin the deal would require. FreeMargin free_margin() double Free margin remaining after the deal. MarginLevel margin_level() double Margin level (%) after the deal.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Two different retcodes. orderCheck result returned_code() == 0 means valid; orderSend success is 10009. Don't confuse them.
  • Set the nested message with mutable_. req.mutable_mql_trade_request()->set_symbol(...).
  • Use before every risky send. It's the cleanest way to surface "not enough money" / "invalid stops" as data instead of a rejected order.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 1) Validate a market BUY
docs.text:
pb::OrderCheckRequest req;
auto* tr = req.mutable_mql_trade_request();
tr->set_action(pb::MRPC_ENUM_TRADE_REQUEST_ACTIONS(0));   // DEAL (market)
tr->set_symbol("EURUSD");
tr->set_order_type(pb::ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY);
tr->set_volume(0.10);
tr->set_price(1.0850);
tr->set_deviation(10);

pb::OrderCheckData d = account.orderCheck(req);
const auto& res = d.mql_trade_check_result();
if (res.returned_code() == 0)
    std::printf("OK — margin %.2f, free after %.2f\n", res.margin(), res.free_margin());
else
    std::printf("Would fail: %u %s\n", res.returned_code(), res.comment().c_str());

docs.title: 2) Check then send
docs.text:
// (build req as above)
if (account.orderCheck(req).mql_trade_check_result().returned_code() == 0) {
    pb::OrderSendRequest s;
    s.set_symbol("EURUSD"); s.set_operation(pb::TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY);
    s.set_volume(0.10); s.set_price(1.0850); s.set_slippage(10);
    std::printf("send retcode %u\n", account.orderSend(s).returned_code());
}

docs.title: 🧱 Enums used
docs.text:
The embedded MrpcMqlTradeRequest is built from several input enums (namespace-scope values, e.g. pb::TRADE_ACTION_DEAL):

Field Enum Values action MRPC_ENUM_TRADE_REQUEST_ACTIONS TRADE_ACTION_DEAL(0), _PENDING(1), _SLTP(2), _MODIFY(3), _REMOVE(4), _CLOSE_BY(5) order_type ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TF ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY(0) … ORDER_TYPE_TF_CLOSE_BY(8) type_filling MRPC_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_FILLING ORDER_FILLING_FOK(0), _IOC(1), _RETURN(2), _BOC(3) type_time TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TIME TMT5_ORDER_TIME_GTC(0), _DAY(1), _SPECIFIED(2), _SPECIFIED_DAY(3)

Full catalog with values: Enums Reference.

docs.text:

  • OrderCalcMargin / OrderCalcProfit — single-number calculators
  • Return Codes
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::orderCheck(...) returns a named OrderCheckResult struct.

docs.title: ✅ Closing a Position (Full or Partial)
docs.text:
Request: close an open position by ticket, fully or partially (OrderCloseData).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::orderClose(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Proto definition: OrderClose (defined in mt5-term-api-trading-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Method: OrderClose(OrderCloseRequest) → OrderCloseReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Closes a position (or part of it); can also delete a pending order by ticket.
  • Why you need it. Exit the market, take profit/cut loss, scale out.
  • Success = returned_code() == 10009.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Closes the ticket in req. Returns the trade result (check returned_code()).
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::OrderCloseData orderClose(const pb::OrderCloseRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

OrderCloseRequest {
  uint64 ticket   = 1;
  double volume   = 2;   // 0 ⇒ close full volume; >0 ⇒ partial close
  int32  slippage = 3;   // max deviation (points)
}

OrderCloseReply { oneof response { OrderCloseData data = 1; Error error = 2; } }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description ticket set_ticket(123456) — uint64 Position (or pending-order) ticket to close. volume set_volume(0.0) — double 0 → close the whole position; a smaller value → partial close. slippage set_slippage(10) — int32 Max price deviation (points).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderCloseData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description ReturnedCode returned_code() uint32_t 10009 = DONE. ReturnedCodeDescription returned_code_description() string Human-readable retcode. ReturnedStringCode returned_string_code() string String retcode. CloseMode close_mode() MRPC_ORDER_CLOSE_MODE How the close was performed (netting/hedging/close-by).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Partial close must respect volume step. The remaining and closed volumes must each be a multiple of SYMBOL_VOLUME_STEP and ≥ SYMBOL_VOLUME_MIN.
  • Hedging vs netting. On a netting account closing is really an opposite deal; close_mode() tells you what the server did.
  • Check the retcode — a normal return does not guarantee a fill.
  • Trade timeout ClientOptions::tradeTimeoutMs (default 60000 ms).

docs.title: 1) Close a whole position
docs.text:
pb::OrderCloseRequest r;
r.set_ticket(123456);
r.set_volume(0.0);        // full
r.set_slippage(10);
pb::OrderCloseData res = account.orderClose(r);
std::printf("Close retcode: %u\n", res.returned_code());

docs.title: 2) Scale out half
docs.text:
pb::OpenedOrdersRequest or_;
for (const auto& p : account.openedOrders(or_).position_infos()) {
    if (p.symbol() != "EURUSD") continue;
    pb::OrderCloseRequest r;
    r.set_ticket(p.ticket());
    r.set_volume(p.volume() / 2.0);   // partial
    r.set_slippage(10);
    std::printf("Partial close retcode: %u\n", account.orderClose(r).returned_code());
    break;
}

docs.title: 3) Close everything
docs.text:
pb::OpenedOrdersRequest or_;
for (const auto& p : account.openedOrders(or_).position_infos()) {
    pb::OrderCloseRequest r; r.set_ticket(p.ticket()); r.set_slippage(10);
    account.orderClose(r);
}

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• OrderSend — open positions
  • OrderModify — change SL/TP instead of closing
  • OpenedOrders — find the ticket and its volume
  • Friendly layer: MT5Sugar::closePosition(ticket) / closeAllPositions().

docs.title: ✅ Modifying an Order or Position
docs.text:
Request: change SL/TP (for a position) or price/SL/TP/expiration (for a pending order) — OrderModifyData.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::orderModify(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Proto definition: OrderModify (defined in mt5-term-api-trading-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Method: OrderModify(OrderModifyRequest) → OrderModifyReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Updates an existing ticket: a position's SL/TP, or a pending order's price, SL/TP, stop-limit and expiration.
  • Why you need it. Trail a stop, move to break-even, reprice a pending order.
  • Success = returned_code() == 10009.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Modifies the ticket in req. Returns the trade result (check returned_code()).
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::OrderModifyData orderModify(const pb::OrderModifyRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

OrderModifyRequest {
  uint64                    ticket               = 1;
  double                    price                = 2;   // pending orders only
  double                    stop_loss            = 3;
  double                    take_profit          = 4;
  double                    stop_limit           = 5;   // *_STOP_LIMIT only
  TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TIME expiration_time_type = 6;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp expiration_time      = 7;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp expiration_time_utc  = 8;
}

OrderModifyReply { oneof response { OrderModifyData data = 1; Error error = 2; } }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description ticket set_ticket(123456) — uint64 Position or pending-order ticket to modify. price set_price(1.0820) New trigger price (pending orders only; ignore for positions). stop_loss set_stop_loss(1.0800) New SL (0 = remove). take_profit set_take_profit(1.0900) New TP (0 = remove). stop_limit set_stop_limit(...) New stop-limit price (for *_STOP_LIMIT). expiration_time_type set_expiration_time_type(...) New expiration policy (pending orders).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderModifyData
docs.text:
Same shape as OrderSend's result:

Accessor Type Description returned_code() uint32_t 10009 = DONE. returned_code_description() string Human-readable retcode. returned_string_code() string String retcode. order() / deal() uint64_t Affected tickets. price() / volume() double Resulting price/volume. bid() / ask() double Market at execution. comment() string Broker comment.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Positions: SL/TP only. For an open position, set stop_loss / take_profit; leave price as-is (price can't move an open position).
  • Respect stops level. SL/TP must be at least SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL points away from price, or the modify is rejected.
  • Read current values first with OpenedOrders so you don't accidentally clear an SL/TP you meant to keep.
  • Trade timeout ClientOptions::tradeTimeoutMs (default 60000 ms).

docs.title: 1) Move a position's stop to break-even
docs.text:
// Find the position
pb::OpenedOrdersRequest or_;
for (const auto& p : account.openedOrders(or_).position_infos()) {
    if (p.symbol() != "EURUSD") continue;
    pb::OrderModifyRequest r;
    r.set_ticket(p.ticket());
    r.set_stop_loss(p.price_open());      // break-even
    r.set_take_profit(p.take_profit());   // keep existing TP
    pb::OrderModifyData res = account.orderModify(r);
    std::printf("Modify retcode: %u\n", res.returned_code());
    break;
}

docs.title: 2) Reprice a pending order
docs.text:
pb::OrderModifyRequest r;
r.set_ticket(987654);
r.set_price(1.0790);
r.set_take_profit(1.0890);
std::printf("retcode %u\n", account.orderModify(r).returned_code());

docs.title: 🧱 Enums used
docs.text:
Field (input) Enum Values expiration_time_type TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TIME TMT5_ORDER_TIME_GTC(0), _DAY(1), _SPECIFIED(2), _SPECIFIED_DAY(3)

The output returned_code is a trade retcode (10009 = DONE), not an enum. Full catalog: Enums Reference · Return Codes.

  • OrderClose — close a position
  • OpenedOrders — read the current ticket/SL/TP first
  • Friendly layer: MT5Sugar::setStopLoss(ticket, price) / setTakeProfit(ticket, price).

docs.title: ✅ Placing an Order (Market or Pending)
docs.text:
Request: open a market position or place a pending order (OrderSendData) — the core trading call.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::orderSend(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Proto definition: OrderSend (defined in mt5-term-api-trading-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Method: OrderSend(OrderSendRequest) → OrderSendReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Sends a trade request: market BUY/SELL, or a pending LIMIT/STOP/STOP_LIMIT order.
  • Why you need it. It's how you actually enter the market.
  • Success = returned_code() == 10009 (DONE). Always check it — a reply is not the same as a fill.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Open a market position (TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY / ..._SELL).
  • Place a pending order (..._BUY_LIMIT, ..._SELL_STOP, …) at a chosen price.
  • Attach SL/TP at entry, set a magic number and comment.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Sends an order. Returns the server's trade result (check returned_code()).
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on transport/validation failure.
pb::OrderSendData orderSend(const pb::OrderSendRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

OrderSendRequest {
  string               symbol               = 1;
  TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE operation            = 2;   // BUY/SELL/BUY_LIMIT/...
  double               volume               = 3;   // lots
  double               price                = 4;   // entry price (0 ⇒ market for BUY/SELL)
  double               stop_limit_price     = 5;   // for *_STOP_LIMIT
  double               stop_loss            = 6;
  double               take_profit          = 7;
  uint64               slippage             = 8;   // max deviation (points)
  uint64               expert_id            = 9;   // magic number
  string               comment              = 10;
  TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TIME expiration_time_type = 11;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp expiration_time      = 12;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp expiration_time_utc  = 13;
  int32                quotes_wait_ms       = 14;
}

OrderSendReply { oneof response { OrderSendData data = 1; Error error = 2; } }

docs.title: 🔽 Input (common fields)
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description symbol set_symbol("EURUSD") Instrument (must be selected in Market Watch). operation set_operation(pb::TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY) Order type (see enum). volume set_volume(0.01) Lots (respect SYMBOL_VOLUME_MIN/STEP). price set_price(1.0850) Entry price; for market BUY/SELL pass the current ask/bid (or 0). Required for pending orders. stop_limit_price set_stop_limit_price(...) Only for *_STOP_LIMIT orders. stop_loss set_stop_loss(1.0800) SL price (0 = none). take_profit set_take_profit(1.0900) TP price (0 = none). slippage set_slippage(10) Max price deviation in points (market orders). expert_id set_expert_id(123456) Magic number (tag your EA's orders). comment set_comment("my-strategy") Free-text comment. expiration_time_type set_expiration_time_type(...) GTC / DAY / SPECIFIED for pending orders.

docs.title: 🧱 Order-type enum — TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE
docs.text: Constant Value Meaning TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY 0 Market buy. TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_SELL 1 Market sell. TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY_LIMIT 2 Buy limit (below market). TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_SELL_LIMIT 3 Sell limit (above market). TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY_STOP 4 Buy stop (above market). TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_SELL_STOP 5 Sell stop (below market). TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY_STOP_LIMIT 6 Buy stop-limit. TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_SELL_STOP_LIMIT 7 Sell stop-limit. TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_CLOSE_BY 8 Close-by (offset opposite).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderSendData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description ReturnedCode returned_code() uint32_t Trade retcode — 10009 = DONE (success). ReturnedCodeDescription returned_code_description() string Human-readable description of the retcode. ReturnedStringCode returned_string_code() string String form of the retcode. RetCodeExternal ret_code_external() int32_t External system return code. Deal deal() uint64_t Deal ticket (for market execution). Order order() uint64_t Order ticket. Volume volume() double Executed/accepted volume. Price price() double Execution price. Bid bid() double Current bid at execution. Ask ask() double Current ask at execution. Comment comment() string Broker comment. RequestId request_id() uint32_t Request correlation id.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Check the retcode, not just the absence of an exception. orderSend() returns normally for a rejected trade too — inspect returned_code() (10009 = DONE). See Return Codes.
  • Select the symbol first (SymbolSelect) and normalize volume against SYMBOL_VOLUME_MIN/STEP.
  • Validate before sending with OrderCheck when you want to know margin impact up front.
  • Trade timeout. Trading RPCs use ClientOptions::tradeTimeoutMs (default 60000 ms).
  • Pending orders need a price (and stop_limit_price for *_STOP_LIMIT) and usually an expiration policy.

docs.title: 1) Market BUY 0.01 lot with SL/TP
docs.text:
// current ask
pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest tr; tr.set_symbol("EURUSD");
double ask = account.symbolInfoTick(tr).ask();

pb::OrderSendRequest r;
r.set_symbol("EURUSD");
r.set_operation(pb::TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY);
r.set_volume(0.01);
r.set_price(ask);
r.set_stop_loss(ask - 0.0050);
r.set_take_profit(ask + 0.0050);
r.set_slippage(10);
r.set_expert_id(777);
r.set_comment("demo-buy");

pb::OrderSendData res = account.orderSend(r);
if (res.returned_code() == 10009)
    std::printf("DONE: order #%llu @ %.5f\n", (unsigned long long)res.order(), res.price());
else
    std::printf("Rejected: %u %s\n", res.returned_code(), res.returned_code_description().c_str());

docs.title: 2) Pending BUY LIMIT below market
docs.text:
pb::OrderSendRequest r;
r.set_symbol("EURUSD");
r.set_operation(pb::TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY_LIMIT);
r.set_volume(0.01);
r.set_price(1.0800);          // trigger price
r.set_take_profit(1.0900);
pb::OrderSendData res = account.orderSend(r);
std::printf("Pending placed: retcode %u, order #%llu\n",
            res.returned_code(), (unsigned long long)res.order());

docs.title: 3) A guard helper
docs.text:
bool sendOk(MT5Account& a, const pb::OrderSendRequest& r, pb::OrderSendData& out) {
    try {
        out = a.orderSend(r);
        return out.returned_code() == 10009;
    } catch (const ApiError& e)      { std::printf("API: %s\n", e.what()); }
      catch (const TransportError& e){ std::printf("NET: %s\n", e.what()); }
    return false;
}

docs.title: MT5Account · Trading Operations — Overview
docs.text: Order execution, position management, and pre-trade calculations. This is the group that actually moves money — read the notes carefully.

docs.title: Order execution & management (TradingHelper)
docs.text:
• OrderSend — open a market position or place a pending order.
  • OrderModify — change SL/TP (position) or price/SL/TP/expiration (pending).
  • OrderClose — close a position fully or partially.

docs.title: Pre-trade calculations (TradeFunctions)
docs.text:
• OrderCalcMargin — margin required for a prospective trade.
  • OrderCalcProfit — profit for a given price move.
  • OrderCheck — full dry-run validation (margin, free margin, retcode).

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English
docs.text:
• "Enter the market" → orderSend().
  • "Change my stop / move my pending" → orderModify().
  • "Get out" → orderClose().
  • "Can I afford it? Will it work?" → orderCalcMargin() / orderCalcProfit() / orderCheck() first.

⚠️ Golden rule: a normal return is not a fill. For orderSend/Modify/Close, success is returned_code() == 10009 (DONE). For orderCheck, a valid request is check returned_code() == 0.

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Returns Success check Open / place an order orderSend OrderSendData returned_code() == 10009 Change SL/TP or pending price orderModify OrderModifyData returned_code() == 10009 Close (full/partial) orderClose OrderCloseData returned_code() == 10009 Margin for a trade orderCalcMargin double (margin()) — Profit for a move orderCalcProfit double (profit()) — Validate everything up front orderCheck MrpcMqlTradeCheckResult result returned_code() == 0

docs.title: 🧱 Order-type enums
docs.text:
Two parallel enums, 1:1 by value:

Use in… Enum Values (0…8) orderSend (operation) TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY, ..._SELL, ..._BUY_LIMIT, ..._SELL_LIMIT, ..._BUY_STOP, ..._SELL_STOP, ..._BUY_STOP_LIMIT, ..._SELL_STOP_LIMIT, ..._CLOSE_BY orderCalc* / orderCheck (order_type) ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TF ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY, ..._SELL, ..._BUY_LIMIT, … ..._CLOSE_BY

(int)TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY == (int)ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY == 0, and so on.

docs.title: ❌ Cross-refs & gotchas
docs.text:
• Check the retcode. Covered above — the single most common mistake.
  • Normalize volume & respect stops level. Snap volume to SYMBOL_VOLUME_STEP (≥ SYMBOL_VOLUME_MIN); keep SL/TP ≥ SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL points from price. See SymbolInfoDouble / SymbolInfoInteger.
  • Select the symbol first. SymbolSelect before trading an unusual symbol.
  • Timestamps via mutable_*(). Expiration fields are google.protobuf.Timestamp.
  • Trade timeout. Trading RPCs use ClientOptions::tradeTimeoutMs (default 60000 ms), longer than read RPCs.
  • orderCheck embeds a MrpcMqlTradeRequest — set it via req.mutable_mql_trade_request().

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippets
docs.text:
// Market BUY with SL/TP
pb::OrderSendRequest r;
r.set_symbol("EURUSD"); r.set_operation(pb::TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY);
r.set_volume(0.01); r.set_price(1.0850);
r.set_stop_loss(1.0800); r.set_take_profit(1.0900); r.set_slippage(10);
std::printf("retcode %u\n", account.orderSend(r).returned_code());   // 10009 = DONE

// Margin for 1 lot
pb::OrderCalcMarginRequest m;
m.set_order_type(pb::ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY); m.set_symbol("EURUSD");
m.set_volume(1.0); m.set_open_price(1.0850);
std::printf("margin %.2f\n", account.orderCalcMargin(m).margin());

// Close a ticket
pb::OrderCloseRequest c; c.set_ticket(123456); c.set_slippage(10);
std::printf("close retcode %u\n", account.orderClose(c).returned_code());

docs.title: ✅ Subscribing to Market Depth (DOM)
docs.text:
Request: open a Level II / Depth-of-Market subscription for a symbol (MarketBookAddData).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::marketBookAdd(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: MarketBookAdd (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: MarketBookAdd(MarketBookAddRequest) → MarketBookAddReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Opens a DOM (order book) subscription for one symbol on the server side.
  • Why you need it. You must subscribe before MarketBookGet returns data.
  • Sanity check. opened_successfully() is true.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Opens a Market Depth subscription for req.symbol().
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::MarketBookAddData marketBookAdd(const pb::MarketBookAddRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

MarketBookAddRequest { string symbol = 1; }

MarketBookAddReply {
  oneof response {
    MarketBookAddData data  = 1;   // { bool opened_successfully = 1; }
    Error             error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description symbol set_symbol("EURUSD") — string Symbol to subscribe DOM for.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — MarketBookAddData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description OpenedSuccessfully opened_successfully() bool true if the subscription opened.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Not all symbols/brokers provide DOM. If opened_successfully() is false, the instrument likely has no Level II data.
  • Always release. Pair every marketBookAdd with a MarketBookRelease when done.
  • Select the symbol first (SymbolSelect).
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 🔗 Usage Example
docs.text:
pb::MarketBookAddRequest r; r.set_symbol("EURUSD");
if (account.marketBookAdd(r).opened_successfully()) {
    // ... poll MarketBookGet ...
    pb::MarketBookReleaseRequest rel; rel.set_symbol("EURUSD");
    account.marketBookRelease(rel);
} else {
    std::puts("DOM not available for this symbol");
}

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• MarketBookGet — read the order book once subscribed
  • MarketBookRelease — unsubscribe
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::marketBookAdd("EURUSD").

docs.title: ✅ Reading the Order Book (DOM)
docs.text:
Request: the current Level II order book for a subscribed symbol (MarketBookGetData).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::marketBookGet(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: MarketBookGet (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: MarketBookGet(MarketBookGetRequest) → MarketBookGetReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Returns the current snapshot of the order book: a list of bid/ask levels with price and volume.
  • Why you need it. Gauge liquidity and depth beyond the top-of-book bid/ask.
  • Prerequisite. You must have called MarketBookAdd for the symbol first.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns the current order book for req.symbol().
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::MarketBookGetData marketBookGet(const pb::MarketBookGetRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

MarketBookGetRequest { string symbol = 1; }

MarketBookGetReply {
  oneof response {
    MarketBookGetData data  = 1;   // { repeated MrpcMqlBookInfo mql_book_infos = 1; }
    Error             error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description symbol set_symbol("EURUSD") — string Symbol (must be subscribed via marketBookAdd).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — MarketBookGetData
docs.text:
Field C++ accessor Element type Description MqlBookInfos mql_book_infos() MrpcMqlBookInfo Order book levels.

Use mql_book_infos_size(), mql_book_infos(i), or range-for.

docs.title: MrpcMqlBookInfo — level fields
docs.text: Accessor Type Description type() BookType Level side: BOOK_TYPE_SELL(0), BOOK_TYPE_BUY(1), BOOK_TYPE_SELL_MARKET(2), BOOK_TYPE_BUY_MARKET(3). price() double Price at this level. volume() int64 Volume at this level (integer). volume_real() double Volume with greater precision.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Levels come in both sides. Filter by type() to split asks (SELL) from bids (BUY).
  • Snapshot, not a stream. Poll marketBookGet for updates, or use tick streaming for top-of-book.
  • Empty book? If you didn't call MarketBookAdd (or the symbol has no DOM), the list may be empty.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 🔗 Usage Example
docs.text:
pb::MarketBookAddRequest add; add.set_symbol("EURUSD");
account.marketBookAdd(add);

pb::MarketBookGetRequest r; r.set_symbol("EURUSD");
pb::MarketBookGetData book = account.marketBookGet(r);

for (const auto& lvl : book.mql_book_infos()) {
    const char* side =
        lvl.type() == pb::BOOK_TYPE_BUY || lvl.type() == pb::BOOK_TYPE_BUY_MARKET ? "BID" : "ASK";
    std::printf("%s  %.5f  x%lld\n", side, lvl.price(), (long long)lvl.volume());
}

pb::MarketBookReleaseRequest rel; rel.set_symbol("EURUSD");
account.marketBookRelease(rel);

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• MarketBookAdd — subscribe first
  • MarketBookRelease — unsubscribe when done
  • SymbolInfoTick — top-of-book bid/ask only
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::marketBookGet("EURUSD") returns a vector<BookEntry>.

docs.title: ✅ Unsubscribing from Market Depth (DOM)
docs.text:
Request: close a Level II / DOM subscription for a symbol (MarketBookReleaseData).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::marketBookRelease(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: MarketBookRelease (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: MarketBookRelease(MarketBookReleaseRequest) → MarketBookReleaseReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Closes the DOM subscription opened by MarketBookAdd.
  • Why you need it. Free server resources when you stop watching the book.
  • Sanity check. closed_successfully() is true.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Closes the Market Depth subscription for req.symbol().
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::MarketBookReleaseData marketBookRelease(const pb::MarketBookReleaseRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

MarketBookReleaseRequest { string symbol = 1; }

MarketBookReleaseReply {
  oneof response {
    MarketBookReleaseData data  = 1;   // { bool closed_successfully = 1; }
    Error                 error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description symbol set_symbol("EURUSD") — string Symbol to unsubscribe DOM for.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — MarketBookReleaseData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description ClosedSuccessfully closed_successfully() bool true if the subscription closed.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Always pair with MarketBookAdd. Leaking subscriptions wastes server resources.
  • Idempotent-ish. Releasing a symbol you never subscribed simply returns false.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 🔗 Usage Example
docs.text:
pb::MarketBookReleaseRequest r; r.set_symbol("EURUSD");
std::printf("DOM closed: %s\n", account.marketBookRelease(r).closed_successfully() ? "yes" : "no");

docs.title: RAII guard pattern
docs.text:
struct DomGuard {
    MT5Account& a; std::string sym; bool ok = false;
    DomGuard(MT5Account& acc, std::string s) : a(acc), sym(std::move(s)) {
        pb::MarketBookAddRequest r; r.set_symbol(sym);
        ok = a.marketBookAdd(r).opened_successfully();
    }
    ~DomGuard() {
        if (ok) { pb::MarketBookReleaseRequest r; r.set_symbol(sym); a.marketBookRelease(r); }
    }
};
// Usage: { DomGuard g(account, "EURUSD"); /* poll marketBookGet */ }  // auto-released

docs.text:
• MarketBookAdd — subscribe
  • MarketBookGet — read the book
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::marketBookRelease("EURUSD").

docs.title: MT5Account · Market Depth (DOM) — Overview
docs.text: Level II quotes / order book: subscribe, read, unsubscribe. A three-step lifecycle on the MarketInfo service.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• MarketBookAdd — subscribe to a symbol's order book (opened_successfully).
  • MarketBookGet — read the current book (mql_book_infos of MrpcMqlBookInfo).
  • MarketBookRelease — unsubscribe (closed_successfully).

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English
docs.text:
The order book is a subscription, not a one-shot read:

  1. marketBookAdd("EURUSD") → start receiving depth.
  2. marketBookGet("EURUSD") → snapshot the current levels (poll as needed).
  3. marketBookRelease("EURUSD") → stop and free resources.

Skipping step 1 means step 2 returns an empty book. Skipping step 3 leaks a subscription.

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Returns Start a DOM subscription marketBookAdd bool (opened_successfully()) Read the current book marketBookGet MrpcMqlBookInfo[] Stop the subscription marketBookRelease bool (closed_successfully())

docs.title: 🧱 Book level — MrpcMqlBookInfo
docs.text: Accessor Type Description type() BookType BOOK_TYPE_SELL(0), BOOK_TYPE_BUY(1), BOOK_TYPE_SELL_MARKET(2), BOOK_TYPE_BUY_MARKET(3). price() double Level price. volume() int64 Level volume (integer). volume_real() double Level volume (high precision).

docs.title: ❌ Cross-refs & gotchas
docs.text:
• Not every symbol/broker has DOM. opened_successfully() == false means no Level II data for that instrument.
  • Poll, don't spin. marketBookGet is a snapshot — poll at a sensible interval instead of a tight loop.
  • Clean up. Prefer an RAII guard (see MarketBookRelease) so a subscription is always released.
  • Select the symbol first (SymbolSelect).

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal lifecycle
docs.text:
pb::MarketBookAddRequest add; add.set_symbol("EURUSD");
if (account.marketBookAdd(add).opened_successfully()) {
    pb::MarketBookGetRequest get; get.set_symbol("EURUSD");
    for (const auto& lvl : account.marketBookGet(get).mql_book_infos())
        std::printf("%d %.5f x%lld\n", (int)lvl.type(), lvl.price(), (long long)lvl.volume());

    pb::MarketBookReleaseRequest rel; rel.set_symbol("EURUSD");
    account.marketBookRelease(rel);
}

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Symbols: SymbolInfoTick — top-of-book bid/ask
  • Streaming: OnSymbolTick — push-based quotes
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service DOM helpers return vector<BookEntry>.

docs.title: MT5Account · Additional Methods — Overview
docs.text: Advanced symbol data, trading sessions, margin rates, batch symbol parameters, tick value/size, and bar history — the methods that don't fit the other groups.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• SymbolInfoMarginRate — initial/maintenance margin rate multipliers for a symbol + order type. (MarketInfo)
  • SymbolInfoSessionQuote — quote session [from, to] per weekday. (MarketInfo)
  • SymbolInfoSessionTrade — trade session [from, to] per weekday. (MarketInfo)
  • SymbolParamsMany — full SymbolParameters (100+ fields) for many symbols, paginated. (AccountHelper)
  • TickValueWithSize — tick value / tick size / contract size for P&L, batched. (AccountHelper)
  • PriceHistory — OHLC bars for a symbol/timeframe. (MarketInfo)

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English
docs.text:
• "How much margin does this symbol really need?" → symbolInfoMarginRate() (+ OrderCalcMargin).
  • "When is it quoting / tradable?" → symbolInfoSessionQuote() / symbolInfoSessionTrade().
  • "Give me everything about my whole watchlist." → symbolParamsMany().
  • "What's a point worth in money?" → tickValueWithSize().
  • "I need candles." → priceHistory().

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Returns Margin rate multipliers symbolInfoMarginRate initial_margin_rate, maintenance_margin_rate Quote session window symbolInfoSessionQuote from, to (Timestamp) Trade session window symbolInfoSessionTrade from, to (Timestamp) Full specs for many symbols symbolParamsMany SymbolParameters[] + pagination Tick value/size for P&L tickValueWithSize TickSizeSymbol[] OHLC bars priceHistory PriceBar[]

docs.title: ❌ Cross-refs & gotchas
docs.text:
• Two order-type enums. symbolInfoMarginRate uses ENUM_ORDER_TYPE (ORDER_TYPE_BUY…), while orderSend uses TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE (TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY…) and orderCalc* use ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TF. Same values, different names.
  • Sessions repeat. A weekday can have several sessions — walk session_index from 0.
  • Batch beats loops. symbolParamsMany / tickValueWithSize fetch many symbols at once — prefer them over per-symbol calls.
  • Timeframe is an int code. priceHistory's timeframe is the raw MT5 ENUM_TIMEFRAMES value (H1 = 16385). See Enums Reference.
  • Use UTC fields. priceHistory and the session data expose UTC variants — prefer them.

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippets
docs.text:
// Margin rate
pb::SymbolInfoMarginRateRequest mr; mr.set_symbol("EURUSD"); mr.set_order_type(pb::ORDER_TYPE_BUY);
auto rate = account.symbolInfoMarginRate(mr);
std::printf("initial %.3f\n", rate.initial_margin_rate());

// Tick value
pb::TickValueWithSizeRequest tv; tv.add_symbol_names("EURUSD");
for (const auto& s : account.tickValueWithSize(tv).symbol_tick_size_infos())
    std::printf("%s tickValue %.5f\n", s.name().c_str(), s.tradetickvalue());

// 100 M15 bars
#include <ctime>
std::time_t now = std::time(nullptr);
pb::PriceHistoryRequest ph;
ph.set_symbol("EURUSD"); ph.set_timeframe(15);
ph.set_from_time_utc(now - 100*15*60); ph.set_to_time_utc(now); ph.set_max_bars(100);
std::printf("%d bars\n", account.priceHistory(ph).bars_size());

docs.text:
• Symbols: Symbol Information overview
  • Trading: OrderCalcMargin — turn margin rates into amounts
  • Enums: Enums Reference — timeframe & order-type codes

docs.title: ✅ Getting OHLC Bars (Price History)
docs.text:
Request: historical OHLC bars for a symbol and timeframe (PriceHistoryData).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::priceHistory(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: PriceHistory (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: PriceHistory(PriceHistoryRequest) → PriceHistoryReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Returns a list of OHLC bars (candles) for a symbol/timeframe in a time window.
  • Why you need it. Indicators, backtests, charts — anything that needs candles.
  • Sanity check. bars_size() > 0 for an active symbol and a sane window.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Pull recent candles (e.g. last 200 × H1) to seed an indicator.
  • Export a date range of bars for analysis.
  • Compute volatility/ATR, highs/lows, moving averages.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns OHLC bars for req.symbol() at req.timeframe().
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::PriceHistoryData priceHistory(const pb::PriceHistoryRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

PriceHistoryRequest {
  string symbol        = 1;
  int32  timeframe     = 2;   // MT5 ENUM_TIMEFRAMES code
  int64  from_time     = 3;   // epoch seconds, broker tz
  int64  to_time       = 4;
  int32  max_bars      = 5;
  int64  from_time_utc = 6;   // epoch seconds, UTC
  int64  to_time_utc   = 7;
}

PriceHistoryReply {
  oneof response {
    PriceHistoryData data  = 1;   // { repeated PriceBar bars = 1; }
    Error            error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description symbol set_symbol("EURUSD") Instrument. timeframe set_timeframe(16385) MT5 ENUM_TIMEFRAMES code (M1=1, M5=5, M15=15, H1=16385, D1=16408, …). See Enums Reference. from_time_utc set_from_time_utc(epoch) Window start (UTC epoch seconds). Prefer the *_utc fields. to_time_utc set_to_time_utc(epoch) Window end (UTC epoch seconds). max_bars set_max_bars(500) Cap on the number of bars returned.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — PriceHistoryData
docs.text:
Field C++ accessor Element type Description Bars bars() PriceBar OHLC bars.

Use bars_size(), bars(i), or range-for.

docs.title: PriceBar — fields
docs.text: Accessor Type Description time() int64 Bar open time (epoch seconds, broker tz). time_utc() int64 Bar open time (epoch seconds, UTC). open() double Open price. high() double High price. low() double Low price. close() double Close price. tick_volume() int64 Tick volume. real_volume() int64 Real (exchange) volume. spread() int32 Spread (points) at the bar.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Use UTC fields. from_time_utc / to_time_utc avoid broker-timezone ambiguity; each bar also carries time_utc().
  • Bound the result. Set max_bars so a wide window doesn't return an enormous payload.
  • Large histories. ClientOptions::maxReceiveMessageBytes (default 64 MB) covers big pulls.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 1) Last 200 H1 bars
docs.text:
#include <ctime>
std::time_t now = std::time(nullptr);

pb::PriceHistoryRequest r;
r.set_symbol("EURUSD");
r.set_timeframe(16385);                       // H1
r.set_from_time_utc(now - 200 * 3600);
r.set_to_time_utc(now);
r.set_max_bars(200);

pb::PriceHistoryData d = account.priceHistory(r);
std::printf("Got %d bars\n", d.bars_size());
for (const auto& b : d.bars())
    std::printf("O %.5f H %.5f L %.5f C %.5f\n", b.open(), b.high(), b.low(), b.close());

docs.title: 2) Highest high / lowest low over the window
docs.text:
double hi = -1e18, lo = 1e18;
for (const auto& b : account.priceHistory(r).bars()) {
    hi = std::max(hi, b.high());
    lo = std::min(lo, b.low());
}
std::printf("Range: %.5f .. %.5f\n", lo, hi);

docs.text:
• SymbolInfoTick — the current tick (not bars)
  • Enums Reference — timeframe codes
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::lastBars("EURUSD", Timeframe::H1, 200) returns named Bar structs with UTC times.

docs.title: ✅ Getting Margin Rates for a Symbol
docs.text:
Request: the initial and maintenance margin rates for a symbol and order type (SymbolInfoMarginRateData).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbolInfoMarginRate(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolInfoMarginRate (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolInfoMarginRate(SymbolInfoMarginRateRequest) → SymbolInfoMarginRateReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Returns the margin rate multipliers for a symbol, per order direction.
  • Why you need it. Fine-grained margin modeling (some symbols/directions have different rates).
  • Sanity check. Rates are usually 1.0 for standard FX; they can differ for exotic/leveraged instruments.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns margin rates for req.symbol() and req.order_type().
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::SymbolInfoMarginRateData symbolInfoMarginRate(const pb::SymbolInfoMarginRateRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

SymbolInfoMarginRateRequest {
  string           symbol     = 1;
  ENUM_ORDER_TYPE  order_type = 2;   // BUY/SELL/...
}

SymbolInfoMarginRateReply {
  oneof response {
    SymbolInfoMarginRateData data  = 1;   // { double initial_margin_rate; double maintenance_margin_rate; }
    Error                    error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description symbol set_symbol("EURUSD") Instrument. order_type set_order_type(pb::ORDER_TYPE_BUY) — ENUM_ORDER_TYPE Direction/type (ORDER_TYPE_BUY(0) … ORDER_TYPE_CLOSE_BY(8)).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolInfoMarginRateData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description InitialMarginRate initial_margin_rate() double Initial margin rate multiplier. MaintenanceMarginRate maintenance_margin_rate() double Maintenance margin rate multiplier.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Multipliers, not money. These scale the base margin requirement; combine with OrderCalcMargin for the actual amount.
  • Direction matters. Query BUY and SELL separately if your broker differentiates.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 🔗 Usage Example
docs.text:
pb::SymbolInfoMarginRateRequest r;
r.set_symbol("EURUSD");
r.set_order_type(pb::ORDER_TYPE_BUY);
pb::SymbolInfoMarginRateData d = account.symbolInfoMarginRate(r);
std::printf("initial=%.3f maintenance=%.3f\n",
            d.initial_margin_rate(), d.maintenance_margin_rate());

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• OrderCalcMargin — actual margin for a trade
  • AccountSummary — account margin mode & free margin
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::symbolMarginRate(...) returns a named MarginRate struct.

docs.title: ✅ Getting Quote Session Times
docs.text:
Request: the quoting session window for a symbol on a given weekday (SymbolInfoSessionQuoteData).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbolInfoSessionQuote(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolInfoSessionQuote (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolInfoSessionQuote(SymbolInfoSessionQuoteRequest) → SymbolInfoSessionQuoteReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Returns the quote session [from, to] for a symbol on a weekday and session index.
  • Why you need it. Know when a symbol is quoting (prices update) vs silent.
  • Sanity check. from() < to() for an active session; an empty/zero window means no session.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns the quote session window. Throws ApiError / TransportError.
pb::SymbolInfoSessionQuoteData symbolInfoSessionQuote(const pb::SymbolInfoSessionQuoteRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

SymbolInfoSessionQuoteRequest {
  string    symbol        = 1;
  DayOfWeek day_of_week   = 2;   // SUNDAY=0 … SATURDAY=6
  uint32    session_index = 3;   // 0-based; a day can have multiple sessions
}

SymbolInfoSessionQuoteReply {
  oneof response {
    SymbolInfoSessionQuoteData data  = 1;   // { Timestamp from; Timestamp to; }
    Error                      error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description symbol set_symbol("EURUSD") Instrument. day_of_week set_day_of_week(pb::MONDAY) — DayOfWeek Weekday (SUNDAY(0) … SATURDAY(6)). session_index set_session_index(0) — uint32 Which session of that day (0-based).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolInfoSessionQuoteData
docs.text:
Field C++ accessor C++ type Description From from() google::protobuf::Timestamp Session start. To to() google::protobuf::Timestamp Session end.

Read .seconds() for epoch seconds (time-of-day within the session day).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Multiple sessions per day. Increment session_index (0, 1, …) until the call stops returning a valid window.
  • Quote vs trade sessions differ. Prices may quote outside of tradable hours — see SymbolInfoSessionTrade.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 🔗 Usage Example
docs.text:
pb::SymbolInfoSessionQuoteRequest r;
r.set_symbol("EURUSD");
r.set_day_of_week(pb::MONDAY);
r.set_session_index(0);
pb::SymbolInfoSessionQuoteData d = account.symbolInfoSessionQuote(r);
std::printf("Quote session: %lld .. %lld\n",
            (long long)d.from().seconds(), (long long)d.to().seconds());

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• SymbolInfoSessionTrade — the tradable session window
  • SymbolInfoInteger — SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE, session counts
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::sessionQuote(...) returns a named SessionTime struct (UTC).

docs.title: ✅ Getting Trade Session Times
docs.text:
Request: the tradable session window for a symbol on a given weekday (SymbolInfoSessionTradeData).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbolInfoSessionTrade(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolInfoSessionTrade (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolInfoSessionTrade(SymbolInfoSessionTradeRequest) → SymbolInfoSessionTradeReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Returns the trade session [from, to] for a symbol on a weekday and session index.
  • Why you need it. Know when you can actually place/modify orders (vs merely watch quotes).
  • Sanity check. from() < to() for an active tradable session.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns the trade session window. Throws ApiError / TransportError.
pb::SymbolInfoSessionTradeData symbolInfoSessionTrade(const pb::SymbolInfoSessionTradeRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

SymbolInfoSessionTradeRequest {
  string    symbol        = 1;
  DayOfWeek day_of_week   = 2;   // SUNDAY=0 … SATURDAY=6
  uint32    session_index = 3;
}

SymbolInfoSessionTradeReply {
  oneof response {
    SymbolInfoSessionTradeData data  = 1;   // { Timestamp from; Timestamp to; }
    Error                      error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description symbol set_symbol("EURUSD") Instrument. day_of_week set_day_of_week(pb::MONDAY) — DayOfWeek Weekday (SUNDAY(0) … SATURDAY(6)). session_index set_session_index(0) — uint32 Which session of that day (0-based).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolInfoSessionTradeData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor C++ type Description From from() google::protobuf::Timestamp Tradable session start. To to() google::protobuf::Timestamp Tradable session end.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Trade ⊆ quote. Tradable hours are usually within (or equal to) the quote session; compare with SymbolInfoSessionQuote.
  • Gate your orders. Use this to avoid sending orders when the market is closed (retcode "market closed", 10018).
  • Multiple sessions per day. Walk session_index (0, 1, …).
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 🔗 Usage Example
docs.text:
pb::SymbolInfoSessionTradeRequest r;
r.set_symbol("EURUSD");
r.set_day_of_week(pb::FRIDAY);
r.set_session_index(0);
pb::SymbolInfoSessionTradeData d = account.symbolInfoSessionTrade(r);
std::printf("Trade session: %lld .. %lld\n",
            (long long)d.from().seconds(), (long long)d.to().seconds());

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• SymbolInfoSessionQuote — the quoting session window
  • OrderSend — placing orders (fails if the market is closed)
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::sessionTrade(...) returns a named SessionTime struct (UTC).

docs.title: ✅ Getting Full Parameters for Many Symbols
docs.text:
Request: detailed parameters for many symbols in one paginated call (SymbolParamsManyData) — every field per symbol, no per-property round-trips.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbolParamsMany(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: SymbolParamsMany (defined in mt5-term-api-account-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: SymbolParamsMany(SymbolParamsManyRequest) → SymbolParamsManyReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Returns a rich SymbolParameters record (100+ fields) for each matching symbol, paginated.
  • Why you need it. The efficient way to snapshot specs for a whole watchlist — far cheaper than many symbolInfo* calls.
  • Sanity check. symbols_total() ≥ symbol_infos_size().

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns detailed parameters for matching symbols (paginated).
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::SymbolParamsManyData symbolParamsMany(const pb::SymbolParamsManyRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

SymbolParamsManyRequest {
  string                          symbol_name    = 1;   // filter (empty = all)
  AH_SYMBOL_PARAMS_MANY_SORT_TYPE sort_type      = 2;
  int32                           page_number    = 3;
  int32                           items_per_page = 4;
}

SymbolParamsManyReply {
  oneof response {
    SymbolParamsManyData data  = 1;
    Error                error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description symbol_name set_symbol_name("EUR") — string Filter by name (empty = all symbols). sort_type set_sort_type(...) — sort enum Result ordering. page_number set_page_number(0) — int32 Zero-based page index. items_per_page set_items_per_page(50) — int32 Page size.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolParamsManyData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor Type Description SymbolInfos symbol_infos() repeated SymbolParameters One rich record per symbol. SymbolsTotal symbols_total() int32 Total matching symbols (all pages). PageNumber page_number() int32 Current page. ItemsPerPage items_per_page() int32 Page size echoed back.

docs.title: SymbolParameters — a sample of the fields
docs.text:
Over 100 fields per symbol; commonly used ones include:

Accessor Type Description name() string Symbol name. digits() int Price decimal digits. point() double Point size. bid() / ask() double Current quotes. volume_min() / volume_max() / volume_step() double Lot limits. trade_tick_value() / trade_tick_size() double Tick value/size. currency_base() / currency_profit() / currency_margin() string Currencies.

The full field set mirrors MT5's symbol specification; reach for the friendly MT5Service::symbolParams() struct when you want named C++ fields without protobuf.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Batch, don't loop. One symbolParamsMany call replaces dozens of symbolInfoDouble/Integer/String calls per symbol.
  • Paginate. Use page_number / items_per_page; read symbols_total() to know how many pages.
  • Large payloads. Covered by ClientOptions::maxReceiveMessageBytes (64 MB default).
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 🔗 Usage Example
docs.text:
pb::SymbolParamsManyRequest r;
r.set_symbol_name("");          // all symbols
r.set_page_number(0);
r.set_items_per_page(50);

pb::SymbolParamsManyData d = account.symbolParamsMany(r);
std::printf("Total symbols: %d (page has %d)\n", d.symbols_total(), d.symbol_infos_size());
for (const auto& s : d.symbol_infos())
    std::printf("%-10s digits=%d\n", s.name().c_str(), s.digits());

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• SymbolInfoDouble / SymbolInfoInteger / SymbolInfoString — single-property reads
  • TickValueWithSize — just the tick value/size for P&L
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::symbolParams("EURUSD") returns a named SymbolInfo.

docs.title: ✅ Getting Tick Value & Size (for P&L)
docs.text:
Request: tick value, tick size and contract size for one or more symbols (TickValueWithSizeData) — the constants that turn points into money.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::tickValueWithSize(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: TickValueWithSize (defined in mt5-term-api-account-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: TickValueWithSize(TickValueWithSizeRequest) → TickValueWithSizeReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Returns tick value / tick size / contract size per symbol in a single batched call.
  • Why you need it. Position sizing and P&L math: money per point, risk per lot.
  • Sanity check. tradetickvalue() for a USD-quoted FX pair ≈ $1 per point per lot (varies by symbol).

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Returns tick value/size info for the requested symbols.
// Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.
pb::TickValueWithSizeData tickValueWithSize(const pb::TickValueWithSizeRequest& req);

Request / Reply:

TickValueWithSizeRequest { repeated string symbol_names = 1; }

TickValueWithSizeReply {
  oneof response {
    TickValueWithSizeData data  = 1;   // { repeated TickSizeSymbol symbol_tick_size_infos = 1; }
    Error                 error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
⬆️ Output — TickValueWithSizeData
docs.text: Field C++ accessor Element type Description SymbolTickSizeInfos symbol_tick_size_infos() TickSizeSymbol One record per symbol.

docs.title: TickSizeSymbol — fields
docs.text: Accessor Type Description index() int32 Index of the symbol in the request. name() string Symbol name. tradecontractsize() double Contract size (units per lot). tradeticksize() double Minimal price change (tick size). tradetickvalue() double Value of one tick in the account currency. tradetickvalueprofit() double Tick value for a profitable move. tradetickvalueloss() double Tick value for a losing move.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Money per point ≈ tradetickvalue() × (SYMBOL_POINT / tradeticksize()). For many FX symbols point == tick size, so it's just tradetickvalue() per point per lot.
  • Batch friendly. Pass your whole watchlist at once instead of one call per symbol.
  • Profit vs loss tick value can differ for some instruments — use the matching one for precise risk math.
  • Automatic reconnection / timeout / exceptions as for every MT5Account method.

docs.title: 🔗 Usage Example
docs.text:
pb::TickValueWithSizeRequest r;
r.add_symbol_names("EURUSD");
r.add_symbol_names("XAUUSD");

for (const auto& s : account.tickValueWithSize(r).symbol_tick_size_infos())
    std::printf("%-8s tickValue=%.5f tickSize=%.5f contract=%.1f\n",
                s.name().c_str(), s.tradetickvalue(), s.tradeticksize(), s.tradecontractsize());

docs.title: Risk-based lot sizing
docs.text:
// lots so that `stopPoints` of adverse move ≈ `riskMoney`
double lotsForRisk(const pb::TickSizeSymbol& s, double stopPoints, double riskMoney) {
    double perPointPerLot = s.tradetickvalue();     // assuming point == tick size
    return riskMoney / (stopPoints * perPointPerLot);
}

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• SymbolInfoDouble — single tick-value/point reads
  • OrderCalcProfit — server-side profit for a move
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::tickValueWithSize({"EURUSD","GBPUSD"}) returns named structs.

docs.title: ✅ Streaming Position Profit Updates
docs.text:
Subscribe: receive periodic profit/loss snapshots for your positions (OnPositionProfitData) on a timer.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::onPositionProfit(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Proto definition: OnPositionProfit (defined in mt5-term-api-subscriptions.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Method: OnPositionProfit(OnPositionProfitRequest) → stream OnPositionProfitData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A timer-driven stream: every timer_period_milliseconds the server pushes which positions are new/updated/deleted, with their profit.
  • Why you need it. Live P/L dashboards and profit-based exits without polling.
  • Lifecycle. Returns a std::unique_ptr<AccountStream> — keep it alive; stop() to end.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Streams periodic position-profit updates to `callback` on a background thread.
// Throws ApiError / TransportError while opening.
std::unique_ptr<AccountStream> onPositionProfit(
    const pb::OnPositionProfitRequest& req,
    std::function<void(const pb::OnPositionProfitData&)> callback);

Request / Stream:

OnPositionProfitRequest {
  int32 timer_period_milliseconds = 1;   // how often to push
  bool  ignore_empty_data         = 2;   // skip ticks with no changes
}

OnPositionProfitData {
  MT5_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE type                      = 1;
  repeated OnPositionProfitPositionInfo new_positions     = 2;
  repeated OnPositionProfitPositionInfo updated_positions = 3;
  repeated OnPositionProfitPositionInfo deleted_positions = 4;
  OnEventAccountInfo            account_info              = 5;
  string                        terminal_instance_guid_id = 6;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description timer_period_milliseconds set_timer_period_milliseconds(1000) Push interval in ms. ignore_empty_data set_ignore_empty_data(true) If true, suppress pushes when nothing changed.

docs.title: ⬆️ Payload — OnPositionProfitData
docs.text: Accessor Type Description new_positions() repeated OnPositionProfitPositionInfo Positions that appeared. updated_positions() repeated OnPositionProfitPositionInfo Positions whose profit changed. deleted_positions() repeated OnPositionProfitPositionInfo Positions that closed. account_info() OnEventAccountInfo Account snapshot. terminal_instance_guid_id() string Terminal session id.

docs.title: OnPositionProfitPositionInfo
docs.text: Accessor Type Description index() uint Index within the batch. ticket() uint64 Position ticket. position_symbol() string Symbol. profit() double Current profit.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Set a sane interval. 500–2000 ms is usually plenty; very small periods add load for little benefit.
  • Use ignore_empty_data to avoid empty ticks when nothing changed.
  • Callback on the reader thread — don't block; guard shared state.
  • Keep the handle alive; stop() to end. Handle API: running(), count(), lastError().
  • See gRPC Streaming.

docs.title: 🔗 Usage Example
docs.text:
#include <thread>
#include <chrono>

pb::OnPositionProfitRequest req;
req.set_timer_period_milliseconds(1000);
req.set_ignore_empty_data(true);

auto stream = account.onPositionProfit(req, [](const pb::OnPositionProfitData& d) {
    for (const auto& p : d.updated_positions())
        std::printf("#%llu %s profit %.2f\n",
                    (unsigned long long)p.ticket(), p.position_symbol().c_str(), p.profit());
});

std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(30));
stream->stop();

docs.title: 🧱 Enums used (in the returned data)
docs.text:
Field Enum Values type() MT5_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE OrderProfit(0), OrderUpdate(1)

Full catalog: Enums Reference.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets — periodic ticket snapshots (lighter)
  • OpenedOrders — full on-demand snapshot
  • gRPC Streaming
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::streamPositionProfit(cb) delivers named PositionProfitEvent structs.

docs.title: ✅ Streaming Position & Pending-Order Ticket Snapshots
docs.text:
Subscribe: receive periodic lists of open position tickets and pending-order tickets (OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsData) on a timer — a lightweight change feed.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::onPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Proto definition: OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets (defined in mt5-term-api-subscriptions.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Method: OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets(OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsRequest) → stream OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A timer-driven stream of just the ticket numbers currently open (positions + pending orders), with a server timestamp.
  • Why you need it. The cheapest way to notice something opened/closed — diff successive snapshots.
  • Lifecycle. Returns a std::unique_ptr<AccountStream> — keep it alive; stop() to end.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Streams periodic ticket snapshots to `callback` on a background thread.
// Throws ApiError / TransportError while opening.
std::unique_ptr<AccountStream> onPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets(
    const pb::OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsRequest& req,
    std::function<void(const pb::OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsData&)> callback);

Request / Stream:

OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsRequest {
  int32 timer_period_milliseconds = 1;
}

OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsData {
  repeated uint64 position_tickets          = 1;
  repeated uint64 pending_order_tickets     = 2;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp server_time     = 3;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp server_time_utc = 4;
  string          terminal_instance_guid_id = 5;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Field C++ setter / type Description timer_period_milliseconds set_timer_period_milliseconds(1000) Push interval in ms.

docs.title: ⬆️ Payload — OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsData
docs.text:
Accessor Type Description position_tickets() repeated uint64 Open position tickets. pending_order_tickets() repeated uint64 Pending order tickets. server_time() Timestamp Snapshot time (broker tz). server_time_utc() Timestamp Snapshot time (UTC). terminal_instance_guid_id() string Terminal session id.

Use position_tickets_size() / pending_order_tickets_size() and indexed/range access.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Snapshot, not deltas. Each message is the current full list — compute diffs against the previous one to detect opens/closes.
  • Lightest stream. Only tickets + timestamp; pair with OpenedOrders when a change warrants full detail.
  • Callback on the reader thread — don't block; guard shared state.
  • Keep the handle alive; stop() to end. Handle API: running(), count(), lastError().
  • See gRPC Streaming.

docs.title: 🔗 Usage Example
docs.text:
#include <thread>
#include <chrono>
#include <set>

std::set<uint64_t> prev;

pb::OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsRequest req;
req.set_timer_period_milliseconds(1000);

auto stream = account.onPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets(req,
    [&](const pb::OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsData& d) {
        std::set<uint64_t> now(d.position_tickets().begin(), d.position_tickets().end());
        for (uint64_t t : now)  if (!prev.count(t)) std::printf("opened #%llu\n", (unsigned long long)t);
        for (uint64_t t : prev) if (!now.count(t))  std::printf("closed #%llu\n", (unsigned long long)t);
        prev.swap(now);
    });

std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(30));
stream->stop();

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• OnPositionProfit — periodic P/L (heavier)
  • OpenedOrdersTickets — one-shot ticket list
  • gRPC Streaming
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::streamTickets(cb) delivers a named TicketsSnapshot struct.

docs.title: ✅ Streaming Live Ticks
docs.text:
Subscribe: receive a callback for every new tick on one or more symbols (OnSymbolTickData), on a background thread.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::onSymbolTick(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Proto definition: OnSymbolTick (defined in mt5-term-api-subscriptions.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Method: OnSymbolTick(OnSymbolTickRequest) → stream OnSymbolTickData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A server stream: the SDK reads ticks on a background thread and calls your callback for each one.
  • Why you need it. Push-based live prices — no polling loop.
  • Lifecycle. The call returns a std::unique_ptr<AccountStream> handle: keep it alive to keep receiving; stop() (or destroying it) ends the subscription.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Opens a tick stream for req.symbol_names(). `callback` runs on a background
// reader thread for every OnSymbolTickData. Returns a handle that owns the stream.
// Throws ApiError / TransportError while opening.
std::unique_ptr<AccountStream> onSymbolTick(
    const pb::OnSymbolTickRequest& req,
    std::function<void(const pb::OnSymbolTickData&)> callback);

Request / Stream:

OnSymbolTickRequest { repeated string symbol_names = 1; }

// server streams OnSymbolTickData:
OnSymbolTickData {
  MrpcSubscriptionMqlTick symbol_tick               = 1;
  string                  terminal_instance_guid_id = 2;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
Field C++ setter / type Description symbol_names add_symbol_names("EURUSD") (repeated) Symbols to stream (one or many).

Prefer one stream with many symbols over many single-symbol streams.

docs.title: ⬆️ Payload — OnSymbolTickData
docs.text: Accessor Type Description symbol_tick() MrpcSubscriptionMqlTick The tick (see below). terminal_instance_guid_id() string Terminal session id.

docs.title: MrpcSubscriptionMqlTick
docs.text: Accessor Type Description symbol() string Symbol. bid() / ask() double Quote. volume() uint64 Volume. time() Timestamp Tick time (broker tz). time_utc() Timestamp Tick time (UTC). time_msc() / time_msc_utc() int64 Milliseconds (broker / UTC). flags() uint32 Tick change flags.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Callback runs on the reader thread. Don't block it — push slow work to another thread/queue. Guard shared state (std::atomic, a mutex).
  • Keep the handle alive. If the unique_ptr is destroyed, the stream stops. Store it for as long as you want ticks.
  • Exceptions in the callback are swallowed by the reader — handle errors inside it.
  • AccountStream handle: stop(), running(), count() (payloads received), lastError().
  • See the gRPC Streaming guide.

docs.title: 1) Stream two symbols for a while
docs.text:
#include <thread>
#include <chrono>
#include <atomic>

std::atomic<int> ticks{0};

pb::OnSymbolTickRequest req;
req.add_symbol_names("EURUSD");
req.add_symbol_names("GBPUSD");

auto stream = account.onSymbolTick(req, [&](const pb::OnSymbolTickData& d) {
    const auto& t = d.symbol_tick();
    std::printf("%s  %.5f / %.5f\n", t.symbol().c_str(), t.bid(), t.ask());
    ++ticks;
});

std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(10));
stream->stop();
std::printf("Received %d ticks\n", ticks.load());

docs.title: 2) Keep only the latest price per symbol
docs.text:
#include <map>
#include <mutex>
std::mutex m;
std::map<std::string, double> lastBid;

auto stream = account.onSymbolTick(req, [&](const pb::OnSymbolTickData& d) {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(m);
    lastBid[d.symbol_tick().symbol()] = d.symbol_tick().bid();
});

docs.title: ✅ Streaming Trade Events
docs.text:
Subscribe: receive a callback whenever positions/orders change (OnTradeData) — opened, closed, modified.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::onTrade(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Proto definition: OnTrade (defined in mt5-term-api-subscriptions.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Method: OnTrade(OnTradeRequest) → stream OnTradeData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A server stream of trade events: new/disappeared positions, orders and history deals.
  • Why you need it. React immediately to fills, closes and modifications instead of polling OpenedOrders.
  • Lifecycle. Returns a std::unique_ptr<AccountStream> — keep it alive; stop() to end.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Streams trade events to `callback` on a background reader thread.
// Throws ApiError / TransportError while opening.
std::unique_ptr<AccountStream> onTrade(
    const pb::OnTradeRequest& req,
    std::function<void(const pb::OnTradeData&)> callback);

Request / Stream:

OnTradeRequest {}   // (empty)

// server streams OnTradeData:
OnTradeData {
  MT5_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE type                      = 1;
  OnTadeEventData               event_data                = 2;
  OnEventAccountInfo            account_info              = 3;
  string                        terminal_instance_guid_id = 4;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description req const pb::OnTradeRequest& Empty request message.

docs.title: ⬆️ Payload — OnTradeData
docs.text: Accessor Type Description type() MT5_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE Event group/type. event_data() OnTadeEventData What changed (see below). account_info() OnEventAccountInfo Account snapshot at the event. terminal_instance_guid_id() string Terminal session id.

docs.title: OnTadeEventData — "what changed" lists
docs.text:
Each is a repeated collection (*_size() + indexed access):

Accessor Description new_positions() Positions that appeared. disappeared_positions() Positions that closed. new_orders() / disappeared_orders() Pending orders added/removed. new_history_orders() / disappeared_history_orders() History order changes. new_history_deals() / disappeared_history_deals() History deal changes.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Event-driven, not a full snapshot. Each message carries deltas (what changed). Keep your own state, or re-read OpenedOrders when you need the full picture.
  • Callback on the reader thread — don't block; guard shared state.
  • Keep the handle alive; stop() to end. Handle API: running(), count(), lastError().
  • See gRPC Streaming.

docs.title: 🔗 Usage Example
docs.text:
#include <thread>
#include <chrono>

pb::OnTradeRequest req;
auto stream = account.onTrade(req, [](const pb::OnTradeData& d) {
    const auto& e = d.event_data();
    if (e.new_positions_size() > 0)
        std::printf("Opened %d position(s)\n", e.new_positions_size());
    if (e.disappeared_positions_size() > 0)
        std::printf("Closed %d position(s)\n", e.disappeared_positions_size());
});

std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::minutes(1));
stream->stop();

docs.title: 🧱 Enums used (in the returned data)
docs.text:
Field Enum Values type() MT5_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE OrderProfit(0), OrderUpdate(1)

The nested order/position/deal infos also carry their own type/state/entry enums (BMT5_ENUM_POSITION_TYPE, BMT5_ENUM_ORDER_STATE, BMT5_ENUM_DEAL_ENTRY_TYPE, …). Full catalog: Enums Reference.
