  • OnPositionProfit — periodic P/L updates
  • OpenedOrders — full current snapshot
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::streamTradeUpdates(cb) delivers named TradeEvent structs.

docs.title: ✅ Streaming the Trade-Transaction Log
docs.text:
Subscribe: receive a callback for every trade transaction (OnTradeTransactionData) — the complete, low-level audit trail of request → transaction → result.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::onTradeTransaction(...) (from #include <metarpc/mt5_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Proto definition: OnTradeTransaction (defined in mt5-term-api-subscriptions.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Method: OnTradeTransaction(OnTradeTransactionRequest) → stream OnTradeTransactionData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The most detailed trade stream: each message carries the originating request, the transaction, and the result.
  • Why you need it. Precise audit/reconciliation — matching exactly what the server did to each request.
  • Lifecycle. Returns a std::unique_ptr<AccountStream> — keep it alive; stop() to end.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
// Streams the detailed transaction log to `callback` on a background thread.
// Throws ApiError / TransportError while opening.
std::unique_ptr<AccountStream> onTradeTransaction(
    const pb::OnTradeTransactionRequest& req,
    std::function<void(const pb::OnTradeTransactionData&)> callback);

Stream payload:

OnTradeTransactionData {
  MT5_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE type                      = 1;
  MqlTradeTransaction           trade_transaction         = 2;
  MqlTradeRequest               trade_request             = 3;
  MqlTradeResult                trade_result              = 4;
  OnEventAccountInfo            account_info              = 5;
  string                        terminal_instance_guid_id = 6;
}

docs.title: ⬆️ Payload — OnTradeTransactionData
docs.text: Accessor Type Description type() MT5_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE Event group/type. trade_transaction() MqlTradeTransaction The transaction (deal/order/position changes). trade_request() MqlTradeRequest The originating request (if any). trade_result() MqlTradeResult The server's result (retcode, deal, order). account_info() OnEventAccountInfo Account snapshot at the event. terminal_instance_guid_id() string Terminal session id.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Finer-grained than OnTrade. Use this when you need the request/result pairing; use OnTrade for simpler "what's open changed" logic.
  • Callback on the reader thread — don't block; guard shared state.
  • Keep the handle alive; stop() to end. Handle API: running(), count(), lastError().
  • See gRPC Streaming.

docs.title: 🔗 Usage Example
docs.text:
#include <thread>
#include <chrono>

pb::OnTradeTransactionRequest req;
auto stream = account.onTradeTransaction(req, [](const pb::OnTradeTransactionData& d) {
    std::printf("txn type=%d, result retcode=%u\n",
                (int)d.type(), d.trade_result().trade_return_code());
});

std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::minutes(1));
stream->stop();

docs.title: 🧱 Enums used (in the returned data)
docs.text:
Field Enum Values type() MT5_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE OrderProfit(0), OrderUpdate(1)

trade_result().trade_return_code() is a trade retcode (10009 = DONE), not an enum. The embedded MqlTradeRequest / MqlTradeTransaction carry order-type / filling / time enums — full catalog: Enums Reference · Return Codes.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• OnTrade — higher-level position/order change events
  • OrderSend — the requests that produce these transactions
  • gRPC Streaming
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service::streamTransactions(cb) delivers named TransactionEvent structs.

docs.title: MT5Account · Streaming Methods — Overview
docs.text: Real-time server streams: ticks, trade events, the transaction log, profit updates, and ticket snapshots. All run on the SubscriptionService and deliver to a callback on a background thread.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• OnSymbolTick — live ticks for one or more symbols.
  • OnTrade — position/order change events (opened, closed, modified).
  • OnTradeTransaction — detailed transaction log (request + transaction + result).
  • OnPositionProfit — periodic profit/loss updates (timer-driven).
  • OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets — periodic ticket snapshots (lightweight).

docs.title: 🧭 The streaming model (read this first)
docs.text:
Every onX(req, callback) returns a std::unique_ptr<AccountStream>:

auto stream = account.onSymbolTick(req, [](const pb::OnSymbolTickData& d){ /* ... */ });
// ... stream is live on a background thread ...
stream->stop();         // end the subscription
  • The SDK reads the server stream on a dedicated background thread and calls your callback for each payload.
  • Keep the handle alive. Destroying the unique_ptr (or calling stop()) cancels the stream.
  • The callback runs on the reader thread. Don't block it — push slow work elsewhere and guard shared state (std::atomic / mutex).
  • Exceptions thrown by the callback are swallowed — handle errors inside it.
  • Payload times are raw broker server time (many payloads also carry a *_utc field).

AccountStream handle API: stop(), running(), count() (payloads received so far), lastError().

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you want… Use Shape Live prices onSymbolTick event per tick React to fills/closes/modifies onTrade delta events Full audit of each transaction onTradeTransaction request + transaction + result Live P/L of positions onPositionProfit timer, new/updated/deleted Cheap "what tickets exist" feed onPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets timer, full ticket snapshot

docs.title: ❌ Cross-refs & gotchas
docs.text:
• Deltas vs snapshots. onTrade / onPositionProfit report changes; onPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets sends a full ticket list each tick (diff it yourself).
  • One stream, many symbols. For ticks, prefer a single onSymbolTick with several symbols over many single-symbol streams.
  • Pick a sensible timer. onPositionProfit / onPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets take timer_period_milliseconds — 500–2000 ms is usually enough; set ignore_empty_data where available.
  • Lifetime bugs are the #1 pitfall. If a stream "stops working", check you still hold its handle.

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal pattern
docs.text:
#include <thread>
#include <chrono>

pb::OnSymbolTickRequest req;
req.add_symbol_names("EURUSD");

auto stream = account.onSymbolTick(req, [](const pb::OnSymbolTickData& d) {
    std::printf("%s %.5f/%.5f\n",
                d.symbol_tick().symbol().c_str(),
                d.symbol_tick().bid(), d.symbol_tick().ask());
});

std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(10));
stream->stop();

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Guide: gRPC Streaming — lifecycle, threading, backpressure
  • Concurrency: Concurrency Model — unary vs stream, running work in parallel
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service stream helpers deliver named event structs with UTC times.

docs.title: MT5Service — Account Methods (Mid-Level)
docs.text:
4 methods for account properties without protobuf ceremony. They wrap the MT5Account Account Information RPCs and return clean C++ values.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — wrappers over MT5Account returning native C++ types.

Implementation: src/mt5_service.cpp (header include/metarpc/mt5_service.hpp).

docs.title: 🎯 Why these exist
docs.text:
// Low-level (MT5Account): build request, unpack Data
namespace pb = mt5_term_api;
pb::AccountInfoDoubleRequest r; r.set_property_id(pb::ACCOUNT_BALANCE);
double balance = account.accountInfoDouble(r).requested_value();

// Mid-level (MT5Service): one call, plain value
double balance = service.accountInfoDouble(pb::ACCOUNT_BALANCE);
  • ✅ Returns double / int64_t / std::string / AccountInfo directly
  • ✅ Builds the request for you, unpacks the Data
  • ✅ accountSummary() fills serverTimeUtc already converted

docs.title: 📋 The 4 methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Low-level equivalent accountSummary() AccountInfo MT5Account::accountSummary() accountInfoDouble(propertyId) double accountInfoDouble(req) → requested_value() accountInfoInteger(propertyId) int64_t accountInfoInteger(req) → requested_value() accountInfoString(propertyId) std::string accountInfoString(req) → requested_value()

propertyId is a plain int — pass the protobuf enum value (e.g. pb::ACCOUNT_BALANCE), which converts to int implicitly.

docs.title: 📦 AccountInfo (DTO)
docs.text:
struct AccountInfo {
    int64_t      login;
    std::string  currency;
    double       balance, equity, credit;
    int64_t      leverage;
    std::string  name, company;
    TradeMode    tradeMode;          // Demo / Contest / Real
    int64_t      serverTime;         // unix seconds, broker clock (raw)
    int64_t      serverTimeUtc;      // same instant in UTC
    int64_t      utcShiftMinutes;    // server clock minus UTC
    std::string  server;             // broker server name used to connect
};

docs.title: 1) accountSummary()
docs.text:
AccountInfo accountSummary();

All account info in one call — use this for 2+ properties.

docs.title: 2) accountInfoDouble(int propertyId)
docs.text:
double accountInfoDouble(int propertyId);

Common ids (AccountInfoDoublePropertyType): ACCOUNT_BALANCE(0), ACCOUNT_CREDIT(1), ACCOUNT_PROFIT(2), ACCOUNT_EQUITY(3), ACCOUNT_MARGIN(4), ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE(5), ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL(6) … (14 total).

docs.title: 3) accountInfoInteger(int propertyId)
docs.text:
int64_t accountInfoInteger(int propertyId);

Common ids (AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType): ACCOUNT_LOGIN(0), ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE(1), ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE(2), ACCOUNT_TRADE_ALLOWED(5), ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE(7) … (11 total).

docs.title: 4) accountInfoString(int propertyId)
docs.text:
std::string accountInfoString(int propertyId);

Ids (AccountInfoStringPropertyType): ACCOUNT_NAME(0), ACCOUNT_SERVER(1), ACCOUNT_CURRENCY(2), ACCOUNT_COMPANY(3).

docs.title: Balance + equity (one call)
docs.text:
AccountInfo s = service.accountSummary();
std::printf("Balance %.2f %s | Equity %.2f | Lev 1:%lld | Broker %s\n",
            s.balance, s.currency.c_str(), s.equity,
            (long long)s.leverage, s.company.c_str());

docs.title: Single property
docs.text:
namespace pb = mt5_term_api;
double freeMargin = service.accountInfoDouble(pb::ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE);
if (freeMargin < 100) std::puts("⚠️ low free margin");

docs.title: Demo vs real guard
docs.text:
if (service.accountInfoInteger(pb::ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE) == 2 /* REAL */)
    throw std::runtime_error("refusing to run on a REAL account");

docs.title: Balance monitor
docs.text:
#include <thread>
#include <chrono>
for (;;) {
    std::printf("Balance: %.2f\n", service.accountInfoDouble(pb::ACCOUNT_BALANCE));
    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(5));
}

docs.title: 🔧 When to use which
docs.text:
1. One property → accountInfoDouble/Integer/String.
  2. Two or more → accountSummary() (already has everything).
  3. Dashboard / report → accountSummary().

docs.title: MT5Service — Symbol Methods (Mid-Level)
docs.text:
16 methods for symbols, quotes, parameters, sessions, tick value, and bars — all returning friendly C++ structs with UTC times. Wrappers over MT5Account Symbol Information and Additional Methods.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL. Implementation: src/mt5_service.cpp.

docs.title: 📋 The methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Description symbolsTotal(selectedOnly=false) int Count of symbols (all or Market Watch) symbolExist(symbol) bool Does the broker know the symbol symbolName(index, selectedOnly=false) std::string Name by index symbolSelect(symbol, select=true) bool Add/remove in Market Watch symbolIsSynchronized(symbol) bool Is its data synchronized symbolList() std::vector<std::string> All symbol names symbolInfoTick(symbol) Tick Latest tick (UTC) symbolParams(symbol) SymbolInfo Recommended — full spec, one symbol symbolParamsMany(nameFilter="") std::vector<SymbolInfo> Full spec, many symbols symbolInfoDouble(symbol, propertyId) double One double property symbolInfoInteger(symbol, propertyId) int64_t One integer property symbolInfoString(symbol, propertyId) std::string One string property symbolInfoMarginRate(symbol, orderType) MarginRate Initial/maintenance margin rates symbolInfoSessionQuote(symbol, day, idx=0) SessionTime Quote session window symbolInfoSessionTrade(symbol, day, idx=0) SessionTime Trade session window tickValueWithSize(symbols) std::vector<TickValueSize> Tick value/size for P&L priceHistory(symbol, tf, from, to, maxBars=0) std::vector<Bar> OHLC bars in a window lastBars(symbol, tf, count) std::vector<Bar> Newest count bars

docs.title: 📦 DTOs
docs.text:
struct Tick {                      // symbolInfoTick()
    std::string symbol; int64_t time, timeMsc;   // UTC seconds / ms
    double bid, ask, last, volume; uint32_t flags;
    bool twoSided() const;         // bid>0 && ask>0 && ask>bid
};

struct SymbolInfo {                // symbolParams() / symbolParamsMany()
    std::string name, description, path;
    std::string currencyBase, currencyProfit, currencyMargin;
    int digits; double point, bid, ask; int spread;
    double contractSize, tickSize, tickValue;
    double volumeMin, volumeMax, volumeStep, volumeLimit;
    int stopsLevel, freezeLevel, tradeMode, tradeCalcMode, tradeExeMode, swapMode;
    double swapLong, swapShort; std::vector<int> fillingModes;
    bool visible, selected, exist; int64_t time;
};

struct Bar { int64_t time; double open, high, low, close;   // time = UTC seconds
             int64_t tickVolume, realVolume; int spread; };

struct MarginRate   { double initial, maintenance; };
struct SessionTime  { int64_t from, to; };                   // UTC seconds
struct TickValueSize{ std::string symbol; double tickValue, tickValueProfit,
                      tickValueLoss, tickSize, contractSize; };

Timeframe enum: M1,M2,M3,M4,M5,M6,M10,M12,M15,M20,M30, H1,H2,H3,H4,H6,H8,H12, D1,W1,MN1 (raw MQL5 ENUM_TIMEFRAMES values).

docs.title: Current price
docs.text:
Tick t = service.symbolInfoTick("EURUSD");
std::printf("%.5f / %.5f (spread %.5f)\n", t.bid, t.ask, t.ask - t.bid);

std::printf("%s: digits=%d point=%.5f volMin=%.2f step=%.2f tickValue=%.5f\n",
            s.name.c_str(), s.digits, s.point, s.volumeMin, s.volumeStep, s.tickValue);

docs.title: Make a symbol quotable, then quote it
docs.text:

    Tick t = service.symbolInfoTick("USDMXN");
    std::printf("USDMXN %.5f/%.5f\n", t.bid, t.ask);
}

docs.title: Last 100 H1 bars
docs.text:

std::printf("%zu bars, last close %.5f\n", bars.size(), bars.empty() ? 0 : bars.back().close);

for (const TickValueSize& v : service.tickValueWithSize({"EURUSD","XAUUSD"}))
    std::printf("%s tickValue=%.5f tickSize=%.5f\n",
                v.symbol.c_str(), v.tickValue, v.tickSize);

1. Need everything about a symbol → symbolParams() (one call vs 10+).
  2. One field only → symbolInfoDouble/Integer/String.
  3. Whole watchlist → symbolParamsMany().
  4. Just the price → symbolInfoTick().
  5. Candles → lastBars() / priceHistory().

docs.title: MT5Service — Position & Orders Methods (Mid-Level)
docs.text:
6 methods for live positions, pending orders, ticket lists and history — all returning friendly C++ structs with UTC times. Wrappers over MT5Account Positions & Orders.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL. Implementation: src/mt5_service.cpp.

docs.title: 📋 The methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Description positionsTotal() int Count of open positions openedOrders() OpenedOrders Positions and pending orders (friendly) positions(magic=-1) std::vector<Position> Open positions (optionally by magic) openedOrdersTickets() OpenedTickets Lightweight — ticket numbers only orderHistory(from, to) std::vector<HistoryItem> Orders/deals history (UTC window) positionsHistory(from, to) std::vector<PositionHistory> Closed positions (UTC window)

from / to are unix seconds, UTC (when the service runs with utcTimes = true, the default).

docs.title: 📦 DTOs
docs.text:
struct Position {                  // openedOrders().positions, positions()
    int64_t ticket; std::string symbol; int type;   // 0 BUY, 1 SELL
    double volume, priceOpen, priceCurrent, stopLoss, takeProfit;
    double profit, swap, commission; int64_t magic; std::string comment;
    int64_t openTime, identifier; int reason;
    bool isBuy() const;            // type == 0
};

struct PendingOrder {              // openedOrders().orders
    int64_t ticket; std::string symbol; int type, state;
    double volumeInitial, volumeCurrent, priceOpen, priceCurrent;
    double stopLoss, takeProfit, stopLimit; int64_t magic; std::string comment;
    int64_t timeSetup, timeExpiration, positionId;
};

struct OpenedOrders { std::vector<Position> positions; std::vector<PendingOrder> orders; };
struct OpenedTickets { std::vector<int64_t> positionTickets, orderTickets; };

struct HistoryItem {               // orderHistory()
    HistoryOrder order; bool hasOrder; Deal deal; bool hasDeal;
};

struct PositionHistory {           // positionsHistory()
    int64_t ticket; std::string symbol; int orderType;
    double volume, openPrice, closePrice, stopLoss, takeProfit;
    double profit, swap, commission, fee;
    int64_t openTime, closeTime, magic; std::string comment;
};

(HistoryOrder and Deal are declared in mt5_service.hpp.)

docs.title: Count, then list
docs.text:
if (service.positionsTotal() > 0) {
    double total = 0;
    for (const Position& p : service.openedOrders().positions) {
        std::printf("#%lld %s %s %.2f  P/L %.2f\n",
                    (long long)p.ticket, p.symbol.c_str(),
                    p.isBuy() ? "BUY" : "SELL", p.volume, p.profit);
        total += p.profit;
    }
    std::printf("Total floating P/L: %.2f\n", total);
}

docs.title: Positions for one EA (magic filter)
docs.text:
for (const Position& p : service.positions(/*magic*/777))
    std::printf("#%lld %s %.2f\n", (long long)p.ticket, p.symbol.c_str(), p.volume);

docs.title: Lightweight ticket diff
docs.text:
OpenedTickets t = service.openedOrdersTickets();
std::printf("%zu open positions, %zu pending orders\n",
            t.positionTickets.size(), t.orderTickets.size());

docs.title: Last 30 days of closed positions
docs.text:
#include <ctime>
int64_t now = (int64_t)std::time(nullptr);
auto hist = service.positionsHistory(now - 30*24*3600, now);

double net = 0; int wins = 0;
for (const PositionHistory& h : hist) { net += h.profit; if (h.profit > 0) ++wins; }
std::printf("Net %.2f over %zu trades (%d wins)\n", net, hist.size(), wins);

docs.title: Order/deal history
docs.text:
auto items = service.orderHistory(now - 7*24*3600, now);
for (const HistoryItem& it : items) {
    if (it.hasDeal)  std::printf("deal  #%lld %s P/L %.2f\n",
                                 (long long)it.deal.ticket, it.deal.symbol.c_str(), it.deal.profit);
    if (it.hasOrder) std::printf("order #%lld %s\n",
                                 (long long)it.order.ticket, it.order.symbol.c_str());
}

docs.title: 🔧 When to use which
docs.text:
1. "Anything open?" → positionsTotal().
  2. Full live picture → openedOrders().
  3. Only tickets (cheap polling) → openedOrdersTickets().
  4. Per-position P&L report → positionsHistory().
  5. Order/deal audit → orderHistory().

docs.title: MT5Service — Trading Methods (Mid-Level)
docs.text:
6 methods to place, modify, close, validate and calculate trades — with plain arguments and friendly results. Wrappers over MT5Account Trading Operations.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL. Implementation: src/mt5_service.cpp.

docs.title: 📋 The methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Description orderSend(OrderRequest) OrderResult Place a market or pending order orderModify(ticket, sl, tp, price=0, stopLimit=0) OrderResult Modify SL/TP (and pending price) orderClose(ticket, volume=0, slippage=10) OrderResult Close/partial-close or delete pending orderCheck(OrderRequest) OrderCheckResult Dry-run validation before sending orderCalcMargin(symbol, orderType, volume, price) double Margin required orderCalcProfit(symbol, orderType, volume, open, close) double Potential profit

orderType is a plain int (pass the protobuf order-type enum value). volume == 0 on orderClose closes the whole position.

docs.title: 📦 DTOs & enum
docs.text:
enum class TradeAction {           // OrderRequest::action
    Buy=0, Sell=1, BuyLimit=2, SellLimit=3,
    BuyStop=4, SellStop=5, BuyStopLimit=6, SellStopLimit=7
};

struct OrderRequest {              // input to orderSend()/orderCheck()
    std::string symbol; TradeAction action; double volume;
    double price;                  // 0 = market (Buy/Sell); required for pendings
    double stopLoss, takeProfit, stopLimit;
    int slippage;                  // points (default 10)
    int64_t magic;                 // sent as expert_id
    std::string comment; int64_t expiration;   // unix seconds; 0 = GTC
};

struct OrderResult {               // orderSend/Modify/Close
    uint32_t retcode;              // 10009 DONE, 10008 PLACED, 10010 DONE_PARTIAL
    int64_t ticket, deal, order; double volume, price, bid, ask;
    std::string comment, retcodeName, retcodeDescription; uint32_t requestId;
    bool ok() const;               // true for accepted retcodes
};

struct OrderCheckResult {          // orderCheck
    uint32_t retcode;              // 0 / 10009 = would succeed
    double balance, equity, profit, margin, freeMargin, marginLevel;
    std::string comment; bool ok() const;
};

docs.title: orderSend(const OrderRequest&) → OrderResult
docs.text: Fill only the fields relevant to the action. Market BUY/SELL may leave price = 0; pendings need price (and stopLimit for *StopLimit).

docs.title: orderModify(ticket, stopLoss, takeProfit, price=0, stopLimit=0) → OrderResult
docs.text: For a position, set stopLoss/takeProfit (leave price 0). For a pending order, you can also move price/stopLimit.

docs.title: orderClose(ticket, volume=0, slippage=10) → OrderResult
docs.text: volume = 0 → close the whole position; a smaller value → partial close. Also deletes a pending order by ticket.

docs.title: orderCheck(const OrderRequest&) → OrderCheckResult
docs.text: Dry-run: reports margin, free margin and a retcode without executing. ok() = would succeed.

docs.title: orderCalcMargin(symbol, orderType, volume, price) → double
docs.text: Margin the trade would require (account currency).

docs.title: orderCalcProfit(symbol, orderType, volume, openPrice, closePrice) → double
docs.text: Profit a move would yield (account currency).

docs.title: Market BUY with SL/TP
docs.text:
OrderRequest req;
req.symbol = "EURUSD";
req.action = TradeAction::Buy;
req.volume = 0.01;
req.price  = service.symbolInfoTick("EURUSD").ask;
req.stopLoss   = req.price - 0.0050;
req.takeProfit = req.price + 0.0050;
req.magic = 777; req.comment = "demo-buy";

OrderResult r = service.orderSend(req);
if (r.ok()) std::printf("DONE: order #%lld @ %.5f\n", (long long)r.order, r.price);
else        std::printf("rejected: %u %s\n", r.retcode, r.retcodeDescription.c_str());

docs.title: Validate first
docs.text:
OrderCheckResult chk = service.orderCheck(req);
if (!chk.ok()) { std::printf("invalid: %s\n", chk.comment.c_str()); return; }
std::printf("margin %.2f, free after %.2f\n", chk.margin, chk.freeMargin);

docs.title: Pending BUY LIMIT
docs.text:
OrderRequest p;
p.symbol = "EURUSD"; p.action = TradeAction::BuyLimit;
p.volume = 0.01; p.price = 1.0800; p.takeProfit = 1.0900;
std::printf("retcode %u\n", service.orderSend(p).retcode);

docs.title: Move stop to break-even
docs.text:
for (const Position& pos : service.openedOrders().positions) {
    if (pos.symbol != "EURUSD") continue;
    OrderResult r = service.orderModify(pos.ticket, pos.priceOpen, pos.takeProfit);
    std::printf("modify retcode %u\n", r.retcode);
    break;
}

docs.title: Close / scale out
docs.text:
service.orderClose(ticket);                 // whole position
service.orderClose(ticket, pos.volume/2);   // half

docs.title: Pre-trade math
docs.text:
namespace pb = mt5_term_api;
double margin = service.orderCalcMargin("EURUSD", pb::ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY, 1.0, 1.0850);
double profit = service.orderCalcProfit("EURUSD", pb::ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY, 1.0, 1.0850, 1.0900);
std::printf("margin %.2f, profit at +50pips %.2f\n", margin, profit);

docs.title: 🔧 Rules
docs.text:
1. Check the result. OrderResult::ok() (or retcode == 10009); OrderCheckResult::ok().
  2. Normalize volume to SymbolInfo::volumeStep and respect stopsLevel for SL/TP.
  3. Validate risky sends with orderCheck() first.
  4. Trade timeout via service.options().tradeTimeoutMs.

docs.title: MT5Service — Market Depth Methods (Mid-Level)
docs.text:
3 methods for the Depth-of-Market / order book, returning a std::vector<BookEntry> instead of protobuf. Wrappers over MT5Account Market Depth (DOM).

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL. Implementation: src/mt5_service.cpp.

docs.title: 📋 The methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Description marketBookAdd(symbol) bool Subscribe to a symbol's DOM marketBookGet(symbol) std::vector<BookEntry> Current DOM snapshot marketBookRelease(symbol) bool Unsubscribe

DOM is a subscription: marketBookAdd → poll marketBookGet → marketBookRelease. Skipping the add returns an empty book; skipping the release leaks the subscription.

docs.title: 📦 DTO
docs.text:
struct BookEntry {                 // one DOM level
    int type;                      // 0 SELL, 1 BUY, 2 SELL_MARKET, 3 BUY_MARKET
    double price;
    int64_t volume;
    double volumeReal;
};

docs.title: Full lifecycle
docs.text:
if (service.marketBookAdd("EURUSD")) {
    for (const BookEntry& lvl : service.marketBookGet("EURUSD")) {
        const char* side = (lvl.type == 1 || lvl.type == 3) ? "BID" : "ASK";
        std::printf("%s  %.5f  x%lld\n", side, lvl.price, (long long)lvl.volume);
    }
    service.marketBookRelease("EURUSD");
}

docs.title: Best bid / best ask from the book
docs.text:
double bestBid = 0, bestAsk = 1e18;
for (const BookEntry& l : service.marketBookGet("EURUSD")) {
    if (l.type == 1 /*BUY*/)  bestBid = std::max(bestBid, l.price);
    if (l.type == 0 /*SELL*/) bestAsk = std::min(bestAsk, l.price);
}
std::printf("top of book: %.5f / %.5f\n", bestBid, bestAsk);

docs.title: RAII cleanup
docs.text:
struct Dom {
    MT5Service& s; std::string sym; bool ok;
    Dom(MT5Service& svc, std::string symbol) : s(svc), sym(std::move(symbol)),
        ok(s.marketBookAdd(sym)) {}
    ~Dom() { if (ok) s.marketBookRelease(sym); }
};
// { Dom d(service, "EURUSD"); auto book = service.marketBookGet("EURUSD"); }  // auto-released

docs.title: 🔧 Notes
docs.text:
• Not all symbols/brokers provide DOM — marketBookAdd returns false when unavailable.
  • Poll, don't spin — marketBookGet is a snapshot.
  • Always release — prefer an RAII guard.

docs.title: MT5Service — Streaming Methods (Mid-Level)
docs.text:
5 real-time streams that deliver friendly event structs (times in UTC) to your callback on a background thread. Wrappers over MT5Account Streaming.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL. Implementation: src/mt5_service.cpp.

docs.title: 📋 The methods
docs.text:
Method Callback payload Description subscribeTicks(symbols, cb) Tick Live ticks for the given symbols streamTradeUpdates(cb) TradeEvent Orders/positions/deals appearing, changing, closing streamTransactions(cb) TransactionEvent Detailed transaction log (request/transaction/result) streamPositionProfits(cb) PositionProfitEvent Periodic position-profit snapshots streamOpenedTickets(cb) TicketsSnapshot Periodic position + pending-order ticket snapshots

Each returns a std::unique_ptr<ServiceStream>.

docs.title: 🧵 The streaming model (read first)
docs.text:
auto stream = service.subscribeTicks({"EURUSD"}, [](const Tick& t) { /* ... */ });
// ... stream is live on a background thread ...
stream->stop();   // cancel and join the reader thread
  • The SDK reads the server stream on a dedicated background thread and calls your callback per payload — already converted to a friendly struct with UTC times.
  • Keep the handle alive. Destroying the unique_ptr (or calling stop()) cancels the stream.
  • The callback runs on the reader thread — don't block it; guard shared state (std::atomic / mutex).
  • ServiceStream API: stop(), running(), count() (payloads delivered), lastError().

See the gRPC Streaming and Concurrency Model guides.

docs.title: 📦 Event DTOs (selected)
docs.text:
struct Tick { std::string symbol; int64_t time, timeMsc;   // UTC
              double bid, ask, last, volume; uint32_t flags; };

struct EventAccountInfo { int64_t login; double balance, credit, equity,
                          margin, freeMargin, marginLevel, profit; };

struct PositionProfitInfo { uint32_t index; int64_t ticket; std::string symbol; double profit; };
struct PositionProfitEvent {
    int type; std::string terminalGuid; EventAccountInfo account;
    std::vector<PositionProfitInfo> newPositions, updatedPositions, deletedPositions;
};

struct TicketsSnapshot {
    std::string terminalGuid;
    std::vector<int64_t> positionTickets, pendingOrderTickets;
    int64_t serverTime;            // UTC seconds
};

TradeEvent and TransactionEvent carry richer sub-structs (TradeOrderInfo, TradePositionInfo, TradeHistory*Info, TradeTransaction, TradeRequestInfo, TradeResultInfo) — all declared in mt5_service.hpp.

docs.title: Live ticks
docs.text:
#include <thread>
#include <chrono>

auto stream = service.subscribeTicks({"EURUSD","GBPUSD"}, [](const Tick& t) {
    std::printf("%s %.5f/%.5f\n", t.symbol.c_str(), t.bid, t.ask);
});
std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(10));
stream->stop();

docs.title: Live P&L
docs.text:
auto s = service.streamPositionProfits([](const PositionProfitEvent& e) {
    for (const PositionProfitInfo& p : e.updatedPositions)
        std::printf("#%lld %s profit %.2f\n",
                    (long long)p.ticket, p.symbol.c_str(), p.profit);
    std::printf("account equity %.2f\n", e.account.equity);
});

docs.title: React to trade events
docs.text:
auto s = service.streamTradeUpdates([](const TradeEvent& e) {
    if (!e.newPositions.empty())
        std::printf("opened %zu position(s)\n", e.newPositions.size());
    if (!e.disappearedPositions.empty())
        std::printf("closed %zu position(s)\n", e.disappearedPositions.size());
});

docs.title: Ticket-diff feed (lightweight)
docs.text:
auto s = service.streamOpenedTickets([](const TicketsSnapshot& snap) {
    std::printf("%zu positions, %zu pending (UTC %lld)\n",
                snap.positionTickets.size(), snap.pendingOrderTickets.size(),
                (long long)snap.serverTime);
});

docs.title: 🔧 Rules
docs.text:
1. Store the handle for as long as you want events.
  2. Keep callbacks fast; offload slow work and guard shared state.
  3. One stream, many symbols for ticks.
  4. Stop on shutdown — stream->stop() (or let the unique_ptr go out of scope).

docs.title: MT5Service — Mid-Level API Overview
docs.text:
A comfortable, protobuf-free facade over MT5Account: friendly C++ structs instead of protobuf messages, plain arguments instead of hand-built *Request objects, and automatic UTC ↔ broker-server time conversion.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — the balance between low-level (MT5Account) and high-level (MT5Sugar). Recommended for most application code.

docs.title: ⚠️ What changes vs MT5Account
docs.text:
MT5Service and MT5Account have the same underlying gRPC calls — the difference is the types and the ceremony:

// Low-level (MT5Account): build a request, unpack the Data wrapper
namespace pb = mt5_term_api;
pb::AccountInfoDoubleRequest r;
r.set_property_id(pb::ACCOUNT_BALANCE);
double balance = account.accountInfoDouble(r).requested_value();   // ← unpack

// Mid-level (MT5Service): one call, plain value
double balance = service.accountInfoDouble(pb::ACCOUNT_BALANCE);   // ← done

// Low-level: protobuf tick, manual time handling
pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest tr; tr.set_symbol("EURUSD");
pb::MrpcMqlTick t = account.symbolInfoTick(tr);
// t.time() is raw broker server time

// Mid-level: friendly struct, time already UTC
Tick tick = service.symbolInfoTick("EURUSD");
std::printf("%.5f / %.5f\n", tick.bid, tick.ask);   // tick.time is UTC seconds

The header is protobuf-free. #include <metarpc/mt5_service.hpp> does not pull the ~11 MB generated protobuf headers (it forward-declares MT5Account), so strategy code compiles fast and only sees the friendly types. Reach the raw layer with service.account() when you need an RPC not surfaced here.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture
docs.text:
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  HIGH-LEVEL: MT5Sugar        ← one-liners      │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                    ↓ owns
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  MID-LEVEL: MT5Service  ← YOU ARE HERE         │
│  friendly C++ structs, UTC times               │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                    ↓ owns
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  LOW-LEVEL: MT5Account   ← protobuf / gRPC     │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Each layer owns the one below: MT5Service owns an MT5Account. Construct the service directly — it creates the account for you.

docs.title: 📦 Creating & connecting
docs.text:
#include <metarpc/mt5_service.hpp>
using namespace metarpc;

// host, port, apiKey, name, utcTimes(=true by default)
MT5Service service("mt5.mrpc.pro", 443);

service.connect(5057947437, "password", "MetaQuotes-Demo");   // blocks until ready
// ... use friendly methods ...
service.disconnect();   // stops the terminal on the server; or close() to just drop the channel
  • No ctx parameter. Deadlines come from service.options() (a ClientOptions&): unaryTimeoutMs, tradeTimeoutMs, maxRetries, …
  • Errors are exceptions: ApiError (server rejected) / TransportError (transport failed past retries).
  • utcTimes = true (default): every time the facade returns is UTC seconds, and every time you pass in is treated as UTC. Set false in the constructor to work in raw broker-server time.
  • Reach low-level: MT5Account& acc = service.account();

docs.title: 1️⃣ Account Methods (4) → full docs

Connection/Time helpers also live on the service: connect/reconnect/isConnected/terminalGuid/disconnect/close/options/account and serverOffsetSeconds/toUtc/toServerTime.

docs.title: 📦 Key DTO structs
docs.text:
struct AccountInfo {               // accountSummary()
    int64_t login; std::string currency;
    double balance, equity, credit; int64_t leverage;
    std::string name, company; TradeMode tradeMode;
    int64_t serverTime, serverTimeUtc, utcShiftMinutes;  // unix seconds
    std::string server;
};

struct Tick {                      // symbolInfoTick(), subscribeTicks()
    std::string symbol; int64_t time, timeMsc;           // UTC seconds / ms
    double bid, ask, last, volume; uint32_t flags;
    bool twoSided() const;
};

struct OrderResult {               // orderSend/Modify/Close
    uint32_t retcode;              // 10009 DONE, 10008 PLACED, …
    int64_t ticket, deal, order; double volume, price, bid, ask;
    std::string comment, retcodeName, retcodeDescription; uint32_t requestId;
    bool ok() const;               // true for accepted retcodes
};

struct OrderCheckResult {          // orderCheck
    uint32_t retcode;              // 0 / 10009 = would succeed
    double balance, equity, profit, margin, freeMargin, marginLevel;
    std::string comment; bool ok() const;
};

Other DTOs: SymbolInfo, Bar, Position, PendingOrder, OpenedOrders, Deal, HistoryOrder, HistoryItem, PositionHistory, MarginRate, SessionTime, BookEntry, TickValueSize, OpenedTickets, and the streaming event structs (TradeEvent, TransactionEvent, PositionProfitEvent, TicketsSnapshot, …). All are declared in mt5_service.hpp.

docs.title: 1) Balance & equity
docs.text:
AccountInfo s = service.accountSummary();
std::printf("Balance %.2f %s | Equity %.2f | Lev 1:%lld\n",
            s.balance, s.currency.c_str(), s.equity, (long long)s.leverage);

docs.title: 2) Current price
docs.text:
Tick t = service.symbolInfoTick("EURUSD");
std::printf("%.5f / %.5f (spread %.5f)\n", t.bid, t.ask, t.ask - t.bid);

docs.title: 3) Validate, then place
docs.text:
OrderRequest req;
req.symbol = "EURUSD";
req.action = TradeAction::Buy;
req.volume = 0.10;
req.price  = service.symbolInfoTick("EURUSD").ask;

OrderCheckResult chk = service.orderCheck(req);
if (!chk.ok()) { std::printf("invalid: %s\n", chk.comment.c_str()); return; }
std::printf("margin %.2f, free after %.2f\n", chk.margin, chk.freeMargin);

OrderResult res = service.orderSend(req);
if (res.ok()) std::printf("order #%lld @ %.5f\n", (long long)res.order, res.price);
else          std::printf("rejected: %u %s\n", res.retcode, res.retcodeDescription.c_str());

docs.title: 4) Live prices (stream)
docs.text:
auto stream = service.subscribeTicks({"EURUSD","GBPUSD"}, [](const Tick& t) {
    std::printf("%s %.5f/%.5f\n", t.symbol.c_str(), t.bid, t.ask);
});
// ... keep `stream` alive ...
stream->stop();

docs.title: 📊 Low-level vs Mid-level
docs.text: Aspect MT5Account (low) MT5Service (mid) Return type protobuf *Data friendly C++ structs Request creation manual *Request automatic Data unpacking .requested_value(), .total() direct Time raw broker seconds UTC (by default) Header weight pulls protobuf protobuf-free Recommended for specific/raw needs most tasks

docs.title: 🔧 Best practices
docs.text:
1. Prefer the "recommended" aggregate methods. accountSummary() over several accountInfo*; symbolParams() over many symbolInfo*.
  2. Check trade retcodes. OrderResult::ok() / retcode == 10009; OrderCheckResult::ok().
  3. Tune timeouts on service.options() instead of a per-call ctx.
  4. Clean up streams and DOM. Keep stream handles alive; marketBookRelease() what you marketBookAdd().
  5. Catch exceptions (ApiError / TransportError) at a sensible boundary.

docs.title: MT5Sugar · Connection
docs.text:
Connect, check liveness, and drop the channel — the one-liner front door to a session. Wraps MT5Service connection.

🧩 Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar). Header: #include <metarpc/mt5_sugar.hpp>, namespace metarpc.

All methods throw ApiError / TransportError on failure (and quickConnect() throws std::runtime_error if an env var is missing).

docs.title: connect(login, password, server, name="", timeoutSeconds=120)
docs.text:
Connect by credentials and broker server name; blocks until the terminal is ready.

Signature: void connect(int64_t login, const std::string& password, const std::string& server, const std::string& name = "", int timeoutSeconds = 120);

Examples

1 — minimal connect 

MT5Sugar sugar("mt5.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(5057947437, "password", "MetaQuotes-Demo");

2 — custom terminal name + longer startup budget 

sugar.connect(5057947437, "password", "MetaQuotes-Demo", "my-bot", /*timeoutSeconds*/180);

3 — connect then sanity-check 

sugar.connect(5057947437, "password", "MetaQuotes-Demo");
if (!sugar.ping()) { std::puts("connected but not responding"); return; }

docs.title: quickConnect()
docs.text:
Connect using the environment variables MT5_LOGIN, MT5_PASSWORD, MT5_SERVER.

Signature: void quickConnect();

Examples

1 — the shortest start 

MT5Sugar sugar;                 // defaults to mt5.mrpc.pro:443
sugar.quickConnect();           // reads MT5_LOGIN / MT5_PASSWORD / MT5_SERVER

2 — handle a missing variable 

try {
    sugar.quickConnect();
} catch (const std::runtime_error& e) {
    std::printf("env not set: %s\n", e.what());
}

docs.title: isConnected()
docs.text:
Whether a successful connect has happened on this client.

Signature: bool isConnected() const;

Examples

1 — branch on state 

if (!sugar.isConnected()) sugar.quickConnect();

docs.title: ping()
docs.text:
Liveness probe: fetches the account summary and returns true if it succeeds.

Signature: bool ping();

Examples

1 — health check 

std::printf("alive: %s\n", sugar.ping() ? "yes" : "no");

2 — reconnect loop 

if (!sugar.ping()) {
    std::puts("stale — reconnecting");
    sugar.connect(5057947437, "password", "MetaQuotes-Demo");
}

docs.title: disconnect()
docs.text:
Drop the gRPC channel. The terminal keeps running on the server (use the service/account layer's disconnect() to actually stop it).

Signature: void disconnect();

Examples

1 — clean shutdown 

sugar.disconnect();

docs.title: service() / account()
docs.text:
Reach the lower layers for anything not wrapped here.

Signatures: MT5Service& service(); · MT5Account& account();

Examples

1 — drop to the mid-level facade 

AccountInfo info = sugar.service().accountSummary();

2 — drop to the raw layer 

namespace pb = mt5_term_api;
pb::AccountSummaryData raw = sugar.account().accountSummary();

docs.title: MT5Sugar · Risk Management
docs.text:
Size positions by risk, check affordability, and compute SL/TP prices — the helpers that turn an idea into a safely-sized order. Built on MT5Service calculations.

🧩 Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar).

Rounding: calculatePositionSize / getMaxLotSize round the volume down to the symbol's volumeStep; calculateSLTP rounds the SL/TP prices to the symbol's digits.

docs.title: calculatePositionSize(symbol, riskPercent, stopLossPips)
docs.text:
Lot size so that a stopLossPips stop risks riskPercent% of the balance.

Signature: double calculatePositionSize(const std::string& symbol, double riskPercent, double stopLossPips);

Examples

1 — risk 1% on a 20-pip stop 

double lots = sugar.calculatePositionSize("EURUSD", 1.0, 20);
std::printf("sized: %.2f lots\n", lots);

2 — size and enter in one flow 

double lots = sugar.calculatePositionSize("EURUSD", 0.5 /*%*/, 30 /*pips*/);
if (lots > 0) sugar.buyMarketWithPips("EURUSD", lots, 30, 60);

docs.title: getMaxLotSize(symbol)
docs.text:
Largest lot the current free margin can open on this symbol.

Signature: double getMaxLotSize(const std::string& symbol);

Examples

1 — cap an order at the affordable max 

double want = 1.0;
double maxLots = sugar.getMaxLotSize("EURUSD");
double vol = std::min(want, maxLots);
if (vol > 0) sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", vol);

docs.title: canOpenPosition(symbol, volume, reason&)
docs.text:
Whether a volume-lot order can be opened now; reason explains a false.

Signature: bool canOpenPosition(const std::string& symbol, double volume, std::string& reason);

Examples

1 — pre-flight check 

std::string why;
if (sugar.canOpenPosition("EURUSD", 0.50, why))
    sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.50);
else
    std::printf("cannot open: %s\n", why.c_str());

2 — size, then confirm, then trade 

double lots = sugar.calculatePositionSize("EURUSD", 1.0, 20);
std::string why;
if (sugar.canOpenPosition("EURUSD", lots, why))
    sugar.buyMarketWithPips("EURUSD", lots, 20, 40);
else
    std::printf("skip (%s)\n", why.c_str());

docs.title: calculateRequiredMargin(symbol, volume)
docs.text:
Margin needed to open volume lots (buy side), in account currency.

Signature: double calculateRequiredMargin(const std::string& symbol, double volume);

Examples

1 — compare against free margin 

double need = sugar.calculateRequiredMargin("EURUSD", 1.0);
std::printf("need %.2f / free %.2f\n", need, sugar.getFreeMargin());

docs.title: calculateSLTP(symbol, direction, entryPrice, slPips, tpPips, slOut&, tpOut&)
docs.text:
Compute absolute SL/TP prices for a direction ("buy" / "sell") from pip distances.

Signature: void calculateSLTP(const std::string& symbol, const std::string& direction, double entryPrice, double stopLossPips, double takeProfitPips, double& slOut, double& tpOut);

Examples

1 — derive prices, then place a limit 

double sl, tp;
double entry = 1.0800;
sugar.calculateSLTP("EURUSD", "buy", entry, /*slPips*/20, /*tpPips*/40, sl, tp);
sugar.buyLimitWithSLTP("EURUSD", 0.01, entry, sl, tp);

2 — short side 

double sl, tp;
sugar.calculateSLTP("EURUSD", "sell", sugar.getBid("EURUSD"), 25, 50, sl, tp);
std::printf("sell SL %.5f TP %.5f\n", sl, tp);

docs.title: MT5Sugar · Account Information
docs.text:
The whole account snapshot in one call. Wraps MT5Service::accountSummary and returns the friendly AccountInfo struct.

🧩 Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar).

struct AccountInfo {
    int64_t login; std::string currency;
    double balance, equity, credit; int64_t leverage;
    std::string name, company; TradeMode tradeMode;      // Demo / Contest / Real
    int64_t serverTime, serverTimeUtc, utcShiftMinutes;  // unix seconds
    std::string server;
};

For a single figure, the Balance / Margin one-liners (getBalance(), getEquity(), …) are shorter. Use getAccountInfo() when you need several fields at once.

docs.title: getAccountInfo()
docs.text:
Full account snapshot.

Signature: AccountInfo getAccountInfo();

Examples

1 — a status line 

AccountInfo a = sugar.getAccountInfo();
std::printf("Acc %lld | %s | Bal %.2f | Eq %.2f | Lev 1:%lld | %s\n",
            (long long)a.login, a.currency.c_str(), a.balance, a.equity,
            (long long)a.leverage, a.company.c_str());

2 — refuse to run on a real account 

AccountInfo a = sugar.getAccountInfo();
if (a.tradeMode == TradeMode::Real)
    throw std::runtime_error("refusing to run a test strategy on a REAL account");

3 — show server time (UTC) 

#include <ctime>
AccountInfo a = sugar.getAccountInfo();
std::time_t utc = (std::time_t)a.serverTimeUtc;
char buf[32]; std::strftime(buf, sizeof buf, "%F %T", std::gmtime(&utc));
std::printf("server time (UTC): %s\n", buf);

docs.title: MT5Sugar · Balance / Margin
docs.text:
Six one-liners for the account's money figures. Each returns a double and wraps MT5Service account reads.

🧩 Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar). Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.

docs.title: getBalance()
docs.text:
Account balance — settled money, excludes floating P/L.

Signature: double getBalance();

Examples

1 — read it 

std::printf("Balance: %.2f\n", sugar.getBalance());

2 — guard before trading 

if (sugar.getBalance() < 100) { std::puts("balance too low"); return; }

docs.title: getEquity()
docs.text:
Equity = balance + floating P/L of open positions.

Signature: double getEquity();

Examples

1 — read it 

std::printf("Equity: %.2f\n", sugar.getEquity());

2 — drawdown vs balance 

double dd = sugar.getBalance() - sugar.getEquity();
if (dd > 0) std::printf("floating loss: %.2f\n", dd);

docs.title: getMargin() / getFreeMargin()
docs.text:
Used margin and free margin (account currency).

Signatures: double getMargin(); · double getFreeMargin();

Examples

1 — how much room is left 

std::printf("Used %.2f | Free %.2f\n", sugar.getMargin(), sugar.getFreeMargin());

2 — can I afford more? 

if (sugar.getFreeMargin() < 50) std::puts("not enough free margin");

docs.title: getMarginLevel()
docs.text:
Margin level in percent (equity / margin × 100); 0 when nothing is open.

Signature: double getMarginLevel();

Examples

1 — risk gauge 

double lvl = sugar.getMarginLevel();
if (lvl != 0 && lvl < 150) std::puts("⚠️ margin level low");

2 — auto-protect 

if (sugar.getMarginLevel() != 0 && sugar.getMarginLevel() < 120)
    sugar.closeAllPositions();

docs.title: getProfit()
docs.text:
Current total floating profit of all open positions.

Signature: double getProfit();

Examples

1 — read it 

std::printf("Floating P/L: %.2f\n", sugar.getProfit());

2 — take profit on the whole book 

if (sugar.getProfit() > 50) {
    std::puts("target hit — closing all");
    sugar.closeAllPositions();
}

docs.title: MT5Sugar · Prices / Quotes
docs.text:
Current prices in one line, plus a compact snapshot and a price-wait helper. Wraps MT5Service symbol reads.

🧩 Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar). Throws ApiError / TransportError on failure.

struct PriceInfo { std::string symbol; double bid, ask, spread; int64_t time; };  // time = UTC seconds

docs.title: getBid(symbol) / getAsk(symbol)
docs.text:
Current best bid / ask.

Signatures: double getBid(const std::string& symbol); · double getAsk(const std::string& symbol);

Examples

1 — read both 

std::printf("EURUSD %.5f / %.5f\n", sugar.getBid("EURUSD"), sugar.getAsk("EURUSD"));

2 — mid price 

double mid = (sugar.getBid("EURUSD") + sugar.getAsk("EURUSD")) / 2.0;

docs.title: getSpread(symbol)
docs.text:
ask - bid in price units.

Signature: double getSpread(const std::string& symbol);

Examples

1 — only trade on a tight spread 

if (sugar.getSpread("EURUSD") <= 0.00015)
    sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.01);

docs.title: getPriceInfo(symbol)
docs.text:
bid / ask / spread / time in a single call.

Signature: PriceInfo getPriceInfo(const std::string& symbol);

Examples

1 — one call for everything 

PriceInfo p = sugar.getPriceInfo("EURUSD");
std::printf("%.5f / %.5f (spread %.5f)\n", p.bid, p.ask, p.spread);

2 — timestamped log line 

PriceInfo p = sugar.getPriceInfo("XAUUSD");
std::printf("[UTC %lld] XAUUSD %.2f\n", (long long)p.time, p.bid);

docs.title: waitForPrice(symbol, targetBid, timeoutMs=10000)
docs.text:
Poll until the bid reaches targetBid (or any tick when targetBid == 0), up to timeoutMs. Returns the last price seen; the result's symbol is empty on timeout.

Signature: PriceInfo waitForPrice(const std::string& symbol, double targetBid, int timeoutMs = 10000);

Examples

1 — wait for a breakout level 

PriceInfo hit = sugar.waitForPrice("EURUSD", 1.0900, 30000);
if (!hit.symbol.empty()) {
    std::printf("level reached at %.5f\n", hit.bid);
    sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.01);
} else {
    std::puts("timed out waiting for level");
}

2 — wait for the next tick 

PriceInfo t = sugar.waitForPrice("EURUSD", 0 /*any tick*/, 5000);

docs.title: MT5Sugar · Simple Trading
docs.text:
Market and pending orders in one line each. Every method returns the resulting ticket (uint64_t), or 0 on a rejected order. Wraps MT5Service::orderSend.

🧩 Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar). Throws ApiError / TransportError on transport/validation failure; a rejected trade returns 0.

No rounding. Volumes/prices are sent exactly as given — normalize against the symbol's volumeStep / digits yourself, or use the Risk Management helpers.

docs.title: buyMarket(symbol, volume) / sellMarket(symbol, volume)
docs.text:
Market BUY / SELL at the current price, no SL/TP.

Signatures: uint64_t buyMarket(const std::string& symbol, double volume); · uint64_t sellMarket(const std::string& symbol, double volume);

Examples

1 — go long 

uint64_t t = sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.01);
if (t) std::printf("opened #%llu\n", (unsigned long long)t);
else   std::puts("order rejected");

2 — go short and remember the ticket 

uint64_t ticket = sugar.sellMarket("GBPUSD", 0.02);
// ... later ...
if (ticket) sugar.closePosition((int64_t)ticket);

3 — flip a position 

uint64_t shortT = sugar.sellMarket("EURUSD", 0.01);
if (shortT) { sugar.closePosition((int64_t)shortT); sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.01); }

docs.title: buyLimit(symbol, volume, price) / sellLimit(symbol, volume, price)
docs.text:
Pending BUY LIMIT (below market) / SELL LIMIT (above market).

Signatures: uint64_t buyLimit(const std::string& symbol, double volume, double price); · uint64_t sellLimit(const std::string& symbol, double volume, double price);

Examples

1 — buy the dip 

double entry = sugar.getBid("EURUSD") - 0.0020;
uint64_t t = sugar.buyLimit("EURUSD", 0.01, entry);

2 — sell into strength 

uint64_t t = sugar.sellLimit("EURUSD", 0.01, sugar.getAsk("EURUSD") + 0.0020);

docs.title: buyStop(symbol, volume, price) / sellStop(symbol, volume, price)
docs.text:
Pending BUY STOP (above market) / SELL STOP (below market) — breakout entries.

Signatures: uint64_t buyStop(const std::string& symbol, double volume, double price); · uint64_t sellStop(const std::string& symbol, double volume, double price);

Examples

1 — breakout long 

double trigger = sugar.getAsk("EURUSD") + 0.0030;
uint64_t t = sugar.buyStop("EURUSD", 0.01, trigger);

2 — breakdown short 

uint64_t t = sugar.sellStop("EURUSD", 0.01, sugar.getBid("EURUSD") - 0.0030);

docs.title: MT5Sugar · Trading with SL/TP
docs.text:
Entries that carry a stop loss and take profit — as absolute prices or as pip distances. Returns the resulting ticket (0 on rejection). Wraps MT5Service::orderSend.

🧩 Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar).

Rounding: the *WithSLTP methods send prices as given; the *WithPips methods round the computed SL/TP to the symbol's digits.

docs.title: buyMarketWithSLTP(symbol, volume, sl, tp) / sellMarketWithSLTP(symbol, volume, sl, tp)
docs.text:
Market order with absolute SL/TP prices.

Signatures: uint64_t buyMarketWithSLTP(const std::string& symbol, double volume, double sl, double tp); · uint64_t sellMarketWithSLTP(const std::string& symbol, double volume, double sl, double tp);

Examples

1 — long with fixed SL/TP prices 

double ask = sugar.getAsk("EURUSD");
uint64_t t = sugar.buyMarketWithSLTP("EURUSD", 0.01, ask - 0.0050, ask + 0.0050);

2 — short, SL above / TP below 

double bid = sugar.getBid("EURUSD");
uint64_t t = sugar.sellMarketWithSLTP("EURUSD", 0.01, bid + 0.0050, bid - 0.0050);

docs.title: buyLimitWithSLTP(symbol, volume, price, sl, tp) / sellLimitWithSLTP(symbol, volume, price, sl, tp)
docs.text:
Pending limit order at price with absolute SL/TP.

Signatures: uint64_t buyLimitWithSLTP(const std::string& symbol, double volume, double price, double sl, double tp); · uint64_t sellLimitWithSLTP(const std::string& symbol, double volume, double price, double sl, double tp);

Examples

1 — buy-limit with protection 

uint64_t t = sugar.buyLimitWithSLTP("EURUSD", 0.01, /*price*/1.0800, /*sl*/1.0770, /*tp*/1.0860);

2 — sell-limit with protection 

uint64_t t = sugar.sellLimitWithSLTP("EURUSD", 0.01, 1.0900, 1.0930, 1.0840);

docs.title: buyMarketWithPips(symbol, volume, slPips, tpPips) / sellMarketWithPips(symbol, volume, slPips, tpPips)
docs.text:
Market order with SL/TP expressed as pip distances from entry (rounded to digits for you).

Signatures: uint64_t buyMarketWithPips(const std::string& symbol, double volume, double slPips, double tpPips); · uint64_t sellMarketWithPips(const std::string& symbol, double volume, double slPips, double tpPips);

Examples

1 — 20-pip stop, 40-pip target (2:1) 

uint64_t t = sugar.buyMarketWithPips("EURUSD", 0.01, /*slPips*/20, /*tpPips*/40);

2 — short, symmetric 30/30 

uint64_t t = sugar.sellMarketWithPips("EURUSD", 0.01, 30, 30);

3 — size by risk, then enter with pips 

double lots = sugar.calculatePositionSize("EURUSD", 1.0 /*%*/, 20 /*pips*/);
uint64_t t  = sugar.buyMarketWithPips("EURUSD", lots, 20, 40);

docs.title: MT5Sugar · Position Management
docs.text:
Close and modify positions — one, by symbol, or all at once. Wraps MT5Service::orderClose / orderModify.

🧩 Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar). bool methods return true on an accepted retcode; bulk methods return the count affected.

docs.title: closePosition(ticket)
docs.text:
Close a whole position by ticket.

Signature: bool closePosition(int64_t ticket);

Examples

1 — close one 

if (sugar.closePosition(123456)) std::puts("closed");

2 — close what you just opened 

uint64_t t = sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.01);
if (t) sugar.closePosition((int64_t)t);

docs.title: closePositionPartial(ticket, volume)
docs.text:
Close part of a position (the rest stays open).

Signature: bool closePositionPartial(int64_t ticket, double volume);

Examples

1 — scale out half 

bool found = false;
Position p = sugar.getPositionByTicket(123456, found);
if (found) sugar.closePositionPartial(p.ticket, p.volume / 2.0);

docs.title: closeAllPositions()
docs.text:
Close every open position; returns how many were closed.

Signature: int closeAllPositions();

Examples

1 — flatten everything 

int n = sugar.closeAllPositions();
std::printf("closed %d position(s)\n", n);

2 — emergency stop on drawdown 

if (sugar.getProfit() < -100) sugar.closeAllPositions();

docs.title: closeAllBySymbol(symbol)
docs.text:
Close all positions on one symbol; returns the count closed.

Signature: int closeAllBySymbol(const std::string& symbol);

Examples

1 — exit a single market 

int n = sugar.closeAllBySymbol("EURUSD");
std::printf("closed %d EURUSD position(s)\n", n);

docs.title: modifyPositionSL(ticket, sl) / modifyPositionTP(ticket, tp)
docs.text:
Set only the stop loss / only the take profit.

Signatures: bool modifyPositionSL(int64_t ticket, double sl); · bool modifyPositionTP(int64_t ticket, double tp);

Examples

1 — move stop to break-even 

bool found = false;
Position p = sugar.getPositionByTicket(123456, found);
if (found) sugar.modifyPositionSL(p.ticket, p.priceOpen);

2 — tighten the target 

sugar.modifyPositionTP(123456, 1.0880);

docs.title: modifyPositionSLTP(ticket, sl, tp)
docs.text:
Set both SL and TP in one call.

Signature: bool modifyPositionSLTP(int64_t ticket, double sl, double tp);

Examples

1 — set both 

sugar.modifyPositionSLTP(123456, /*sl*/1.0800, /*tp*/1.0900);

2 — trail behind price 

bool found = false;
Position p = sugar.getPositionByTicket(123456, found);
if (found && p.isBuy()) {
    double newSl = sugar.getBid(p.symbol) - 0.0030;     // 30-pip trail
    if (newSl > p.stopLoss) sugar.modifyPositionSLTP(p.ticket, newSl, p.takeProfit);
}

docs.title: MT5Sugar · Position Information
docs.text:
Read open positions and their P&L — all, by symbol, by ticket, or aggregated. Wraps MT5Service positions. Returns the friendly Position struct.

🧩 Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar).

struct Position { int64_t ticket; std::string symbol; int type; /*0 BUY,1 SELL*/
                  double volume, priceOpen, priceCurrent, stopLoss, takeProfit;
                  double profit, swap, commission; int64_t magic; std::string comment;
                  int64_t openTime, identifier; int reason; bool isBuy() const; };

docs.title: getOpenPositions()
docs.text:
All open positions.

Signature: std::vector<Position> getOpenPositions();

Examples

1 — list them 

for (const Position& p : sugar.getOpenPositions())
    std::printf("#%lld %s %s %.2f  P/L %.2f\n",
                (long long)p.ticket, p.symbol.c_str(),
                p.isBuy() ? "BUY" : "SELL", p.volume, p.profit);

2 — close the worst loser 

auto ps = sugar.getOpenPositions();
if (!ps.empty()) {
    const Position* worst = &ps[0];
    for (const auto& p : ps) if (p.profit < worst->profit) worst = &p;
    if (worst->profit < 0) sugar.closePosition(worst->ticket);
}

docs.title: getPositionsBySymbol(symbol)
docs.text:
Open positions on one symbol.

Signature: std::vector<Position> getPositionsBySymbol(const std::string& symbol);

Examples

1 — net volume on a symbol 

double net = 0;
for (const Position& p : sugar.getPositionsBySymbol("EURUSD"))
    net += p.isBuy() ? p.volume : -p.volume;
std::printf("net EURUSD exposure: %.2f lots\n", net);

docs.title: getPositionByTicket(ticket, found&)
docs.text:
One position by ticket; found is set false if there is none.

Signature: Position getPositionByTicket(int64_t ticket, bool& found);

Examples

1 — look one up safely 

bool found = false;
Position p = sugar.getPositionByTicket(123456, found);
if (found) std::printf("profit %.2f\n", p.profit);
else       std::puts("no such position");

docs.title: hasOpenPosition(symbol) / countOpenPositions()
docs.text:
Is there any position on the symbol / how many positions in total.

Signatures: bool hasOpenPosition(const std::string& symbol); · int countOpenPositions();

Examples

1 — don't stack entries 

if (!sugar.hasOpenPosition("EURUSD"))
    sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.01);

2 — cap concurrent positions 

if (sugar.countOpenPositions() < 5)
    sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.01);

docs.title: getTotalProfit() / getProfitBySymbol(symbol)
docs.text:
Summed floating profit across all positions / on one symbol.

Signatures: double getTotalProfit(); · double getProfitBySymbol(const std::string& symbol);

Examples

1 — book-wide target 

if (sugar.getTotalProfit() > 50) sugar.closeAllPositions();

2 — per-symbol target 

if (sugar.getProfitBySymbol("EURUSD") > 20) sugar.closeAllBySymbol("EURUSD");

docs.title: MT5Sugar · History / Statistics
docs.text:
Closed-trade history over convenient windows (today, yesterday, this week/month, custom), realized-profit totals, and a one-call daily summary. Day boundaries are UTC. Wraps MT5Service::positionsHistory.

🧩 Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar). History methods return std::vector<PositionHistory>.

struct DailyStats { int totalDeals, winningDeals, losingDeals;
                    double winRate, totalProfit, bestDeal, worstDeal; };

docs.title: getDealsToday() / getDealsYesterday() / getDealsThisWeek() / getDealsThisMonth()
docs.text:
Closed positions over the named window.

Signatures: std::vector<PositionHistory> getDealsToday(); (and ...Yesterday() / ...ThisWeek() / ...ThisMonth())

Examples

1 — count today's trades 

auto today = sugar.getDealsToday();
std::printf("%zu closed trades today\n", today.size());

2 — list this week with P/L 

for (const PositionHistory& h : sugar.getDealsThisWeek())
    std::printf("#%lld %s  P/L %.2f\n", (long long)h.ticket, h.symbol.c_str(), h.profit);

docs.title: getDealsDateRange(fromUnix, toUnix)
docs.text:
Closed positions in a custom UTC window.

Signature: std::vector<PositionHistory> getDealsDateRange(int64_t fromUnix, int64_t toUnix);

Examples

1 — last 90 days 

#include <ctime>
int64_t now = (int64_t)std::time(nullptr);
auto quarter = sugar.getDealsDateRange(now - 90LL*24*3600, now);
std::printf("%zu trades in the last 90 days\n", quarter.size());

docs.title: getProfitToday() / getProfitThisWeek() / getProfitThisMonth()
docs.text:
Net realized profit over the window.

Signatures: double getProfitToday(); · double getProfitThisWeek(); · double getProfitThisMonth();

Examples

1 — daily P&L line 

std::printf("Today %.2f | Week %.2f | Month %.2f\n",
            sugar.getProfitToday(), sugar.getProfitThisWeek(), sugar.getProfitThisMonth());

2 — stop trading after a daily loss limit 

if (sugar.getProfitToday() < -200) { std::puts("daily loss limit hit"); sugar.closeAllPositions(); }

docs.title: getDailyStats()
docs.text:
Today's win/loss summary in one struct.

Signature: DailyStats getDailyStats();

Examples

1 — print the scorecard 

DailyStats d = sugar.getDailyStats();
std::printf("Deals %d | Wins %d | Losses %d | Win rate %.0f%% | Net %.2f\n",
            d.totalDeals, d.winningDeals, d.losingDeals, d.winRate, d.totalProfit);
std::printf("Best %.2f | Worst %.2f\n", d.bestDeal, d.worstDeal);

2 — gate new entries on today's win rate 

DailyStats d = sugar.getDailyStats();
if (d.totalDeals >= 5 && d.winRate < 30) std::puts("rough day — pausing entries");

docs.title: MT5Sugar · Symbol Information
docs.text:
Quick symbol look-ups a strategy needs before trading — full spec, availability, digits, and the minimum stop distance. Wraps MT5Service symbol reads.

🧩 Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar).

docs.title: getSymbolInfo(symbol)
docs.text:
Full parameters for a symbol (returns the friendly SymbolInfo struct).

Signature: SymbolInfo getSymbolInfo(const std::string& symbol);

Examples

1 — read the essentials 

SymbolInfo s = sugar.getSymbolInfo("EURUSD");
std::printf("%s: digits=%d point=%.5f volMin=%.2f step=%.2f\n",
            s.name.c_str(), s.digits, s.point, s.volumeMin, s.volumeStep);

2 — normalize a desired volume to the step 

SymbolInfo s = sugar.getSymbolInfo("EURUSD");
double want = 0.037;
double norm = std::round(want / s.volumeStep) * s.volumeStep;
norm = std::max(s.volumeMin, std::min(s.volumeMax, norm));

docs.text:
Every symbol name on the terminal.

Signature: std::vector<std::string> getAllSymbols();

Examples

auto all = sugar.getAllSymbols();

for (const auto& s : sugar.getAllSymbols())
    if (s.rfind("EUR", 0) == 0) std::printf("%s\n", s.c_str());

docs.title: MT5Sugar — Complete API Reference
docs.text:
High-level convenience methods for MetaTrader 5 trading automation in C++.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL. MT5Sugar owns an MT5Service (and the underlying MT5Account) and offers the shortest possible one-liners for everyday tasks — "what's my balance?", "what's the bid?", "buy 0.1 lots", "close everything". No context, no request objects, no protobuf.

MT5Sugar covers:

  • 🔌 Simplified connection management
  • 💰 Balance / margin read-outs
  • 📈 Prices & quotes
  • 💹 Simple trading + trading with SL/TP (prices or pip distances)
  • 💼 Position management (close/modify one, by symbol, or all)
  • 📋 Position information & live P&L
  • 📊 History & daily statistics
  • 🧮 Risk-based position sizing and pre-trade checks

Rounding note: the raw order methods (buyMarket, buyLimitWithSLTP, modifyPositionSLTP, …) send volumes/prices exactly as given. The helpers round: calculateSLTP and buy/sellMarketWithPips round SL/TP to the symbol's digits; calculatePositionSize / getMaxLotSize round volume down to volumeStep.

docs.title: 📦 Construct & connect
docs.text:
#include <metarpc/mt5_sugar.hpp>
using namespace metarpc;

MT5Sugar sugar("mt5.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(5057947437, "password", "MetaQuotes-Demo");   // or sugar.quickConnect() from env

double bal = sugar.getBalance();
uint64_t ticket = sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.01);
sugar.closePosition((int64_t)ticket);
sugar.disconnect();
  • Header is protobuf-free — compiles fast.
  • Errors are exceptions: ApiError / TransportError.
  • Drop down when you outgrow it: sugar.service() (friendly facade) or sugar.account() (raw RPCs).
  • Order methods return the resulting ticket (uint64_t), 0 on a rejected order; management methods return bool / counts.

docs.title: 💡 End-to-end example
docs.text:
#include <metarpc/mt5_sugar.hpp>
using namespace metarpc;

int main() {
    MT5Sugar sugar("mt5.mrpc.pro", 443);
    sugar.connect(5057947437, "password", "MetaQuotes-Demo");

    if (!sugar.isSymbolAvailable("EURUSD")) { std::puts("symbol n/a"); return 1; }

    // Size by risk, validate, trade
    double lots = sugar.calculatePositionSize("EURUSD", 1.0 /*%*/, 20 /*pips*/);
    std::string reason;
    if (sugar.canOpenPosition("EURUSD", lots, reason)) {
        uint64_t t = sugar.buyMarketWithPips("EURUSD", lots, 20, 40);
        std::printf("opened #%llu (%.2f lots)\n", (unsigned long long)t, lots);
    } else {
        std::printf("skip: %s\n", reason.c_str());
    }

    std::printf("Equity %.2f | Open P/L %.2f\n", sugar.getEquity(), sugar.getTotalProfit());
    sugar.disconnect();
}

docs.title: 🔧 Best practices
docs.text:
1. Check tickets. Order methods return 0 on rejection — test before assuming a fill.
  2. Size with risk helpers. Prefer calculatePositionSize + canOpenPosition over hard-coded lots.
  3. Clean up. disconnect() when done (also after a failed connect).
  4. Drop down when needed. sugar.service() / sugar.account() for anything not wrapped here.

docs.title: Strategies — Master Overview
docs.text:
Orchestrators are small strategy managers built on top of MT5Sugar: they wrap a decision loop (read state → act → repeat) around the one-liner API. A preset coordinates orchestrators behind a single decision. All of them live in examples/demos/ and run from the demos launcher.

Educational examples, not production systems

These orchestrators use deliberately simple heuristics (a trailing offset, a fixed grid, a few account thresholds). They demonstrate the pattern — a strategy built from the SDK — and are templates to build on, not turnkey trading systems. They place small live orders on the demo account and clean up after themselves.

docs.title: The pattern
docs.text:
Each orchestrator is a class that:

  1. takes a connected MT5Sugar& and a small Config in its constructor,
  2. exposes a run() (or execute()) that loops for a bounded number of cycles,
  3. acts through Sugar / Service calls and prints what it does.
class RiskManager {
public:
    struct Config { double maxDrawdownPct{5}; double minMarginLevel{150}; int cycles{5}; };
    RiskManager(metarpc::MT5Sugar& sugar, Config cfg);
    void run();   // read metrics → evaluate limits → act
};

docs.title: Orchestrators
docs.text:
Each orchestrator has its own page with the annotated class and several worked examples:

# Orchestrator What it does Key Sugar calls 11 Trailing Stop Opens one position, then raises its stop loss as price advances (never lowers it); closes at the end. buyMarket, getBid, modifyPositionSL, closePosition 13 Grid Trader Lays a symmetric grid of pending orders around price (levels each side, stepPips apart), lists it, then removes it. buyLimit, sellLimit, service().openedOrders, closePosition 14 Risk Manager Monitors account health each cycle; if drawdown or margin level breaches a limit, it closes everything (kill-switch). getEquity, getMarginLevel, getTotalProfit, closeAllPositions

docs.title: Trailing Stop →
docs.text:
Ride winners, cap the downside. Each cycle reads the bid and, if price advanced, tightens the SL to trailPips behind it — never looser.

double wantSL = bid - trailPips * pip;
if (wantSL > bestSL) { bestSL = wantSL; sugar.modifyPositionSL(ticket, bestSL); }

docs.title: Grid Trader →
docs.text:
Fade a range: buy-limits below price, sell-limits above, levels each side.

for (int i = 1; i <= levels; ++i) {
    sugar.buyLimit (sym, vol, bid - i * stepPips * pip);   // below price
    sugar.sellLimit(sym, vol, ask + i * stepPips * pip);   // above price
}
// … later: sugar.closePosition(ticket) deletes each pending order.

docs.title: Risk Manager →
docs.text:
A kill-switch: monitor account health and flatten everything on a breach.

double ddPct = (startBalance - sugar.getEquity()) / startBalance * 100.0;
if (ddPct > maxDrawdownPct || (open > 0 && marginLevel > 0 && marginLevel < minMarginLevel))
    sugar.closeAllPositions();   // kill-switch

docs.title: Preset
docs.text:
# Preset What it does 16 Adaptive Market Mode Analyses recent bars, classifies the market (Trending / Ranging / Volatile) and dispatches to the matching orchestrator. 
// analyse last 20 H1 bars → pick a mode → run the right orchestrator
if      (spike > 2.5) demo_risk_manager(sugar, cfg);     // VOLATILE  → defensive
else if (trend > 2.0) demo_trailing_stop(sugar, cfg);    // TRENDING  → ride it
else                  demo_grid_trader(sugar, cfg);      // RANGING   → fade it

docs.title: Orchestrator · Grid Trader
docs.text:
Lay a symmetric grid of pending orders around the current price — buy-limits below, sell-limits above — then list and remove them. Demonstrates pending-order placement + cleanup on MT5Sugar (+ service()).

Source: examples/demos/orchestrators/13_grid_trader.cpp · Run: ./build/demos 13 · API level: HIGH (Sugar) + service()

Educational example

Places small live pending orders on the demo account and deletes them all before returning — nothing is left open. The fixed grid is a template, not a strategy.

docs.title: 🎯 What it does
docs.text:
1. Reads bid/ask.
  2. For each level i = 1…levels, places a buy-limit i·stepPips below and a sell-limit i·stepPips above.
  3. Lists the live pending orders via service().openedOrders().orders.
  4. Deletes every ticket it placed (closePosition deletes a pending by ticket).

docs.title: 🧩 The pattern
docs.text:
GridTrader{config} → for i in 1..levels: buyLimit(bid - i·step) + sellLimit(ask + i·step)
→ list (service().openedOrders) → remove (closePosition per ticket)

docs.title: ⚙️ Config
docs.text:
struct Config {
    int    levels{2};        // pending orders on each side
    double stepPips{20.0};   // distance between levels
    double volume{0.01};
};

docs.title: 🏗️ The orchestrator (annotated)
docs.text:
class GridTrader {
public:
    struct Config { int levels{2}; double stepPips{20.0}; double volume{0.01}; };

    GridTrader(MT5Sugar& sugar, std::string symbol, Config cfg)
        : m_s(sugar), m_sym(std::move(symbol)), m_cfg(cfg) {
        m_pip = sugar.getSymbolInfo(m_sym).point;
        int d = sugar.getSymbolDigits(m_sym);
        if (d == 3 || d == 5) m_pip *= 10.0;
    }

    void run() {
        double bid = m_s.getBid(m_sym), ask = m_s.getAsk(m_sym);

        std::vector<uint64_t> tickets;
        for (int i = 1; i <= m_cfg.levels; ++i) {
            double below = bid - i * m_cfg.stepPips * m_pip;   // buy-limit under price
            double above = ask + i * m_cfg.stepPips * m_pip;   // sell-limit over price
            uint64_t b = m_s.buyLimit (m_sym, m_cfg.volume, below);
            uint64_t s = m_s.sellLimit(m_sym, m_cfg.volume, above);
            if (b) tickets.push_back(b);
            if (s) tickets.push_back(s);
        }
        if (tickets.empty()) return;              // market closed / too close to price

        auto pendings = m_s.service().openedOrders().orders;   // the friendly PendingOrder list

        for (uint64_t t : tickets) m_s.closePosition((int64_t)t);   // clean up everything we placed
    }
private:
    MT5Sugar& m_s; std::string m_sym; double m_pip{0}; Config m_cfg;
};

Key Sugar/Service calls: getBid / getAsk · buyLimit / sellLimit · service().openedOrders() · closePosition (deletes a pending).

docs.title: 1) Run it with defaults
docs.text:
MT5Sugar sugar("mt5.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(5057947437, "password", "MetaQuotes-Demo");

GridTrader gt(sugar, "EURUSD", GridTrader::Config{});
gt.run();   // 2 levels/side, 20-pip step, places → lists → removes

docs.title: 2) A wider, deeper grid
docs.text:
GridTrader::Config cfg;
cfg.levels   = 5;       // 5 orders each side (10 pending total)
cfg.stepPips = 15;      // tighter spacing
cfg.volume   = 0.02;
GridTrader(sugar, "EURUSD", cfg).run();

docs.title: 3) Place a grid and keep it (manage elsewhere)
docs.text:
Drop the cleanup loop and return the tickets so another component can manage fills:

std::vector<uint64_t> placeGrid(MT5Sugar& sugar, const std::string& sym,
                                int levels, double stepPips, double vol) {
    double pip = sugar.getSymbolInfo(sym).point;
    if (sugar.getSymbolDigits(sym) % 2 == 1) pip *= 10.0;
    double bid = sugar.getBid(sym), ask = sugar.getAsk(sym);

    std::vector<uint64_t> t;
    for (int i = 1; i <= levels; ++i) {
        if (uint64_t b = sugar.buyLimit (sym, vol, bid - i*stepPips*pip)) t.push_back(b);
        if (uint64_t s = sugar.sellLimit(sym, vol, ask + i*stepPips*pip)) t.push_back(s);
    }
    return t;   // caller decides when to cancel
}

docs.title: 4) One-sided grid (buy-the-dip ladder only)
docs.text:
double pip = sugar.getSymbolInfo("EURUSD").point * 10.0;
double bid = sugar.getBid("EURUSD");
for (int i = 1; i <= 4; ++i)
    sugar.buyLimit("EURUSD", 0.01, bid - i * 15 * pip);   // ladder of buy-limits below

docs.title: 5) Cancel only the far orders, keep the near ones
docs.text:
auto placed = placeGrid(sugar, "EURUSD", 5, 15, 0.01);   // from example 3
// ... later, thin the grid: cancel every other ticket ...
for (size_t i = 0; i < placed.size(); ++i)
    if (i % 2 == 0) sugar.closePosition((int64_t)placed[i]);

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• No fill management. The demo never lets the grid fill — it places, lists, removes. A real grid needs rules for filled legs (SL/TP, rebalancing).
  • Too close to price is rejected. Limits inside the spread / min-stop distance won't be accepted — stepPips must clear it.
  • closePosition on a ticket deletes a pending order and closes a position — same call, context decides. Track which tickets are which.
  • Symbol must be selectable/open. An empty tickets means the market was closed or prices too tight.
